I always make a batch of scones or cookies when I’m feeling down. It’s the kind of thing that grounds you. I think part of that is the comfort of routine. Especially after running a small business, you get so used to the rhythm of it. Though I must say, sometimes I miss the chaos of it all. I can imagine. I used to work in a small administrative office, and even though it was more structured, there was always a sense of community. It’s funny how these small interactions can mean so much. Exactly. I think that’s one of the reasons I love living in Peterborough—it has this quiet charm, and you can always find someone to chat with in the shops or on the street.

So, do you know what’s happening with the new flat in town? I heard it's supposed to be like a real student ghetto, but I’m not sure yet. I mean, it’s got all the amenities, but it's £600 a week for a single room. That’s more than my old place in Barrow, honestly. Oh yeah, I heard about that too. But I think it's gonna be packed. I mean, I got a friend who said he saw a sign saying 'Last chance to apply before the block fills up.' Didn’t even get the chance to check it out, but I’m already thinking about moving there. I can’t live in the uni halls anymore. It's like a dungeon, honestly. You can't even get a decent meal without someone shouting at you. I know, I know. I’m still stuck with the uni flat, and it's honestly a nightmare. The dorm I’m in, there’s this one guy who keeps playing loud music at 2 a.m. I mean, he’s not even a student here, he’s just staying over, and it's like a warzone. I’m seriously thinking about moving to the city and finding a room with someone else. It’s not like I can afford a flat, but maybe I can split the cost? I know, I know. It’s really hard. I mean, I’m still saving up for the deposit. I’m already in debt from that stupid car I bought in the summer. Oh, and I’m trying not to mention it to my mum, because I know she'll just guilt-trip me into paying it back. Anyway, what about the housewarming party next weekend? I was planning on asking Anna to come, but I’m still not sure if she'll be there. She said she might be working that day. Oh, she's coming. I saw her on Instagram the other day, she posted a photo of her new outfit. She’s trying to look like she's all grown up, but I can tell she's still getting used to being a student. Anyway, I think we’re all going to the party. I heard there's going to be some cheap beer and pizza. It’s the usual. Yeah, I go every time. It's like our little social club.

So, do you remember when we first moved to Bolton? It was like the whole town was one big family. I used to run around with my mates, and my mum would always be on the lookout for me. Oh, I remember that well. You were always getting into trouble with the local bus driver. I swear, he used to chase you down the street every time you missed your stop. Man, I still remember that! I used to sneak onto the bus just to get a free ride. My mates and I would all pile in at the back and laugh the whole way. You'd get in trouble every time, but it was so much fun. Yeah, and then we had that one time when we got stuck on the bus for an hour because of a breakdown. I still remember the driver trying to fix it in the rain. We all ended up soaked and laughing our heads off. You were so lucky. I had to work late that night, and I was so worried about you. I couldn't find you anywhere. I thought something terrible had happened. That sounds like a story from another time. Back in London, I was always worried about getting late for work. One time, I missed my bus by five minutes, and I had to run all the way to the office. I almost missed my first meeting. Yeah, but in Bolton, everything felt so much closer. We could walk everywhere. I loved the sense of community there. Even though we were poor, we had everything we needed. That's true. Even now, when I go back, I feel that same sense of belonging. I still meet people there, and we talk like we always have. I wish I had that kind of connection here in Istria. Sometimes it feels like everyone is from somewhere else. I miss the way people used to know each other from the local supermarket or the park. I know what you mean. Even in London, there was a kind of community, even if it was more about the coffee shops and pubs. I still miss the conversations we used to have over a cup of coffee with friends. I think it's about the people you're with. No matter where you go, if you have a strong group of friends or family, it makes all the difference.

I just got back from Cornwall, lads. That YHA volunteering was a bit of a trip, but it was worth it. I met some great people, and the views from the lighthouse were just breathtaking. Oh, I heard you went up there! I remember you talking about it in the post office the other week. Did you manage to get any good photos? Yeah, I did. A few, but I think one of them got taken by a local. It was of the sea at sunset, and the photographer said he’d like to put it in his gallery. I don’t know if I’ll ever get that back, but it was nice of him to say. That’s the kind of thing that happens when you’re out and about. You never know who you’ll meet or what you’ll end up doing. I remember when I did the cycle race in Yorkshire — it was a mad day, but I got some amazing shots of the countryside. That’s right, I remember you saying you did the Yorkshire in a day. I thought it was one of those things where you just buckle down and ride as much as you can. It was, but it wasn’t easy. I didn’t know what I was getting myself into. I had crabs – those little ones, you know, and they made the journey a bit more challenging. Crabs? You mean the ones that live in the sea? Or the ones that crawl in your shoes? No, not the sea ones. Those are the ones that get in your socks when you’re walking in the fields. I got one under my foot when I was trying to make it to the next village. It took me ages to get it out. I can only imagine. I once had that happen on a walk in the park. It was quite the surprise. But I suppose it’s all part of the adventure. Aye, it is. You never know what you’ll come across when you’re out exploring. I think the best part of the trip was the people. We had a good time with the other volunteers. That’s the spirit. You learn something new every time you travel. I think that’s what makes it all worthwhile — the stories you bring back. I couldn’t agree more. I’m always looking forward to the next trip, even if it’s just a local walk.

Right, so I was thinking, what’s for dinner? I’m starving, and I don’t want to go out again tonight. Well, we’ve got some leftover chicken and some beans. Not the most exciting, but it’ll do. Or we could just order pizza. I’m in the mood for something cheesy and greasy. Oh, you always go for the greasy stuff. Remember the time you tried to eat a whole pizza by yourself and ended up with a cheese beard? That was  one  time. And I had a good reason—my mum was in the room and I didn’t want to embarrass myself. Yeah, but you still looked like a giant melted cheese log. Alright, alright, don’t remind me. I’m still not over that. But seriously, I’m not going to argue with pizza. Let’s just do it. Yeah, pizza it is. I’ll order two large ones. One for me, one for... well, for all of us. You mean for you and your pizza obsession. Silly. Anyway, I was also thinking about the weekend. Are you going to the music festival this Saturday? Yeah, I’m planning on it. I’ve got my ticket and everything. What about you? I’m not sure yet. I’m still trying to sort out my work schedule. Maybe I’ll go. But I’m not promising anything. Yeah, I get that. Work’s been crazy lately. But if you’re free, you should definitely go. It’s a great event, and it’s a chance to see some good music. You always know how to keep the conversation positive. I try. Besides, if you’re going, I might as well tag along. I’ve heard some great stuff about the lineup. Alright then, we’re all going. It’ll be fun. I’ll even bring my best dance moves. Oh, don’t get excited. You’re not going to be dancing. You’ll be collapsing on the floor like a lovesick puppy. That’s the spirit! Alright, I’m ready to order pizza. Let’s do this. I’ll get the phone. You two can argue over the toppings. Yes, sir. Commander Pizza. You’re such a drama queen. Come on, let’s go. I’ve had enough of this conversation. It’s time for real food. Yeah, yeah, I’m coming. Just give me a minute to finish my salad.

I can't believe it's already been a week since I got back from Barcelona! I still feel like I'm on holiday, even though I've been home for days. I know, I feel the same! You were gone for three days, and now it's like you were away for a month. How was it? Did you do everything you wanted? It was amazing! We saw the Sagrada Família, the Beaches, went to a few tapas bars. Oh, and we had this incredible dinner at that little seafood place in El Raval. The food was just out of this world. That sounds incredible! I’ve always wanted to go to Barcelona, but I’m always too busy. You must have had so much fun. Did you meet anyone interesting? We did! There was this guy who worked at the hotel where we stayed. He was really friendly, and we ended up having a few drinks after checking out. He showed us around the city and gave us some great tips for the next time we go. Oh, that sounds like a nice way to spend the weekend. I’m planning to go to Paris next month for a short trip. Have you ever been? No, not yet. I’ve been meaning to for ages. I’ve heard it's just as beautiful, but maybe even more romantic. I’m thinking of going with my cousin next year. Do you want to come with me? I’d love to! But I’m not sure my shift schedule will work. I’ve got some really important exams coming up, and I can’t afford to miss work. Maybe next time? Yeah, I understand. I’m not sure about my plans either, but I’m thinking of taking a weekend trip soon. Maybe to the countryside. I’ve heard it's really peaceful there. That sounds like a good idea. I could use some time away from work. Maybe we could plan something together? I’ve been wanting to go to the seaside for a while now. Definitely! I’ll talk to my boss and see if I can take some time off. Let’s keep in touch and plan something soon. I can’t wait to go on more adventures with you. I can’t wait either! Let’s make it happen. I’m really looking forward to the next time we go out together.

Good morning, by the way, how’s the weather today? I’ve been trying to get out of the house all week, and it’s been a bit too grey for my liking. It's actually quite nice, really. I’ve been out walking my dog this morning. The sea was calm, and the breeze was just right. You’d think with the summer coming, it’d be better, but I guess it’s still too early. I suppose so. I used to live in Dorchester, you know, and the weather there is always unpredictable. But I’ve always found that the sea can be calming. It helps me clear my head after a long week at the school. That’s what I love about being an entrepreneur. You have to deal with a lot of stress, but sometimes, a walk by the sea or a good cup of coffee helps reset the mind. I remember when I first started my business, I used to work late into the night, and the pressure was non-stop. I can only imagine. As a teacher, I have my own challenges, but they’re more structured. I mean, I have to deal with exams, marking, and all the other administrative stuff, but there's a routine. I suppose that’s what makes it manageable. Yeah, I guess structure helps, but sometimes it's the lack of it that makes you grow. I did have a moment last year when I thought, “Maybe I should just go back to a more traditional job.” But then I realized that the freedom, the creativity, the ability to make decisions—those were the things I missed. That’s a good point. I’ve always found that having a balance is important. I think the key is to know when to take a step back and when to push forward. I know that sometimes you have to take risks, even if it's just in your own life. Exactly. I think that’s what makes life interesting. You don’t always have to follow the same path. I’ve had some twists and turns, but I wouldn’t change a thing. You learn from every experience, whether it’s good or bad. I agree. I think we all have our own stories, and it's the way we go about telling them that makes us who we are. Maybe one day I’ll start my own business, but for now, I’m happy teaching.

I just got a text from my cousin, and she’s mad at me. She says I didn’t tell her about the housemates we’re getting. I’m so sorry, I didn’t mean to keep it a secret. Oh no, what’s going on? You didn’t tell her? She’s your cousin, though. You’d think you’d have a bit more of a chat before making a big move like that. Yeah, I know, but I was just so busy with exams and everything. I didn’t think she’d care that much. But now she’s asking me all sorts of questions, like, are they nice? Do they have a cat? Is there a fridge? My sister would’ve done the same. She’d probably have been ranting about the housemates for weeks. But I guess I can understand. You didn’t want to overwhelm her, and you’re not wrong, but maybe next time you should’ve given her a heads-up. I know, I know. I just didn’t think it was that big of a deal. I mean, we’ve had some arguments about the space, but it’s not like we’ve moved in yet. We’re just still in the process of choosing who we’re going to be with. Yeah, but it’s better to let people in on it early. You don’t want to have to explain everything later when you’ve already moved in and it’s too late to change your mind. I guess. But also, I don’t want to rush into anything. I mean, it’s not like we have a lot of money. We’re both still studying, and we can’t afford to be in a situation where we’re not happy. That makes sense. I understand. But you know, you should be telling your cousin more. She’s a close friend, and she deserves to know. You don’t want her to feel like she’s being left out or that you’re making decisions without her input. I know, I just didn’t want to make her worry. But maybe I should’ve taken the chance to tell her properly. I mean, we’ve been together for almost a year now, and I think it’s time we started talking about more serious stuff. Yeah, I think so too. You’re not in a rush, but you’re not wasting time either.

I've just got back from the shop, love. Thought I'd get a bit of food in before it gets too cold. Oh, thank goodness. I was worried you'd forgotten again. You know how easy it is to get distracted these days. Aye, it's all the same, really. I got the usual: tinned beans, some bread, and a few eggs. Ate a bit of the toast on the way back. That’s not a bad idea. You’re getting too old to be starving yourself, you know. You should eat more like a young man. I’m not a young man, nor do I want to be. I’ve seen enough of the world to last a lifetime. Still, I suppose I should try to keep up with the times. Well, you’re not the only one. I’ve been trying to keep up with the younger generation. They’ve got all these new gadgets and apps that I can’t even understand. Aye, I’ve been watching the telly the other day, and they were showing some sort of smart fridge. You put in what you need, and it orders it for you. That sounds like a dream. I can’t imagine having to do all that. I’ve had my fridge for thirty years, and it’s still working fine. I suppose that’s the way of the world. Things change, and people change with them. I used to be a bit of a gadget man, back in my day. I remember that. You used to fix things around the house, didn’t you? Even the kettle once. Aye, I had a knack for that. Used to fix things that others thought were impossible. But now, I just leave it to the professionals. Well, you’ve done enough for one lifetime. Let’s just say you’ve earned your rest. I suppose you’re right. We’ve had a good life, haven’t we? Aye, we have. And I’m glad we’re still together, even after all these years. There’s nothing I’d rather be doing than sitting here with you, love. You know what I say, then? Let’s just enjoy every day. It’s not much, but it’s enough. Aye, that’s the way to look at it. Life’s too short to worry about the rest. I couldn’t agree more.

Oh, it’s getting late, isn’t it? I think it’s time we all got ready for dinner. I’ve got a bit of a headache from marking those GCSE papers this morning, and I’m sure I’ve overdone it. I don’t know, Grandma. I just got back from the library, and I wanted to read a bit more. I’ve got this new book that’s really got me hooked. It’s about a boy who goes on a quest to find the truth about his family. Oh, I remember when I was your age, I used to read those kinds of books too. You know, like that one with the wizard and the magic sword. I still have the cover somewhere, I think. Yeah, and I had that sword too, only it was a toy. I used to pretend I was a knight and ride around the garden on my tricycle. I remember you, Grandpa, always telling me I was too clumsy to be a knight. Oh, you were! You fell over more than you walked. But you did have that determination, didn’t you? You wanted to be a knight, and you were going to save the kingdom. I remember the day you tried to take down the garden gate with that sword. Yeah, I remember that. I think I actually broke the gate. Grandpa had to fix it. And you, Grandma, you just laughed and said I was being a brave knight, even though I was crying and covered in dirt. I did. I always believed in you, even when the others didn’t. You were a special child, even if you were a bit of a mess. And I was the one who had to clean up after you. I used to wish I could just take you away and train you properly. You’d have had a hard time of it, old chap. You couldn’t even tie your own shoes half the time. I remember you once tried to run with the dog and ended up falling into the pond. Wait, was that really you? I thought that was just a story you told us to make us laugh. It was a mix of truth and fiction, I think. But it was a good laugh, and it brought us all together. I still have that photo of you in the pond, covered in mud, with the dog wagging its tail.

Alright, lads, I’ve been thinking about these health supplements I’ve been taking. You know, the ones that claim to boost your immune system and all that. But I’ve been feeling like I’m just paying for a placebo. What’s your take? Honestly, I’m not sure. I’ve been meaning to check them out more. I’ve heard mixed things about them. Some people swear by them, but I’ve also heard stories where they’ve made people feel worse. You ever try any? Yeah, I did. I tried this one called “Vitality Max” last year. It was supposed to help with energy and focus. I felt like I had more energy at first, but then I started getting really bloated. I had to stop. It was ridiculous. That sounds rough. I used to take protein shakes all the time thinking they’d help me build muscle better. Turned out I was just eating a lot of sugar and not actually getting the protein I needed. I started doing more cardio and eating better instead. I’ve been thinking about getting a smartwatch for tracking my health. I’ve heard people say they’re great for keeping an eye on heart rate and sleep. But I’m not sure if it’s worth the money. I mean, I can just use my phone’s fitness app, right? Yeah, but I think the smartwatch gives you more detailed data. I’ve been looking into apps too. There’s one called “FitTrack Pro” that’s supposed to track everything from your calorie intake to your mood. It’s kind of like a digital diary for your health. That sounds like something a tech geek would love. I’ve been meaning to get a smartwatch, but I’m still waiting for the right one. I don’t want to spend too much, but I also don’t want to end up with something that doesn’t work. I think the key is to find something that works for you. If you’re into tech, go for it. If you’re more laid back, stick with basics. I’ve got a Fitbit, and it’s been pretty useful for keeping track of my steps and sleep. Yeah, I’ve got one too. It’s not the fanciest, but it keeps me motivated. I used to be terrible at exercising, but now I’m actually getting into it.

Alright, I think we should start making the shopping list for tomorrow. I need eggs, bread, and some fruit. What do you think? Yeah, I agree. I was just thinking about eggs and bread too. Do we need anything else for the week? I mean, the kids might need some snacks for school. Oh, I forgot about the snacks. I wanted to get some granola bars and maybe a bag of chips. But I don’t want to overdo it. I know you said we’re trying to be healthier. Yeah, but the kids love chips. Maybe just a small bag. And if we can get some fresh fruit like apples or bananas, that would be good. My mum always said fruit is better than snacks. Right, and I think we should check the fridge and pantry before we go. We might not need everything. Oh wait, have we seen the wasps around the garden again? Oh, those were the ones I saw earlier. They were pretty aggressive. I think we might need to do something about them before the kids go out. Yeah, I saw them too. I’ve read that you can use something like vinegar or a garlic spray to keep them away. Does that work? I remember reading something like that. I think it’s better than using insecticide because it’s safer around kids. But if they’re really bad, we might need to call a professional. Wait, what if one of them bites me? I’ve heard that you can use something like an antihistamine or a cold compress. But I’ve also heard that if it’s a wasp sting, it might be more painful than a bee sting. Actually, wasp stings can be more dangerous because they inject venom directly. I’d recommend avoiding direct contact and using something like Benadryl for the itching. If it gets swollen or red, you should see a doctor. Okay, thanks for the advice. I’ll make sure to carry some antihistamine pills just in case. Let’s not forget to add some first aid supplies to the shopping list too. That’s a good idea. And by the way, did you see the football match on TV last night? It was epic. I think the team we support is going to do well this season. Yeah, I was really into it. I even stayed up late to watch the final half.

Hey, do you remember that time we had that weird PE lesson with that teacher who thought jumping jacks were a form of art? Oh yeah! I still can't believe he made us all do 100 of them in a row. I think I passed out halfway through. That's not even the worst. Remember when he tried to teach us how to do a handstand? I think I broke my arm trying to do it. Oh no, was it really that bad? I thought I was doing okay, but then I heard someone laughing and looked over and saw my teacher doing a handstand! It was so embarrassing. Yeah, and then he said, "You guys are all just not flexible enough!" Like, we're 14, not 10! That’s the thing about PE teachers – they’re always trying to make us do things we don’t want to do. I mean, I like science more than that. Totally! I mean, who wouldn’t want to sit in a lab with beakers and microscopes instead of sweating in the gym? Exactly! But still, I think the worst part of school is Instagram. I swear, it’s like everyone feels the need to post about everything – even the most boring things. Yeah, and some of the people on there don’t even go to the same school as us. I mean, I saw one of our teachers in a video with some TikToker. Wasn’t that weird? Oh my gosh, that was so awkward. I think the TikToker was trying to make it look like they were a real student. But then they said something about “studying for exams” and it was so out of context. I know! I mean, it’s kind of funny, but it also makes me feel like we’re not even real. Like, are we just some kind of social media content? Ugh, I know. I think we need to stick to our own stuff. Like, instead of watching all those videos, maybe we should just do something fun. Like, go to the park or something. Yeah! Maybe we can even go to the park and post about it. If we go, we could at least be real people, not just pixels on a screen. Yeah, that sounds like a plan. I mean, we’re not going to change the world, but maybe we can at least have a little bit of fun.

I can't believe I've got a cold. I was supposed to be working on that research report today, and now I’m just sitting here with a fever and a sore throat. You poor thing. I’m so sorry to hear that. I had food poisoning last week, and it was a real nightmare. I couldn't even eat properly for days. Yeah, I know what you mean. I remember watching a documentary on the NHS a few weeks ago. It said that hospitals are dealing with more cases of food poisoning and colds than ever before. It was really worrying. I think part of it is just people not being careful with food anymore. I mean, I’ve been trying to get back into cooking, but I’m still not confident. I tried making a stir fry the other day, and it ended up being inedible. That’s a shame. I guess we all have moments like that. Speaking of which, I remember reading about a new technology they’re using in hospitals to monitor patients’ vital signs using cameras. It’s based on body language recognition. Oh, that sounds really high-tech. I read about it in a journal article last week. They use AI to detect subtle changes in body language that might indicate pain or discomfort. It’s amazing how far we’ve come in medical tech. It really is. I think it could be a game-changer, especially for people who can’t communicate their symptoms clearly, like young children or elderly patients. But I also worry about privacy. What if the system misinterprets something? That’s a fair point. It’s all well and good if it works, but there’s always the risk of misdiagnosis. I guess that’s where the human element is still so important. Definitely. I mean, even with all the technology, there’s something to be said for a doctor reading someone’s body language in person. I think it’s just a part of the whole healthcare experience. Exactly. I also remember watching a show with Lloyd Grossman the other day. I know he’s not exactly a health expert, but he made some interesting comments about vaccination and public health. It was a bit of a mixed bag. Yeah, he’s a bit of a controversial figure, isn’t he? I think he started out as a comedian but got into politics and media.

I just landed the word "syllabic" on the board. That’s one of those tricky ones, isn’t it? Oh, I know! I’ve been trying to think of that for ages. It’s such a long word, and it’s not even a common one. Do you think I should use it again? Well, if you’ve got it in your vocabulary, by all means use it. I remember when I was a teacher, I used to encourage students to use interesting words. It shows you’ve got a good grasp of the language. Yes, I agree. It makes the game more exciting when you throw in some less common words. But don’t overdo it, Myrtle. You don’t want to get stuck with a rack full of letters you can’t use. I think I’ve got a good rack now, though. Let me see... "Scrabble" has been a great way to keep my mind sharp. I’ve been getting better at thinking on my feet. That’s true. It’s like a mental workout, isn’t it? I’ve even started using some words in my work emails. It’s amazing how something as simple as a board game can have such an impact. You’re not the only one. I often find myself using words I learned from Scrabble in my lessons. It’s quite rewarding to see the children pick them up too. And isn't it great how this game brings people together? I remember when I was your age, I used to play with my students after school. It was a great way to bond and unwind. Yes, it’s a great way to chat and have fun. Speaking of which, I was thinking about the gridlock at the shopping centre last weekend. Have you all been there? Oh, I was stuck in that traffic for over an hour. I nearly missed my appointment for the music magazine. I was so frustrated. I had a similar experience. I was waiting for my daughter to pick up some supplies and got stuck in the queue at the butcher’s shop. I think it was the busiest day of the week. I’ve had my share of queueing experiences too. But I always make it a point to be patient. I think it’s just part of living in a bustling city like Manchester. True, but you know what really gets me?

I've been meaning to ask you, what do you think about that talk they had about the printing systems? It really got me thinking, you know. Oh, you mean the one where that inventor from Germany was talking about how he built this whole system from scratch? Fascinating stuff, really. I mean, I never thought of it that way before. I know, it's amazing how you can take something so simple and turn it into a business. I remember when I was running my gallery, it was always about how to present the art. Didn’t think about the mechanics of it. Exactly! And you know, I was in Germany once for an exhibition. That was a few years back. I had a friend who was an art dealer there, and he showed me around. I remember how they set up the whole exhibition space. It was all about flow, about guiding the viewer through the pieces, just like a good museum. That does sound a lot like the principles we used in our gallery back in the day. We had to make sure that the lighting and the placement of the pieces highlighted the art, not the walls. Oh, you're absolutely right. And the printing system he spoke about, it's like that. It's got to be intuitive, right? I suppose so. It's interesting how these systems can be both technical and artistic. It makes you realize how much work goes into making things look easy. Like those vintage posters you see at the market. They look so simple, but the process behind them is so intricate. Exactly. And the guy from Germany, he talked about how he had to educate customers on how to use the system. It was a bit of a challenge, but once people got the hang of it, it was like magic. I can imagine. You have to make it so user-friendly that even the least tech-savvy person can navigate it. It's surprising how much the right design can change the experience. It really is. I think that’s the key to any successful project, whether it’s art or technology. It’s not just about what you do, but how you do it. You're absolutely right. That's something I've always believed in. I mean, I never wanted my art to just sit in a gallery.

I can't believe we've been on the road for six hours already. I was just reading about the history of the word "Cornwall"—it’s actually from the Cornish people, right? I can't believe we've made it this far. I just had to tell you about that long cycle ride I did as a kid. You know, when I was about twelve, my dad took me on this epic trip from Almondsbury all the way to Exeter. I've been thinking a lot about how we can use social networking to support our educational project. It aligns with the inclusive education principles we both support. I couldn't agree more. Let's start by outlining a few case study ideas and then figure out the best way to present them.

I just had the most incredible conversation with my old friend, Tom. We met up for coffee, and he was talking about his recent trip to the coast. It reminded me how much I miss the sea. I think we both need that. Life gets so busy, and it’s easy to forget how important it is to take time for each other and for ourselves. I couldn’t agree more. Let’s make it happen. I’ll check the weather and get back to you. It’s about time we all took a break and just enjoyed the sea again.

I just can't believe what I saw on that fashion show last night. That red dress... it was like it had been dipped in blood! Yeah, I know. I mean, it was  bold —but honestly, I don’t think it’s for everyone. I’d say it’s more like a statement piece. You know, for someone who’s not afraid to make a splash. I think it’s interesting how fashion is starting to blur the lines between art and wearables. It’s like, you don’t just wear clothes anymore—you  wear  a piece of performance art. Exactly! It’s about time someone started making fashion a bit more...  ethical . To sustainable fashion! And to not getting murdered by the fashion police. To not getting murdered by the fashion police! And to not being  dipped in blood  on the red carpet. Cheers! Now, who’s up for a coffee and a trip to the thrift store? I’m in. But don’t expect me to look like a  victim  of the fashion industry.

Mum, I just got a message from my friend Lily saying her photos for the school magazine are  still  not good enough. She keeps uploading them and then deleting them. Oh, I remember when I was your age, I used to take photos of everything — my dog, the cat, even the dust on the windowsill. But I never got it right. I know, but I think I’m getting better. I tried using the camera app on my phone last week and took some pictures of the sea at Hastings. I even got the light right! That’s brilliant! I’m proud of you. You know, when I was at college, I used to take photographs for the university magazine. It’s one of the few things I was good at. Really? Did you ever take pictures of anything scary? Just remember, even the best photographers had to start somewhere.

I just popped round, didn't I? You know, I thought I’d give you a shout and see if you wanted to go for a walk or something. It’s been ages since we've had a proper chat. Oh, you came round! I hear you, but I still think the problem is deeper than that. I mean, how can you even apply for a house if you can’t sleep at night? I’ve been having trouble sleeping since the kids started acting up. I think I’ve been up more than I’ve been down. That’s very hard. I’m trying to teach my students how to manage their time and get some rest, but I have to admit, it’s not easy.

I've been thinking a lot lately, Bob. I know it's not the best time, but I feel like I need to talk about this. You remember how I've been feeling a bit adrift since I retired? That means more than you know. I think I'm ready to take this step, even if it's scary. I just need to go slow and stay grounded.

I've been meaning to ask you, how did you find the job interview the other day? I heard it was for a position in Manchester. Oh, it was a bit of a rollercoaster. I think it's important to encourage that kind of passion, even if it's controversial. At the end of the day, we've all got to find a way to navigate these kinds of debates together. Exactly. I think it's about the balance between having strong opinions and maintaining respect for others' views.

I've been thinking, you know, we could put together a mousetrap game for the kids. It's a classic, and it's always a hit at family gatherings. I mean, in London, we usually just use traps and catch mice, but not like that. I’ve heard of kids trying to build their own mousetrap games, though. You can’t outsmart a mouse with too many strings and whistles. Yeah, I think you have to keep it simple. I mean, the American go-to is the classic snap trap. It’s reliable and doesn’t require a lot of creativity.

I’m back! I brought some clothes for the weekend, just thought I’d check in before I unpack. Oh, and I got some really nice stuff—finally found that jacket I’ve been eyeing for ages. Oh, brilliant! So, what do you think of that last try? I swear, that player from Leinster was inches away from scoring. It was a brutal tackle, but fair play, he kept his cool. Yeah, it was a proper rugby moment. So, do you know, I’ve been thinking about moving house again. I’m just so tired of this flat. It’s been over two years since I moved in, and I still haven’t found a proper place to put everything. Alright, so I just got back from a weekend trip to Exeter. That was a real trip — not just the weather, but the roads were a mess. I swear, I had to park two miles away and walk the rest. It was like a real dog movie.

I can't believe I just spent £200 on a new set of tyres. I thought they’d last a bit longer than that. You’re not the only one. Oh, there’s someone at the door. I’ll just get it. Ah, it’s the postman with the weekly newsletter. Mum, you don’t have to get up. We’ve got it covered. Oh, he’s not the postman. Alright, do you remember the pirate story I told you last night? The one about Captain Blood and his treasure map? Yes! I mean, do you really think they all had those? I don’t think so! I think some of them were just pretending to be pirates to scare people off. Or maybe they just wanted to look cool. I mean, I’ve seen pirates in the movies, and they look really dramatic. Definitely dramatic! But wait, have you ever thought about how pirates actually lived? I read a book last week about real pirates, and it was amazing. Was it about the Blackbeard or someone else? Both! Blackbeard was really scary. He had a beard that was so thick and hairy, people thought he was a ghost. That sounds cool! But I wonder if he really had that beard or if it was just a way to scare people. I think it was real! But maybe he used wax or something to make it look more terrifying. Anyway, speaking of terrifying, have you heard about the circus workshop coming up? It's in Stratford, right? Yes! Mom said we might be able to go if we get enough people. I've always wanted to see a real circus. Me too! I want to ride the trapeze and maybe learn how to juggle. I think it's going to be fun. That sounds fantastic. And it’s right near Shakespeare’s hometown. I think we should go. It’ll be a great way to celebrate Shakespeare week, too. We could even make stop motion animation of our own pirate adventure! Like with clay figures and magic. Yeah! And maybe even add some magic tricks. I saw a video of a magician who makes things disappear with his hands. That’s a great idea! I’ll start planning the story. Who knows, maybe we’ll be the next Pirates of the Caribbean! Or the next Wonderland! Or maybe even the next Shakespeare! Well, adventurers, I think we have a lot to look forward to!

Well, do you remember that time we were in Jeddah, and I tried to sail my little boat from there to Cyprus? I had no idea the rules were so strict! I thought it would be a simple trip, just a bit of fun. But I got caught by the coast guard and ended up in a cell for a few hours! Oh, I remember! You were so upset. I thought you were joking at first. But I had a friend who had a similar experience. He was caught trying to smuggle a whole bunch of dental magazines into the country. Apparently, the customs officer thought they were contraband. Oh, that's a good one. I still can't believe that. But what’s even more interesting is how strict the laws are on alcohol. I was teaching in Saudi Arabia, and I had to be very careful. Even bringing a single bottle of wine across the border could get you into trouble. Yes, I remember that too. When I was working as a dentist, I had to take a few holidays. One time, I was in Riyadh and decided to have a drink with some colleagues. I got caught and had to explain myself to the police. It was a bit of a shock, but I wasn't arrested. Just a warning. Ha! I had a similar experience. I was in Jeddah trying to buy some whiskey, and I thought I could sneak it past the customs. But no, they caught me. I had to pay a fine and give it up. I was so embarrassed. I can imagine. But you had the better end of the deal. I was once in a country where even talking about alcohol in public was frowned upon. I had to be very careful not to mention it at all. It was a bit of a culture shock. I think the biggest challenge was adapting to the social norms. In Saudi Arabia, everything is so rigid. You can’t even sit with the opposite sex in certain places. I was teaching English, and I had to be extremely careful with my language. We had to be careful not to use any slang or idioms that might be offensive. That must have been difficult. I think the hardest part for me was the lack of personal freedom. I was used to being able to do whatever I wanted, but in those countries, everything was so controlled.

I can't believe it's already April. You know, I was just thinking about how quickly time flies. We had those big plans for the summer, and now it feels like we're already halfway through the year. Yeah, I know, I've been feeling the same. But it's also good to have the holidays coming up. I think I'm going to take the kids to Cornwall again this year. The sea air always does wonders for the kids, and it gives me a break from the office. Cool! I hope I get to go too. But, like, I don't know... I'm not sure if I can convince my parents to let me go. They still think I'm too young for that kind of trip. I mean, I'm 15 now! I should be able to make my own decisions. Oh, I remember when I was 15. You were still trying to figure out whether you liked boys or girls. And now you're talking about holidays and travel? Time does move fast. But I think you're more mature than you think. Yeah, I think she's got a point. She's not just a teenager anymore. She's starting to think about her future. I remember when I was in her position, I was so worried about school and grades, and trying to figure out what I wanted to do after. It's a tough time. You're not helping, Mum. I know I'm just a kid, but I'm doing my best. I got a part-time job at the local library, and I'm even thinking about applying for a summer job. I want to earn some money and save up for that camera I saw online. That's great, love. You're showing initiative. I think you're going to do very well. Speaking of which, have you thought about applying for that work experience at the marketing agency? It could be a great opportunity. I told her about it, but she was a bit hesitant. I think she feels like she's not ready. But you know, she's got a lot of potential. She just needs to keep pushing herself. Yeah, I know. I'll try. I just need a little push. And maybe a bit more time to think about it. You've got all the time in the world.

I can't believe we've made it through Istria without getting lost. I thought for sure we'd end up in some remote village with no signal and a poor signal for GPS. It's a bit of a twist, isn't it? I mean, you'd think with all those vineyards and olive groves, there'd be more signposts. But I reckon it's all about the charm of the place. A little chaos adds to the character. Oh, I don't mind a bit of journey! It's just like the old days when we used to get lost in Bolton trying to find the nearest takeaway. Still, I'm starving. Any idea when we'll get to that truffle farm you mentioned? Actually, I've got a bit of a plan. We're going to stop at the next village and grab some local cheese and wine. I heard about a chef there who's been using Istrian truffles in his dishes for years. He's got a real reputation. That sounds amazing. I've always been a fan of truffles—especially when they're paired with something like duck or roast pork. I remember my A-levels, I had to write an essay on the history of truffle farming. It was a bit of a stretch, but it helped me get a good grade. I know the feeling. I was the one who got picked for that group project on the history of truffles. You don't even know what you're in for until you're in the middle of it. But it's those little moments that stick with you. I'm still trying to get my head around stem cells and education. My teacher said it's a big topic, but I'm not sure I'll ever get it. I mean, I can't even remember the difference between a mitosis and a meiosis. That's not so bad. I've got a friend who's a biology teacher. He says it's all about understanding the basics before you can move on. I mean, if you can't get meiosis, how are you going to get to something like CRISPR? Yeah, I guess it's like learning to drive. You start with the basics—turning the key, putting the car in gear—then you move on to more complex things. Exactly.

So, I was just thinking—did you know that the word 'humbug' actually comes from a play by Lewis Carroll? I read it in a linguistics journal last week. It’s fascinating how certain words evolve over time.    Hmm, I didn't know that. I mean, I know 'humbug' is used to describe nonsense, but I never thought it had such a literary origin. I guess language is like a living thing, isn’t it? Always changing and adapting.    Yeah, I think that’s one of the things I love about studying language. It’s not just about words—it’s about how people use them, how they shift meaning, and how they reflect the culture around them. I mean, I’m not even sure if I’ve ever used the word ‘humbug’ in a real conversation.    That’s funny. I used it last week during a meeting. I was trying to convince my team that the project was not just a ‘humbug’—that it had real value. They didn’t get it, though. Maybe it’s more of a British expression.    I can imagine. I’ve heard people use words like that in the marketing world too. Like, ‘this is just a buzzword’ or ‘that’s all just hot air.’ Sometimes it’s hard to tell what’s real and what’s just jargon.    I’ve been working on a project that’s been a bit of a rollercoaster. I think I might have to be more careful with my vocabulary now. I don’t want to accidentally say something that sounds like a ‘humbug’ in the office.    That’s a good point. Language can be so powerful. It can both connect people and, at times, create misunderstandings. I think that’s why it’s so important for language researchers to study how it’s used in different contexts.    I suppose that’s why we’re all here, right? Even if we’re not all in the same field. It’s interesting how our occupations shape the way we use language.    Yeah, I guess you could say that. I mean, I’m just a projects assistant, but I’ve noticed how different departments use words in completely different ways. It’s like a whole new language every day.    You might as well be a linguist yourself. You’re already starting to see the patterns. I’m impressed.    Well, I’m not sure I can claim that title, but I’ll take the compliment.

I just checked the map again, and we’re only about a 40-minute drive from Tarnow. Should be easy enough, but I’m still a bit nervous about the roads. I’ve never been this far east in Poland. I know what you mean. I’ve driven through some pretty remote parts of the country, but Tarnow isn’t too bad. Just make sure you keep an eye out for the signs, especially near the village. I remember there was a stretch where the road narrowed a bit, and it’s easy to get lost if you’re not careful. Yeah, I’ve heard about that. I’m hoping the GPS will keep me on track, but I’ve had some weird experiences with it before. I once followed it into a forest and ended up walking for half an hour. Ha! That’s the trouble with relying too much on technology. I prefer to look at the road signs and keep a map handy. You never know when the GPS might go off the rails, especially in rural areas. Good point. I’ll bring the physical map just in case. Speaking of which, do you think we should stop for supplies before we go? I feel like we’re running low on food, and I don’t want to arrive hungry. Definitely. There’s a small town called Szczawnica just a few miles before Tarnow. It has a few grocery stores and a café. We can grab a quick bite and rest for a bit. Plus, it’s a good chance to stretch our legs and maybe buy some snacks for the road. Perfect. I’ll make a mental note to stop there. I’ve also been meaning to ask about your trip to Poland last year. How did it go? I heard you stayed in a hostel in Kraków. It was great! The hostel was run by a bunch of volunteers, and they had all sorts of activities. I even took a walking tour of the Old Town. It was amazing how different it felt compared to the cities I’ve been to in the UK. The architecture was so different, and the people were so friendly. That sounds incredible. I’ve always wanted to visit Poland, but I’ve been putting it off for a while. I guess it’s time to start planning a proper trip.

I just can’t get over the new kit Manchester City have. It’s so bold, isn’t it? That neon blue and white with those giant sponsor logos. I mean, it’s not like they’re hiding anything, is it? Not anymore. Yeah, I agree. It’s a bit much, to be honest. I don’t mind the design, but the amount of sponsor stuff on the front—it feels like they’re giving away their identity. Why not just have a clean look and let the team’s name shine through? Fair point. But then again, the money they’re getting from sponsors is massive. It’s not just about the kit; it’s about the brand. You’ve got to think about the business side of it. I mean, if you’re a team like Manchester City, you’re not just playing football anymore—you’re a global brand. I get that, but it doesn’t mean they have to sacrifice their identity for a logo. I mean, I still love the old kits, you know? The traditional ones with the club crest and minimal branding. There’s something nostalgic about them. Definitely. I remember when clubs had more creativity with their kits. You’d get those classic designs that people still wear today. But now it feels like every team is just selling the same thing: sponsorship and merch. It’s a bit of a shame, isn’t it? I mean, football was meant to be about the passion and the team, not just the branding. But then again, the game has changed. When I was growing up, we didn’t have all these sponsors everywhere. It was simpler. I guess that’s the thing. Sports sponsorship has become such a huge part of the game. Even the stadiums now have massive ads. It’s like you can’t escape it. I mean, I was just at a match last week, and the screens were filled with McDonald’s stuff. You can’t even watch the game without seeing their logo. Oh, I know. I tried to avoid the ads, but honestly, it’s everywhere. It’s like being in a branded space. I’ve started to think maybe the next step is just having a McDonald’s kit. I mean, with how much they’re paying for sponsorships, it’s not far-fetched. Ha! I’d love to see that.

I just got a new recording of our conversation from last week, and I can't believe how much I said. I feel like I've been ranting about everything from the cost of living to my brother-in-law's latest antics. Oh, I bet you did. You always have something to say, even when it's not really important. I was just thinking about that train trip we took last month with the kids. Remember how we got stuck on the platform for an hour because of a broken signal? Oh, don't even start. That was the worst day. The kids were squabbling, the train was delayed, and I was so stressed I could barely breathe. I still can't believe I made it through that without losing my temper. It was ridiculous. I mean, I've been on trains all my life, and I've never had an experience like that. But you know what's even worse? The way I've been feeling lately. I'm just so tired, and I don't even know where to start. I mean, why do I feel like I'm falling apart? I know, I know. You've been going through so much. I think it's just the way things are right now. With the job seekers allowance, the cost of living, and the way people are acting these days, it's hard to stay positive. I mean, have you seen the way people are talking about benefits? It's like they don't even know what it means to be someone who's struggling. Yeah, I've noticed that too. It's so frustrating. I don't want to be seen as someone who's just asking for help, but I don't know what else I can do. I've tried everything, and still, I can't find a job. It's like the system is set up to fail people like me. I know, I really do. But you're not alone. I've been there too, and I know it's tough. Maybe you should talk to someone. I mean, you don't have to do it all on your own. Let me know if you need help with anything. I'm here for you. Thanks, I appreciate that. I just need a little support right now. It's hard being unemployed, especially when everyone else seems to have everything figured out.

So, do you think the sat nav is finally working reliably now? I’ve had enough of it giving me wrong directions. I nearly missed my train last week because of it. Oh, I know what you mean. I’ve had a few close calls with it too. Last week, it told me to take a road that didn’t exist. I ended up walking for 10 minutes just to get back on the right track. I nearly got stuck in a field. Oh, I know that feeling. I’ve had the same thing happen when I was driving to the shops. I thought I saw a road, but it turned out to be a dirt track. I had to turn around and go the long way. It was quite an adventure. It’s ridiculous. I mean, I’m not even sure how these things work anymore. I just hope that one day they’ll be accurate. Wait, did you hear about that plane crash in the last week? Yeah, I heard that. They said it was a small plane that crashed near the airport. I was just thinking about how technology can be both a blessing and a curse. Sometimes it leaves us in a worse situation than before. It’s funny how things change. I remember when we used to just rely on maps and compasses. I think my son would have had a better chance of getting somewhere without the sat nav. You know what I found interesting? I saw a new convenience store in town. It’s called “Quick Bite.” I stopped in the other day for a coffee and some snacks. They serve really good pastries and have a great range of drinks. Oh, I’ve heard about that. I think they opened up a couple of months ago. I haven’t been there yet, but I need to. I like the idea of being able to grab a quick snack without having to go to the supermarket. I like that idea. I used to go to the supermarket a lot, but it’s such a long drive. I can’t stand the traffic. It’s gotten so bad over the years. I always end up waiting for ages just to get to the store. I remember when I used to drive to work. That was back in the day when traffic wasn’t as bad.

Hey, do you know what’s up with the new trainee teachers? I swear, one of them just walked into class and started talking about quantum physics like it’s part of the English curriculum. Oh, don’t be ridiculous! They’re just trying to make things interesting. But honestly, I think they’re making it harder for us. I mean, who even knows what quantum physics is? We’re supposed to be learning about Shakespeare and GCSE English, not physics. Exactly! I mean, it’s one thing to have a teacher who’s passionate about science, but it’s another thing to have one who thinks they’re teaching English. I had a test last week on  Macbeth  and the teacher started talking about the chemical reactions in the play. Like, what? What’s the point? I know, right? And the worst part is, she was so excited about it that she made us all write an essay about the “scientific principles behind the witches’ prophecy.” I think I’m going to fail that one just for the sake of it. Oh, I can relate. I tried to write about the superstition and the symbolism, but she said it wasn’t “scientific enough.” I mean, what is she even grading on? Do we all have to be scientists now? I think the school is trying to push more STEM subjects into the English department. It’s like they think every subject should be a bit of everything. But honestly, I don’t think that’s helping. We’re all confused and stressed. I know. And what about the people at school? I mean, the teachers are supposed to help us, but sometimes it feels like they’re just trying to impress the headmaster or something. I get that. I’ve heard some of the older teachers are trying to get promoted, so they’re adopting all these new methods, even if they don’t make sense. It’s like they’re trying to be the next big thing in education. Yeah, but we’re just trying to pass our exams. I mean, what if we fail? I’m not even sure what we’re supposed to do anymore. I know. But maybe we should start a study group. That way, we can all help each other out and figure things out together. That’s a good idea. I’ll talk to the others and see if they’re up for it.

Alright, so I was just thinking about religion again. I mean, I’ve been watching this show called  The Matrix , and it makes me wonder—how do people find meaning in life anyway? I don’t know, love. That show’s weird. But you know, I was brought up in a catholic family, and I think that’s why I feel like I need to believe in something. I mean, I used to go to church every Sunday, but now I just... don’t know. Yeah, I guess. But what if there’s no God? Like, what if we’re just all in this simulation, like in  The Matrix ? That’s what I’ve been wondering about. My friend said it’s like being in a dream. Mmm... Oh, look at you, little man. You’re just learning to talk. But I bet you’ll grow up and start questioning things too. Maybe even join a cult or something? Wait, what? Why would I join a cult? I mean, I’ve heard of Scientology, right? They’re like a religion, but it’s not real. It’s just people making up stuff. I know, but it’s got a lot of followers. I heard some people think it’s a scam. It’s got all these rules and stuff. I mean, I don’t know. I just don’t want someone to take advantage of my son. Yeah, I guess. But what about nuns? I mean, I’ve seen these old movies where they’re like, super strict and stuff. But I don’t think they’re all bad. Some of them help people. True. My sister was a nun for a while. She helped a lot of people in the community. But she left because she felt like she wasn’t being heard. She said it was too controlling. That sounds intense. I mean, I can’t imagine living in a place like that. I’d probably go crazy. I know. But sometimes people need structure. Especially when they’re young. You know, growing up in the city, it’s so chaotic. But life’s like that. You have to find your own path. I guess. I just feel like I’m confused. I don’t know what I believe in. I mean, I don’t even know if I believe in anything. But I want to. You’ll figure it out, love.

I just got a text from my cousin. She's going to do some dancing lessons in the city next week. I think it's about time I gave it a go too. I mean, I’ve always been a bit awkward on my feet, but I’ve heard it’s a great way to meet people. Yeah, I remember when I first tried ballroom dancing at university. It was like trying to walk on water. But once you get the rhythm, it's actually kind of fun. You know, it's not just about the dance steps—it's about connection. That's true. I’ve been thinking about it for ages. I’ve even been checking out the local studios online. You know, they do all sorts of styles now—salsa, tango, even belly dancing. I was like, “Why not pick one and just try it?” That’s the spirit! You can always give it a go and see if you like it. I think it might help you meet some people too, you know, if you're looking for a new hobby or even a new friend. Speaking of friends, I’ve been meaning to ask you about that charity event we talked about earlier. Have you sorted out the details for the one in Manchester? Yeah, I actually did. We’re planning to do a bit of fundraising through a bake sale and a quiz night. I’ve already sent out the invitations. It’s going to be a great way to raise some money and have a bit of fun too. That sounds like a good plan. I’m in. I can help with the baking. I’ve got some great recipes from my mom. You know, the kind that make people go “Oh my god, that’s the best cake I’ve ever had.” Perfect! I can’t wait to see what you come up with. Oh, and speaking of food, I’ve been thinking about trying that new restaurant near the station. The reviews are amazing. I heard about it too. I’ve been meaning to go. I think it’s somewhere that serves both meat and vegetarian dishes. I’ve been trying to eat more healthily lately, but it’s hard when you’re in a city and you can’t always find good food. I know what you mean. But it’s worth the trip, I promise.

So, do you think we should stop at the next market? I’ve heard the local olive oil is amazing and I’d love to try some fresh local produce. I think that’s a great idea. I’ve heard the markets in Istria are fantastic—especially for fresh food and local crafts. We might even find some nice souvenirs for the kids. Yeah, I heard the markets here are like a big festival. I bet there’s a lot of cool stuff to check out. Can we get some pizza too? I’m starving. Definitely get some pizza. You know, I’ve been to some markets in London, but I think the ones here are way more lively. You can’t beat the mix of local culture and food. I agree, the vibe here is so different from the big cities. It’s like a real slice of life. And the cars here—especially the old ones—are just so unique. I bet some of them are from the 70s or 80s. Oh, I’ve noticed that too. The cars are a mix of old and new. I think it’s part of the charm. Plus, the roads here are so scenic. We should try to take a detour and see the countryside more. Can we stop at that hilltop park we saw on the map? I’m sure there’s a nice view from there. Maybe even a picnic? That sounds perfect. I’ve always loved the idea of a picnic with a view. And with the weather like this, it’s a great day to be outdoors. I think the olive oil and wine we’ll buy from the market would make a great picnic. I can’t wait. I’m also thinking about trying one of those local music festivals we heard about. They’re supposed to have live music, food stalls, and art. That’s a good point. I think the festival season is just starting. We should check the dates and see if we can plan a stop. You know, the kids would love it. Yeah, and if we take a caravan or camp somewhere, we could have a really cool experience. I remember seeing some amazing camping sites online. I love the idea of a caravan. It’s a bit of a challenge, but it’s also a unique way to travel. I think we could manage it if we plan ahead.

Right, so I was just telling my mates about the recording I made of that weird game we played last night. It was like, you know, that one where you have to say random words and make them into a story? Oh yeah, that game! I was so awful at it. I ended up saying “anal” and then tried to make it into a story about a kitchen appliance. It was ridiculous. Oh no, you said “anal”? That’s not even a word! Yeah, but what if someone takes it the wrong way? I mean, it’s a word that can have a different meaning, you know? It’s not just a game anymore. That’s true. But in the context of the game, it was just a word. I mean, we all knew what we were doing. It was just part of the fun. I guess. Maybe I’ll just keep it to myself. I mean, it’s not like I want to ruin the memory of that night. It was probably the most entertaining thing that’s happened in a while. Exactly! You should just keep it as a joke. No one’s going to take it seriously, and if they do, well, that’s on them. I think it’s better not to share it. You know how some people are. One wrong word and you’re in trouble. Alright, let’s just agree to keep it a secret. We can all be the only people who know about that recording.

Mate, I swear I've been having these weird dreams about food lately. Last night, I dreamed I was in a Michelin-starred restaurant, but all the dishes were just toast and hummus. It was bizarre. You’re not the only one. I had a dream last week where I was in a food fight at a café, and everyone was throwing pizza. I ended up with a piece of garlic bread in my hair. But I reckon the real issue is we’re all too busy with work, and we don’t even get time to think about what we’re eating. It could be fun, and it might even get us out of the habit of just grabbing something from the fridge. That’s a good idea. I could cook something that’s not too complicated. Maybe a lasagna? I’ve always wanted to try making a proper chocolate cake. My mum’s recipe is legendary, but I’ve never got it right. Maybe this is my chance. And I’ll bring a salad. I’ve been trying to eat more greens, but I’m not sure what I’m doing wrong. Maybe I can get some help from the two of you. To a better relationship with food, and maybe a little bit of fun in the office.

I've been thinking a lot about social networking lately. You know, how it's changing the way people interact. It's almost like we're all just scrolling through life instead of really living it. Yeah, I can't deny that. I mean, I've started spending more time on LinkedIn than I used to. It's almost like it's the new coffee break. You know, you're not just chatting with colleagues, you're networking, learning, and even finding new job opportunities. Oh, I do that too. But I also use Facebook for more personal stuff. I've made some great connections through there. My cousin who lives in Australia even found me through Facebook, and now we talk more regularly. That's interesting. I've got a friend from back home in Radcliffe who's been on Facebook for years. But he's always been pretty private. I guess the problem is, it's so easy to connect with people, but sometimes it's hard to know who’s real and who's just faking it. That's true. I've had some people who just seem too perfect. Like, they're always posting about their travels, their beautiful homes, and perfect family photos. It's a bit much sometimes. I mean, it's all good and well, but maybe we should remember that everyone has their own version of reality. Exactly. I think social media has its place, but it's important to keep a balance. I mean, I still prefer face-to-face conversations. There's something about seeing someone in person that just can't be replicated online. I agree. I think the key is to use social networking as a tool, not a replacement for real interaction. I mean, it's a great way to stay in touch with people, but you can't replace the human element. Yeah, and besides, there's the chance to make new friends and learn new things. I mean, I've met some really interesting people through LinkedIn. One of them even recommended me for a job at the library. That's good to hear. I think the main thing is staying mindful of how we use it. It's not all bad, but it's easy to get lost in the noise. I couldn't agree more. Social networking's a double-edged sword, but as long as we remember to use it wisely, it can be a powerful tool.

I've been thinking a lot about the new hospice project. We need to make sure it's not just a building, but a place that truly supports the needs of patients and their families. What do you think about the location we're considering? I agree completely. The location is crucial. It should be accessible, yet offer a peaceful environment. I've been reviewing the site maps and the local health services. The proximity to existing healthcare facilities would be beneficial. Oh, yes, and it’s important to consider the relationships with local hospices as well. We don't want to duplicate services but rather complement them. I've spoken with a few people from the hospice association, and they seem open to collaboration. That's good to hear. We need to be careful not to overextend the budget, though. I've been in talks with some estate agents about potential sites. They've highlighted several options, but we need to look at the long-term implications for the community and the patients. Absolutely, and the use of the budget will be key. I've been thinking about the business case—how we can justify the investment. Maybe we can focus on the end-of-life care and the nursing support as a differentiator. Exactly. The rationale for the location is tied to the healthcare landscape here in Kent. We need to take into account the demographics and the current utilization of health services. It's a bit of a balancing act between accessibility and the financial sustainability of the project. I think also the political aspect can't be ignored. There's a lot of talk about health budgets and how they're being reallocated. We need to make sure our case is strong enough to secure funding and support from local authorities. And the building itself—what do you think it should look like? We need to create a space that's both functional and comforting. I'm thinking about incorporating natural light and open spaces to promote well-being. I'm with you. It's not just about the structure, it's about the atmosphere. We need to involve the community in the design process to ensure it meets their needs. Have you thought about how we'll communicate the vision to the public? I've been working on a presentation for the next board meeting. I think it's time we start finalizing the details and getting feedback from the team.

I just found this photo from when we were all at the Royal Ascot a few years back. Can you believe it’s been so long? I still remember how hot it was, and how you nearly fainted from the heat, Mark. Oh, don’t remind me. I was so proud of myself for making it through the day without collapsing. But look at you, Julie—still in that pink dress you wore.
