It’s always good to have a chat, you know, even if it’s about something like debt collecting or PPI. That sounds like a good idea, Bob. I’d love to see everyone again.

I just had the most frustrating day at work. I was teaching a group of teenagers about the legal system, and I got so confused when one of them asked me, "Does the judge get paid more than the barrister?" I had no idea how to answer that. Oh, that’s a good question. I work in the court system, you know. I’m a part-time court usher. So I’ve seen a lot of different people come in and out. I mean, judges have a lot more power and are expected to make decisions that affect people’s lives. But I’ve never really thought about how the system works behind the scenes. It’s a bit of a mystery to most people, actually. You’ve got the judges, the magistrates, then the lawyers, and then the court staff like us. It’s all very structured, but you don’t always see the whole picture. I find it fascinating, though. I can imagine. I’ve always been interested in how the justice system works. I think it’s important for people to understand their rights and how the system is supposed to protect them. But I wonder if it’s actually doing that. That’s a huge question. I think the system is there, but it’s not perfect. I’ve seen some cases where people didn’t get the justice they deserved. It’s also very frustrating because the courts are overworked, and sometimes the process takes months or even years. I’ve heard that too. I’m thinking about taking a course in legal studies. I’m not sure if I want to go into law, but it’s just a way to understand the system better. Do you think it’s worth it? I think it’s always worth it to learn about how things work, especially something as important as the justice system. It helps you make informed decisions in your own life. Plus, you never know where it might take you. That’s true. I’ll have to keep that in mind. Thanks for the advice. I think I’m going to take the course next term. You’ll do great. And if you ever want to talk more about the system, I’m always here.

I just feel so happy today, don't you? The sun is shining, the birds are singing, and the kids are being so well-behaved. It's one of those rare days when everything just falls into place. Yeah, Mummy, I feel happy too. And I was thinking about the rhyme we learned at school. It goes, "The more you have, the more you need." But I don't think that's true, do you? I think it's not true. I think if you have lots of money, you can buy everything, but you still don't feel happy. Like, if you have a big house, you can still feel sad. That’s a very thoughtful point, sweetie. I think you’re starting to understand more about happiness than most grown-ups. But let me say this—money can make life easier, and that can bring happiness. But I don’t think it’s the only thing that brings happiness. So, is having lots of money the same as being happy? I mean, I don’t know what it’s like to have a lot of money, but I think if you have a lot, you might not need to worry about things like food or clothes. Yeah, but then you might still feel lonely. I read a story about a rich man who had everything but no friends. He was very sad because no one wanted to be around him. That’s a beautiful story, isn’t it? It shows that happiness isn’t just about money—it's about people, love, and making the most of the little things. Like, for example, when we sit together like this, laughing and talking, that’s happiness right there. I know! And when we play together, and when you read us stories. You always make us feel happy. And when you give us a hug. That’s the best part. Aww, you’re so sweet. I love you both so much. And I do believe that money can help, but it's not the key to happiness. The real key is being with the people we love and finding joy in the simple things. So, even if we don’t have a lot of money, we can still be happy? Exactly. And I think that’s the most important thing of all. That’s what makes life truly wonderful. So, let’s just keep making the most of every day, together.

So, do you think patents are really worth it? I mean, I've heard about some inventors getting millions from their ideas, but I also read that a lot of people don't get the recognition they deserve. Yeah, I guess it depends on what you're aiming for. If you want to make money and protect your idea, then patents are definitely useful. But honestly, I don't think most people go into invention just for money. It's more about solving a problem or making life easier. That makes sense. I mean, like, who wouldn't want to invent something that changes the world? But I wonder if there are still opportunities for people like us to come up with something new without being too rich or connected. I think there are. I mean, I've heard about some startups in the UK and even in China that are really pushing innovation. They’re investing a lot in tech and green energy. Maybe that's where the future is. I heard China is investing heavily in renewable energy. I mean, isn't that a big deal? I think they're building solar farms and wind turbines faster than most countries. Yeah, and they're also investing in AI and robotics. It's crazy how fast they're developing. I think the way they’re funding new ideas is different from the UK, though. They’re more about huge-scale projects and government support. That’s interesting. I wonder if we can learn from that. Like, in the UK, we're more hesitant to invest in big ideas because of the economy, right? Maybe, but I think the way the education system is set up here helps. We’re taught to think critically about innovation from a young age. I mean, I still remember my science teacher telling us that the next big invention could come from any of us. That’s encouraging to hear. I mean, if someone like me, who’s just a student, can think about future careers and inventions, maybe it's not as impossible as it seems. Exactly. We just need to keep learning and stay curious. And who knows? Maybe one day, we’ll be the ones patenting the next big thing. I hope so! Maybe we can even go into business together one day. It's not like we can't dream, right?

I can't believe we've been here for three days already. It’s been so busy with the kids and everything, I almost forgot how much fun it is to just relax and enjoy a proper lunch without worrying about anything else. I know, I felt the same. It’s been a while since we’ve all gotten together like this. I think it’s good for us to take a break from the usual routine. Yeah, I agree. I mean, it's not every day we get to be here, skiing and enjoying the mountains. But I must say, I’ve been wanting to try the ski lift again. I think I’m getting the hang of it now. You’re doing great! My brother said you were one of the fastest on the slope this morning. I didn’t know you had it in you. Oh, he said that? Well, I suppose it’s a bit easier now that I’ve got the hang of the poles. I was so nervous the first time, thinking I might fall. But the instructor was really patient with me. He should be proud. I think you’ve been working really hard. You know, I’ve been meaning to ask—have you thought about joining a ski club back home? Maybe when we get back, we can start training for next season? That’s a great idea. I’ve actually been thinking about that too. It might be fun to have a group to ski with, especially during the winter months. We could even organise a weekend trip to the mountains every now and then. I like that. We could make it a tradition. I think the kids would love it too. They’ve been talking about wanting to go skiing for ages. Well, if we can manage the time, I think it’s worth trying. I’ll start looking into some local ski clubs while we’re here. Maybe we can meet up with some of the members and plan a few trips together. That sounds like a plan. I can’t wait to see the kids get into it. It’s been so long since we’ve all been together like this, and it’s making me really appreciate the time we have.

I've been thinking a lot about how to fix those strings on the badminton rackets. I know they're always breaking, and it's a real pain. Have you considered using something like cable ties? Oh, I've thought about that too. Cable ties are great because they're strong and easy to use. But I'm not sure if they'd be the best option for all situations. If the strings are too tight or too loose, they might break more easily. Maybe we should look into the right tension and positioning. Definitely. I’ve noticed that some people use a special tool to measure the tension. It’s a bit of an investment, but I think it could save us time in the long run. What do you think about that? I agree. It might be worth it. Also, I was wondering about the cost. Do you have any idea how much it would be to get the right equipment? I think it's around £20-£30 for a decent tension meter. But I'm not sure. Maybe we could check online or ask a friend who's into this sort of thing. That sounds good. I could help with that. Oh, by the way, I was talking about the word "fleet." I think it was used in a funny way at the weekend, and I wasn't sure what it meant. Maybe you can explain it to me? Oh, right! "Fleet" can mean a group of vehicles, like a fleet of cars, or it can mean a group of people working together. I think you heard it in the context of a team. Oh, right! I was trying to use it in a business context, but I got confused. I guess I need to be more careful with my vocabulary. Don’t worry. It's easy to mix up. Speaking of vocabulary, I’ve been thinking about marketing this repair service. Have you considered putting it up on a website or social media? That's a great idea. I could set up a simple site with some photos and the service details. I bet it would get more customers. Exactly! And if we're feeling ambitious, we might even go on Dragons’ Den. Now you're talking!

Well, I've been thinkin’ about that painting I saw in the gallery in Norwich last week. It was one of those abstract ones, you know, with all the bold colours and shapes. I couldn’t tell what it was meant to represent, but it made me feel a bit strange, like it was reachin’ out to me. Yeah, I saw that too. I didn’t get it either, but I thought it was quite bold. It reminded me of that time I tried to paint a landscape and ended up with a mess of blue and green. I think I gave it to my brother. He said it looked like the sea, which I suppose it did in a way. You know, I think art is all about interpretation. Some people see a tree, others see a storm. It's like, you can't put a label on it. I teach art, so I always encourage my students to think about what they feel rather than what they see. Exactly. It's about the personal connection, isn’t it? I mean, I don’t really get into art much, but when I do, it's like a conversation with the artist. You can almost hear their thoughts in the strokes and the colour choices. I suppose that’s the beauty of it. You don’t have to understand it to enjoy it. I remember when I was younger, I used to go to the local art club. It was a bit like a social club, really. We’d talk about everything from the weather to the meaning behind the art. And you’d have about five people tryin’ to explain the same painting. It was chaotic, but fun. Sounds like the kind of place I’d have loved. My students always say they learn more from the discussions than the actual techniques. It’s surprising how much you can learn just by talking about it. I agree. I think art is like that. It brings people together, even if they don't all see the same thing. It's a way of expressing what words can't. Yeah, I think that's true. I wonder if I’ll ever get back into it. I’ve always had a soft spot for the old masters, you know, the ones with the big, bold brushstrokes. You could always start with a canvas and a brush.

I swear, I can't believe how hard it is to find a decent girl these days. They're all like, "Oh, I'm too busy working and studying to date." What's the point of dating if you’re not even going to try? Yeah, I know what you mean. I mean, I'm a mental health nurse, for God’s sake. I work 12-hour shifts and I’ve got a postgraduate degree. But every time I go out, it’s like I’m the only one who’s not grinding. It’s like everyone else has a life or something. Exactly! And it’s not just dating. I mean, look at the way people talk these days. It’s like they’ve all forgotten how to use proper English. It’s ridiculous. I had to write an email last week, and I used the word “literally” five times. What even is that word anymore? I know, right? I used to think it was just the younger generation, but now even my elderly patients use it. One of them told me, “I literally can’t believe how much I’ve changed since I was a kid.” What does that even mean? I think they’re just trying to sound more modern. But it’s just so annoying. I mean, I’m a project co-ordinator, and I have to write emails, reports, everything. I can’t afford to have typos or bad grammar. I feel you. I just got back from a shift, and I didn’t even clean the kitchen. I mean, what’s the point? I’m too tired to even think about it. I just want to collapse on the couch and watch some Netflix. I’m the same. I’ve been procrastinating for weeks. I’ve got this report that’s due tomorrow, and I haven’t even started it. I just keep telling myself, “I’ll do it tomorrow,” and then tomorrow comes and I’m still not done. I know, I know. I’ve been doing the same thing. But we’re not going to get anywhere if we keep putting it off. I think we should set a timer and just sit down and write it together. That’s a good idea. We could even make it a game or something. Maybe give each other points for getting sections done. Or maybe we can just sit there and complain about everything else instead.

I can't believe it's already 9pm. I feel like I've been sat here for hours, but I haven't even had my coffee yet. It's strange how time slips away when you're just chatting like this. It's not that strange, really. You know, I think it's because we're both creatures of habit. We always end up on the sofa at this time, talking about the day, or worse, about the things we'd rather not talk about. Exactly. And yet, we never seem to run out of things to say. I wonder how that works. I mean, I've heard people say that married life is about compromise and routine, but I think it's more like the kind of shared madness that you fall into together. I agree. I think what we have is more of a partnership than just a marriage. We both have our quirks, and we've learned to accept them. Like, for instance, I still don't understand why you can't quit smoking, even though you say it's bad for you. Oh, please, don't start. I'm trying. I've even tried the patches, and the nicotine gum, and everything. But there's something about the ritual of a cigarette in the evening. It's like a small rebellion against the day’s stress, and I can't seem to break it. I get it. I used to drink a lot, and I thought that was my way of coping too. But now I think it's more about the culture than the coping. I mean, there’s a whole generation that grew up in the smoking and drinking culture, and it’s hard to break away from it all. That makes sense. But I also think that intelligence and common sense can be at odds. Like, you might know that smoking is bad for you, but you still do it. It’s like the brain has its own logic that doesn’t match with what you know. Exactly. And that’s the thing about feminism, too. You can argue about equality all you want, but sometimes the cultural norms are so ingrained that it’s hard to change them. It’s not just about rights—it’s about changing the way people think. I go along with that. It’s like trying to convince someone that the sun rises in the east when they’ve always seen it from the west.

I just got a text from the farmer, love. He said they’ve got a new calf and they’re planning to let the kids feed it today. I think it’ll be a great opportunity for the kids to learn about animals and responsibility. Can we really feed a calf? Is it safe? I mean, I’ve never seen one up close before. I think it’s going to be fun. I’ve heard they have a special area where the kids can touch the animals. Maybe even get to feed them some grain or something. Yeah, that’s the plan. They’re hoping the kids will get hands-on experience. It’s a learning experience and also a chance to have some fun. But I do want to make sure they behave properly. I don’t want them to be too rowdy or upset the animals. I hope they don’t get scared. I’m not sure if I’d be brave enough to touch a calf. I’d be scared too! But maybe if we do it together, it’ll be easier. I can help you. That’s the spirit. I think it’s important for children to have these kinds of experiences. They’ll remember it for years to come. Speaking of remembering, I was just thinking about the school report – it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster with the children’s behaviour. Are they acting up? I heard from the school that they’ve been getting into a few little scrapes. Yeah, they’re not listening properly. I think they’re getting distracted with all the new things going on. I mean, it’s a big school now with lots of kids. I know. It’s frustrating, but I think the key is to be consistent. I’ve been trying to remind them that they need to behave well if they want to be able to do things like this farm visit. If they misbehave at school, they might not be allowed to go. It’s something I need to talk to them about later. I agree. It’s important they understand the rules. I mean, we do have to keep them safe and teach them responsibility. And don’t forget the DVDs we bought! I think we can go through them on the way to the farm. They’ll be entertained. Yes, I was thinking of that too.

I just finished a new sock, and I'm so proud of how it turned out. I think it's going to be perfect for the winter months. I’m already thinking about what I’ll do with the next pair. That’s amazing, I love how you’re getting into the rhythm of it. I’ve been trying to pick up the needles again, but I keep losing track of where I left off. Maybe I should start with something simpler, like a scarf or a hat. Yeah, hats are a good idea. They’re not as complicated as socks, and you can make them in different styles. I’ve been watching some videos online about how to do the ribbing, and it’s actually not that hard once you get the hang of it. I’ve been meaning to look into that too. I think I’ve got a few old yarns stashed away that I could use. Wait, did you know that the Olympic Games are coming up? I’ve been thinking about how the athletes train and how they handle the pressure. It’s pretty intense, isn’t it? Oh yes, I watched a documentary about the athletes preparing for the Olympics. They go through so much training, and the mental strength they have is incredible. I remember reading about a gymnast who had to deal with a lot of injuries but still managed to win gold. It’s inspiring. It really is. I think the Olympics are a great opportunity for people from all over the world to come together. It’s one of the few events where everyone is there to celebrate and compete, not to criticize or judge. Totally. It’s also surprising how much art is involved in the Olympics, especially in the opening and closing ceremonies. I was so moved by the way they incorporated traditional dances and music from different countries. Speaking of art, have you seen any good exhibitions lately? My sister mentioned there was an interesting show at the Cambridge Art Gallery about Easter traditions. I think it’s a mix of historical and contemporary pieces. I haven’t been there yet, but I’d love to. I’ve always found Easter to be a special time, not just for the religious aspects but also for the way it brings people together. The egg hunts and the family gatherings are such a big part of it.

I just got back from the Natural History Museum. That’s one of the few places I still enjoy going to. It’s got a real sense of wonder, you know? Yeah, I remember you saying that before. I’ve been meaning to go, but I’m not really into that kind of thing. I prefer the art galleries more. Though I must say, the Imax cinema in London is a different story. I took my granddad there last week, and he was absolutely amazed by the 3D effects. Oh, I’d love to see that. I’ve heard the new dinosaurs exhibit is fantastic. But I’m not sure I’d go for 3D. I always find it a bit dizzying. Although, I must admit, it does make the experience more immersive. I suppose it depends on the person. I like the way it enhances the storytelling. But then again, I’m not really into the newer tech. I’m more of a traditionalist, you know? I can see that. But then again, I’ve always been more into the educational aspects of museums. I think they’re one of the few places where you can still feel like you’re learning something. Although, I must say, the queues are longer than ever these days. Mate, I know. I was stuck in one for over an hour just to get into the main hall. It’s a real shame. I think public transport has gotten worse too. I had to take the tube to get to the museum, and it was a nightmare. I was so late, I missed the last train. Oh no, that’s terrible. I always find the tube a bit of a gamble. I walk more now, even if it takes longer. I think part of it is the fear of missing the last train. I’ve had it happen too many times. Yeah, I know exactly what you mean. I used to work in London, and I had to take the train every day. These days, I just don’t have the patience. I’m not even sure I could afford to take the tube regularly these days. That’s the thing, isn’t it? With the cost of living rising, it’s hard to justify even the most convenient routes. But I still think there’s something special about going out and seeing the world, even if it means a bit of a struggle.

So, do you reckon we're still going to have that Christmas dinner at the flat? I know it's not the same as back home, but it's better than nothing, eh? Yeah, I think we should. And maybe even some proper turkey — I’ve got a chicken in the fridge, so I can fake it a bit. Perfect. Oh, and I’ve got some old Christmas movies queued up. Maybe we can start watching them once the food is ready. I think we might need something to distract us from the madness of planning the dinner.

Alright, I’m done with my dinner. You two want anything? I’ve got some left over chip butty from last night. Oh, thank you, I’ll have a chip butty then. I’m starving. You know how it is when you work all day and then come home to nothing. Yeah, I know the feeling. But at least I’ve got my café to go back to. I mean, I’m doing this new business in Margate, and it’s not easy, but it’s worth it. Didn’t you say the reviews on Twitter have been a bit of a nightmare lately? Oh, you don’t know the half of it. One customer left a review saying my coffee was “like sludge” and another said I didn’t know what I was doing. It’s not even the worst. I had someone say my design was “influenced by a toddler’s crayon art.” Oh no! That’s brutal. I’ve had some bad reviews myself. One time, a customer said my pastries were “like cardboard and regret.” I almost cried. Wait, are you serious? Did you tell them to take it back? No, I just laughed it off. You can’t take it too seriously, right? I mean, people are just having a bad day. But honestly, it’s gotten to me. I’ve started checking my phone every time I leave the shop. I know what you mean. I’ve even started a new account just to track the reviews. It’s like this weird game now—trying to get positive reviews before the negative ones. Sounds like a lot of pressure. I mean, I’m just a student, but I still get a bit anxious about my projects. I guess we’re all worrying about what people think these days. Yeah, it’s the internet. Everyone has an opinion. Sometimes it’s just a case of bad timing or bad mood. But hey, if we can laugh about it, maybe it’s not so bad. Exactly. I mean, I’m not going to let a few bad reviews stop me. I’ve got a café to run and a dream to chase. Besides, Margate is a cool place. It’s got character, and I think that shines through in my work. Well, I’m proud of you. You’ve got guts. I mean, starting a new business is no joke, especially in a place like Margate.

I just made a new batch of raspberry jam. It’s delicious, and I think it’s going to be perfect with some fresh homemade bread and butter. I’m so glad I planted those raspberry bushes in the garden last spring. That sounds amazing, Mrs. Smith. Mom, can I have some of the jam with my toast? I’m starving after biking to school this morning. Oh, you’ve been biking all the way? That’s a long ride. Aren’t you tired? Not really! It was actually fun. I rode past the park and saw a lot of birds. I even spotted a couple of baby birds in the nest. They looked so cute. Oh, what birds were they? I’ve been trying to figure out what kind of birds are nesting in the garden. I think I’ve seen a few sparrow nests, but I’m not sure. Maybe they’re robins? I saw a robin in the garden the other day. It was sitting on some eggs. I didn’t want to scare it, so I just stood there and watched for a while. I think that might be it. They do build nests in the most unexpected places. I was even watching a gerbil run through the garden the other day. It was so cute. I’ve been trying to figure out how to get it to come out of its cage so I can name it. Can we name it after your favorite animal? I like gerbils. They're so fluffy! Yeah, I like gerbils too. They’d be a great pet. I think they’re better than a goldfish because they can run around and have fun. I agree. But I still need to find out more about them. Maybe I should do some research online. I’ve also been thinking about starting a vegetable patch. My sister-in-law said that growing your own food is much better for you. That’s true. I’ve been trying to get my toddler to eat more vegetables. I don’t know how, though. She just hates them. I always end up giving her a little bit of chocolate ice cream instead. I know the struggle. My son used to refuse veggies too. But he started eating them when I started making them into fun shapes. I even started baking them into cookies. He loved that.

I just got back from the market. I picked up some fresh veggies and a nice selection of cheeses. Did you know they’re having a sale on local produce today? It’s a bit of a hassle, but I thought it’d be worth it for the quality. Oh, really? I haven’t been to the market in ages. I’ve been relying on the shop around the corner, but I guess I should try something new. I just got my hair cut, so I’m in a bit of a mood for a change. You know, I was thinking about getting a new look too. Oh, you’ve had your hair cut? I saw you yesterday at the park, looking rather sharp. You look like you’ve been doing some shopping too. I heard you were helping out with the garden, right? Yeah, I was helping out a bit with the garden. My cousin’s got a plant that’s been dying, and I thought I’d give it a bit of attention. She’s been quite ill lately, so I figured I could do a few things for her while she’s resting. That’s very kind of you. I’ve been thinking about helping out my neighbor too. She’s been struggling with her cooking, and I remember she used to be quite good. Maybe I can bring over some meals this week? That’s a lovely idea. I’m quite old, but I still have a few skills. I used to cook quite a bit before I retired. If you need help, I’m more than happy to lend a hand. I can even make some nice dishes for you. That would be great! I’ve been wanting to try out some new recipes, and I’m not sure where to start. Maybe we can take a cooking class together? I’ve heard the local community center has some great classes. That sounds like a great idea. I’ve been meaning to get back into cooking too. I’ve been working too much lately. Maybe we can arrange a day to go together? I’d be happy to join. I’ve got a few old cookbooks that I’ve kept over the years. If we do this, I’ll bring them along. I think it’s time we all started looking after each other more. Absolutely.

Right, so we need to start weaning the baby this week, don’t we? I got the doctor’s note saying it’s time. But I’m a bit nervous. You know, it’s not like with the last one, I had so much more time to prepare. I know, I was worried too. But honestly, it’s not that bad. The baby is actually getting more interested in solid food now. She’s been watching us eat and grabbing bits of toast. It’s like she’s ready for this. That’s good to hear. I just hope she doesn’t get too fussy. I don’t want to make her hate the idea of eating. I remember how my mother used to do it – just force-feed her until she threw up. Not the best approach. Oh, I know, I remember that too. But I’m going to be gentle. Maybe start with some pureed carrots or something simple. I’ve read that it’s best to start with something bland and easy to digest. Yeah, that sounds like a good plan. And I’ve got some baby-led weaning books I can use. I thought about getting some of those jars of purees too. But I’m not sure if it’s necessary. I think it’s better to be prepared. You never know when the baby might have a reaction. Although, honestly, I also want to try baby-led weaning – let her explore the food with her hands. It feels more natural. That might be a good idea. I’ve been meaning to try that with the next baby. But for now, I think starting with a little bit of puree is safer. Speaking of which, have you thought about the weekend? Are you going to the sign language class with your friend? No, actually, I was thinking of skipping it. I’ve been so busy with the baby and the school. But maybe I should go. It’s always good to meet other people and learn something new. Yeah, I think it’s worth the time. You go, and I’ll take care of the baby. Just don’t forget to bring your notebook. I’ve got one too, and I think we can help each other out. Thanks, I’ll bring the notebook. I’ll make sure to get there on time. And maybe we can even meet up after the class for a coffee.

I just love the way the hills roll out here. You can see everything from this spot—the whole village, the fields, the old mill by the river. It's like the countryside has its own heartbeat, you know? Yeah, I agree. There's something about the quiet that really makes you think. You know, I remember when we first came here, I was so fascinated by how different it is from London. A lot of people would say it's too quiet, but I find it peaceful. Absolutely. It's not just the quiet—it's the way the light changes here. You can almost feel the seasons shifting as you walk through the fields. The way the sun catches the hills in the morning... It's like a painting. Yeah, and the people here, they have this kind of rhythm too. You can tell they’ve lived here for generations. They know the land like it’s part of their body. I think that’s why the villages feel so alive even when they’re not busy. Exactly. I mean, look at the way the farmers work with the land, and how the villagers support each other. There’s a strong sense of community here. I think that's what makes it special. It's not just about the landscape—it's about the way people live with it. I couldn’t agree more. It’s funny, though. Sometimes I think about how fast things are changing in the cities. There’s this constant rush, this need to be somewhere. But out here, time seems to slow down. You can just be. That’s the beauty of it, isn’t it? Even in a place like this, you can still feel the pulse of the world. But here, you can choose to be part of it or just observe it. It’s like you're part of the countryside itself. Maybe that’s why I feel so at home here. It's not just the views or the peace. It's the feeling of being connected—to the land, to the people, to something bigger than ourselves. Exactly. It's a rare thing, you know. To find a place where you feel like you're not just visiting, but you're part of something lasting. Yeah, and that’s why I’m so glad we chose to live here.

So, do you remember that film we watched last year? The one with the cyclist in it? I think it was called  The Rider  or something like that. Yeah, I remember that! It was really intense, wasn’t it? I mean, the way they portrayed the cyclist’s journey—it felt so real. I’ve been thinking about it ever since. It was great, but I’ve been meaning to ask you something. Why do you think so many films are about cyclists? Like, it’s not like we’re the most popular sport or anything. Or maybe it’s just the aesthetic? Hmm, that’s a good question. I think it’s the freedom aspect. You know, the way a cyclist can move through a city without the constraints of cars. It’s like they’re in their own world. I mean, the way they’re often shown in films is almost like a metaphor for independence. That’s true. I guess there’s also the idea of discipline and endurance, which makes them kind of relatable. Plus, they’re not always the main characters, which is interesting. I mean, they’re just there, moving, not necessarily trying to change the world, but still having a huge impact on it. Exactly. And I’ve been thinking about that a lot lately because my sister’s working as a cycling instructor now. She’s actually been telling me about how much the job’s changed since the pandemic. It’s not just about teaching people how to ride anymore—it’s about safety, mental health, even urban planning. Oh, really? That’s a different angle. I didn’t think about it like that. So, are there more people cycling now than before? Definitely. And the job market’s changed too. I’ve seen a lot of ads for cycle training and infrastructure projects. It’s kind of ironic that the bike, which has been around for centuries, is now at the forefront of urban mobility. It’s funny how things can shift so much. I guess we’re living in a time where sustainability is more important than ever. Maybe that’s why people are gravitating towards cycling more. Yeah, I think you’re right. And with the way things are going, I can see it becoming even more mainstream. It’s not just about exercise or getting from A to B anymore—it’s about the culture and the community.

I just love this walk we’re on. The fields are so peaceful, and the air feels different out here compared to the city. You know, I was thinking about the research I was doing last week on cash crops and how they’re changing the rural landscape. Yeah, I can imagine. I read a paper on that last year. It’s fascinating how things are shifting. But I still think there’s a charm to traditional farming, even if it’s not as profitable. Absolutely. I mean, it’s not just about the economics. There's a cultural aspect, too. The way the land is used, the way people live here—those things are part of the identity, right? Definitely. I was in Norfolk last summer, and I remember seeing these beautiful wildflower meadows. You know, they’re not just pretty; they’re important for biodiversity. I was telling my sister about it, and she said she never noticed them before. That’s the thing about the countryside, isn’t it? You have to slow down to notice details. It’s like when we’re walking—there’s this rhythm to it, this connection with nature. And the flowers, too. I’ve been trying to grow some in my garden. I’ve got these tulips and daffodils, but I’m still figuring out the best way to care for them. You don’t get much help when you’re on your own, do you? Honestly, I think it’s one of the things I miss most about the city. Being able to talk to someone about something as simple as a flower and share a bit of knowledge. I mean, we’ve got this beautiful countryside here, and I feel lucky to be part of it. I couldn’t agree more. It’s not just about the view or the fresh air. It’s about the community, the shared experience. And yeah, the football—I can’t help but think about the local team. They’ve been doing well this season. Ah, the local team! I remember the match we went to last month. It was electric. People were so passionate. It reminded me of how language and culture are tied together in these small communities. Exactly. I think that's what I love most about being in the countryside. It’s not just about the land—it’s about the people, the stories, the way we connect through it all.

Alright, so I just got an email about the flat we were looking at in Newcastle. Let me read it out... It says they've got a viewing scheduled for next Tuesday. I need to check if you're free then. Yeah, I’m free as long as it doesn’t clash with my engineering project meeting. I can shift it if needed. But I’m really keen to see that place. The flat with the garden? I think that's the one. Yep, that's the one. The agent mentioned it's in a quiet area, close to the Angel of the North. You know, the big statue. I've always wanted to go there, but the last time I was up there, the car park was a nightmare. I remember getting stuck in a queue for over an hour. Oh, I heard about that. They said the parking situation is getting worse every year. Maybe we should consider getting a parking permit? I mean, if we're thinking about moving there, it's worth investing in some kind of solution. That’s a good point. I know a few people who have gone down that route. I'll keep an eye out for any info on that. Speaking of which, have you got the keys to the car? I was going to take it to the garage this weekend for a service, but I need to check the oil levels first. Yep, they’re in the glove compartment. I already checked the oil and it's fine. But I did notice the tire pressure on the rear left is a bit low. Maybe we should top that up before the viewing? I don’t want to get pulled over on the A1. Definitely. I’ll pick up some air pressure stuff on the way. Also, did you get the tickets for the football match next week? I was thinking of going to the match with the lads to celebrate the viewing. Yeah, I got them. It's that Newcastle team, right? I'm told it's going to be a tough game, but I’m looking forward to it. It's been a while since I’ve seen a game live. That’s the spirit. Let’s make it a memorable day. I’ll bring the snacks and the drinks. Just go easy on the cheering, though. I don’t want to end up with a head injury from the crowd.

I just saw a documentary about the trial of a famous actor who was accused of animal cruelty. It was so shocking, really. I mean, how could someone do that to a dog? I've always thought celebrities should be held to higher standards. I bet you're right. But then again, they’re just people, like the rest of us. I mean, if someone had a bad day and snapped, who’s to say they wouldn’t do something like that? Still, I can't believe it. Oh, I was watching the same thing last night. It was upsetting, but I think it’s a good reminder that even people in the public eye can have dark sides. But you know, I’m more interested in the wildlife stuff you two were talking about earlier. Oh, right! I was telling her about the geese that come down to the river every winter. They’re such a sight, aren’t they? I mean, they just waddle around and make all that noise, but they’re so graceful when they fly. Yeah, I’ve seen them too. I get up early and take my coffee out by the river sometimes. It’s peaceful. I love watching them. They’re like little celebrities of the water, aren’t they? Oh, they’re not just any geese, though. I remember once seeing a family of them with little ones. The parents would fly off and come back with food, and the babies would just waddle after them. It was so sweet. That sounds like a classic wildlife moment. I think it’s the migration that’s so fascinating. It’s like they know something we don’t. They just trust their instincts, you know? Exactly. And the fact that they come all the way from the north, right? I mean, I’ve heard stories about how they travel thousands of miles just to find their winter home. It’s incredible. Yes, it’s a reminder of how nature is full of wonders. I don’t know how people can focus on celebrities and their trials when there’s so much to learn from the world around us. Maybe we should take a walk by the river sometime. I’d love to see them for myself. That sounds like a great idea. I’d love to take you both. It’s always nice to appreciate the simple things.

I can't believe it's already April. I feel like we just had the spring equinox yesterday. Have you seen the weather lately? It's been so unpredictable. I know, right? One minute it's sunbathing and the next, it's rain and sleet. I was trying to take the kids to the park this morning, but the forecast said heavy rain. I ended up just staying home with a cup of tea and a book. That sounds like a good plan. I think I'd rather read than be caught in the rain. By the way, how's the baby doing? I heard you're expecting again soon. Oh, it's still a bit early, but the doctor said everything's looking good. The last scan was a bit of a rollercoaster, but I think we're in the clear. I just hope I can keep up with the two kids and the housework. That’s no small task. I remember when I had my first child, I thought I was going to collapse from exhaustion. But you're doing great. I'm just hoping I can survive my upcoming job interview next week. You'll be fine. You've always been so prepared. I remember when you asked me for advice about interviews. You were so nervous, but you held your own. I still think you should have taken the head of department position last year. I know, I know. I was scared of the responsibility. But I just couldn't shake the feeling that I wasn’t ready. I'm not sure I ever will be, honestly. Also, I've been having these strange dreams about being interviewed in front of a panel of people who all have about five heads each. Oh, come on, you're overthinking it. Just remember, you've been teaching for years. You handle the classroom like a pro. Why not bring that confidence into the interview? I know, I know. I'll try. It's just that the whole thing feels so high stakes. I can't help but think about how much I'm going to miss the kids if I get the job. Well, if you do, I'll be here to help you with the baby and the housework. Just remember, I'm your partner in crime, even if I am still getting the hang of being a full-time mother.

So, do you ever think about what’s next? I mean, like, after uni, after work, like... what’s beyond all this? I think about it all the time, honestly. I mean, I’m in admin, and I know it’s not the dream job, but it’s stable. Still, I feel like I’m just... waiting for something bigger to happen. I know what you mean. I’m in production control, and it’s not exactly glamorous, but it’s a good job. Still, sometimes I wonder if I’m settling. Like, what if I had gone into something else? Yeah, I get that. I’ve always wanted to work in the arts, but my parents pushed me to go into something more... practical. I guess they wanted me to be safe. I can totally relate. My parents are similar. I mean, I love what I do, but sometimes I wonder if I could be doing something more creative. You know, like working in a museum or something? I’d love that. I used to volunteer at a local gallery, and it was so inspiring. But I think I’m too scared to take the leap. What if I fail? What if I can’t afford to take a break? I think that’s the thing, isn’t it? Fear of failure. It’s so easy to get stuck in a routine, even if you’re not happy. But maybe we should try to make a plan. Like, a small step toward something new. That sounds good. I mean, I’m not sure what I’d do, but maybe I could take a short course or something. Or maybe just start talking to people in the industry. Yeah, that’s a start. I mean, it’s not like we’re not capable. We both have postgrad degrees, for crying out loud. We’ve got the skills. We just need a chance to use them. Exactly. I think I’m going to start looking into some courses next month. Maybe something online? It’s a way to keep my skills sharp without committing to a full-time job. That’s brilliant. I should do the same. Maybe I could even start writing or something. You know, in my spare time. It’s not like I can’t afford to try. Yeah, and if it doesn’t work out, we can always fall back on what we have.

I swear, I don’t know how you do it, Lottie. I’m just so annoyed with Josh lately. He’s been with this girl from the café, and I can’t even tell if he’s serious or not. Oh, I know what you mean, Jess. I’ve been so jealous of Maisie’s new boyfriend. He’s got that whole “I’m not your type” vibe, but he’s always giving her that look when she’s not looking. It’s so annoying. You know, I was just thinking about this the other day. It’s funny how people think they’re not your type, but then they end up being the one you end up with. Honestly, I’m still trying to figure out if Marco is serious or not. One day he’s saying he’s not into relationships, and the next day he’s asking me out to dinner. Yeah, I get that. But it’s just so frustrating when you’re in a relationship and the other person is flirtin’ with someone else. I mean, I’ve been with Sam for like three months, and he’s always talking about his mates and their girlfriends. Sometimes I think he’s just trying to impress them, not me. I feel that. I’m with Tom now, and he’s always on his phone, messing around with his apps. I don’t know if he’s actually seeing someone or if he’s just playing it cool. I’m so confused. Honestly, I think it’s just part of being young. You don’t know what you want, and you’re scared to commit. I mean, I’m still figuring things out myself. I’m with Marco, but I’m not sure if I’m ready for a real relationship. I just want to have fun and see where it goes. I guess. But I don’t wanna be the one to sit around, waiting for someone to take the first step. I mean, if they’re not into relationships, then why are they even with me? I know, right? It’s like you’re holding your breath, waiting for them to decide. And when they don’t, you feel like you’re the one who’s lost. Exactly. I think the key is to talk about it. If you’re in a relationship, you should be open about your feelings.

Alright, let’s see—what’s for dinner? I’ve got the chicken and mash, and I think I’ve got the veg sorted too. That sounds good, Mum. Can I have some more mash? I’m still hungry from the hockey match today. Of course, but try to eat slower. You’re getting bigger, and if you don’t watch your portions, you’ll be like your dad. I’m not that big, you know. I’m just built like that. And I don’t eat that much. You’re just like your mother when she was your age. She used to eat the whole plate and still have room for seconds. Yeah, but I think I’m going to be like Dad. I’m already getting pretty big. Well, you’ll be fine. Just make sure you’re active. You’ve got to keep up with the hockey. Speaking of hockey, I’m thinking about joining the team again next season. I’ve been practicing a lot with my mates. That’s great. You’ve got a good shot. I remember when you were still in primary school and you scored that goal against St. Mary’s. You were like a little rocket. Yeah, I was pretty good back then. I still think I could be better if I trained more. You’ve got the talent, but you need the discipline. I remember when I was your age, I used to play every day. Even in the winter, I’d get up early and go to the field. So, what about the trip to France next month? Are we still going? Yes, we are. I’ve got the tickets and everything. It’s going to be a great opportunity for you to see Europe and get some travel experience. That’s a good idea. I think you should take the kids. It’s a chance for them to see the world while they’re still young. I’d love to go. I’ve never been to France. I’ve heard it’s amazing. I’m excited. I’ve been looking up some stuff online about Paris. I think I want to go to the Eiffel Tower. Well, if you promise to behave, I won’t say no. But you’ll have to keep up with the rest of us. Deal! I’ll be the best behaved kid on the trip.

I can't believe we've been on the road for six hours already. I thought it would take less time to get to the Redwoods. Have you seen how much traffic there is? I know, it's crazy. I thought this would be a scenic drive, not like a rush hour in London. I mean, I've been stuck in rush hour in London before, but this is different. It's like the whole state is trying to get to the same spot. It's not just the traffic. We've had to stop twice for roadside emergencies. First, a flat tire on the way out, then a bear crossing the road—literally! We had to pull over and wait for it to cross. Oh my God, a bear? That’s insane! I didn’t think bears were that common in California. I mean, I know they're in the Redwoods, but I didn’t expect to see one on the highway. What did you do? Did you take a photo? No way! I was too scared to even take my phone out. I just sat there and waited, hoping it would cross quickly. It did, eventually. But I still don’t know how it got there. I mean, are they really that bold? I don’t know. Maybe they’re just trying to get to the nearest Starbucks. Honestly, the animals here are wilder than the people. I've seen more squirrels in the car than people on the road. That’s true. I think the only thing more chaotic than the traffic is the wildlife. But at least it's a unique experience. I mean, most people don’t get to see a bear on a highway. I’m just glad we’re not the ones who got stuck in the middle of it. Yeah, I guess. I mean, it’s kind of an adventure. I just hope we make it to the guesthouse before it gets dark. I’m not looking forward to another sleepless night on the road. Me neither. I think I’ve had enough road trips for one lifetime. But hey, if we make it, we can finally enjoy the Redwoods without the stress of the road. Let’s just hope the next stretch is smoother. Agree. Let’s just keep going. Maybe the bears will leave us alone after this. Or maybe we’ll just keep running into them.

Alright, lads, what’s for dinner? I’m in the mood for something hearty, and I’ve got chicken kievs in the fridge! You always go for the same thing, Dad! You know, the last time we had chicken kievs, you said it was the best meal you’d ever had. And it was! But this time, I’ve got a new twist. I’ve added some garlic and fresh herbs. I think it’s gonna be a real treat. Yeah, but I still think you’re the only one who’d ever make chicken kievs. I mean, who even  has  that recipe? You’re joking, aren’t you? It’s a classic. And it’s been passed down through the family. I mean, my grandma used to make them every Sunday. Yeah, and she also said she was the best cook in the world. I still remember the time she burned the toast and called it “charred perfection.” That was  my  toast. I was just a baby then, but I remember the smoke. I think I still have the scars. You’re not the only one. I still remember the time I tried to make them and ended up with a fire in the kitchen. You had to call the fire brigade. You were  so  embarrassed. I remember you blaming it on the chicken. I blame the chicken? I blame the  heat ! You know, we’re going to visit Granny later. Should we take the chicken kievs? Yeah, she loves them. And I think she still has that little oven she used to make them in. Perfect. We’ll take them over. And if we can’t get her to try a new recipe, we’ll just stick with the kievs. Sounds good. I just hope she doesn’t try to make them again. If she does, I’m out. I’ve had enough of burnt chicken. Alright, let’s get the food out. We’ve got a rugby match on later, so we need to eat before that. Oh, the match is on? I thought it was on Friday. I told you last week, it's on Saturday. You didn’t listen. I think I’ll stay home and watch the kids. I’ve got a headache. You sure? You’ve been eating too many biscuits. And I’ve been eating too many biscuits. You two are the same.

I just received the vintage cups and saucers from eBay. They’re absolutely beautiful—those floral patterns are so retro, don’t you think? Oh, they look amazing! I’d love to see them in person. You know I’ve always had a soft spot for things like that. They must have been from the 60s or 70s? Yeah, I think so. The listing said they were from the 1970s, and the condition is spotless. I can’t believe they were still for sale. I’ve been looking for a set like that for ages. That’s great. I’d love to have a few sets like that in my kitchen. They really add character. I’m thinking of starting a little collection myself, just for the nostalgia. I think you’d be perfect for that. You’re always so particular about things. Speaking of which, I’ve been thinking about the local community market this weekend. It’s not too late to go, is it? Yeah, it’s still on. I’ve got a few things I want to check out—maybe some handmade bread? I saw someone selling buckwheat bread, and it looked really good. I’ve been meaning to try it. Oh, I love buckwheat bread. It’s so healthy and has this amazing nutty flavor. I’ve been making it at home lately, but I’m not sure how I’d manage the baking process. Maybe I should get some tips from the market. You should definitely go. It’s a great way to support local producers and find some unique stuff. I might even bring a few cups and saucers from your collection to the market. You know, to show off. That sounds like a plan. I’ll make sure to have a few extra sets ready to display. It’s always fun to share things with others. Oh, and I’m thinking of organizing a small work leaving do for Sarah. Do you have any ideas? I could help with that. Why don’t we host it at the community center? It’s a great space and we’ve got enough people who would be interested in attending. That sounds good. I’ll reach out to Sarah and let her know. I think it’ll be a great way to celebrate her work and give everyone a chance to say goodbye properly. Exactly. I can’t wait to see everyone there.

I just got a text from my cousin, he's in France too. He said he's been working in banking, but he's been getting some weird calls about money laundering. I asked him what he meant, and he just said, “You wouldn’t believe the fines they’re throwing at us.” I know what you mean. I’ve got a cousin who’s a bank manager in London. He’s been telling me about all these new regulations. They’re cracking down on money laundering like it’s a terrorist act. It’s a nightmare, honestly. Every time he tries to process a transaction, he has to check a hundred different things. I don’t get it. I mean, I’ve heard about that stuff on the news, but I thought it was more about big corporations or something. You’d think the banks would be the ones who know what they’re doing. But if you’re a small business owner, like my dad, he’s got to deal with all this paperwork just to open an account. Exactly. My brother-in-law runs a small shop, and he’s had to do all sorts of things just to keep his business legit. You’ve got to file all these forms and get approvals, and still, there’s a chance they’ll say no. I was telling him last week that if the government’s not careful, they’re going to drive all the small businesses out of the country. Yeah, I hear that too. And it’s not just the paperwork. I’ve heard someone got fined for something they didn’t even know was a crime. One of my friends got caught up in it by accident. He was just trying to send money to his cousin in Romania, and they started asking questions about where the money came from. Turns out, it was all because of some random document he signed. That’s the thing. It’s not just about the laws; it’s about the way the system is set up. If you’re not careful, you could end up in a lot of trouble. I was trying to explain this to my sister when she started talking about her kids. She’s got a little one, and she’s worried about what kind of careers they’ll have. She says she doesn’t want them to end up in anything like that.

I just can’t believe how cold it’s been this week. I’ve had to wear my thick coat even inside the house, and it’s still not enough. Yeah, I know what you mean. It’s been quite a shock after the warm summer we had. I think it’s the early autumn wind that’s making it feel so much colder than it actually is. It’s not just the wind, though. I’ve noticed that the mornings are especially frosty. I had to put on my boots and a hat just to walk the dog outside this morning. I totally agree. My baby brother is still getting used to the cold. I’ve been thinking about taking up a new hobby. Do you have any recommendations? Well, I used to enjoy gardening. It’s a great way to unwind and get some fresh air. I haven’t done it much since I retired, but I still have a few plants in the garden. Maybe you could try that. It’s not too difficult, and you can do it at your own pace. That sounds like a great idea.

So, did you get anything for Valentine’s Day? I mean, I know it’s not like it’s a big deal or anything, but I still like to do something. Honestly, I just got a card and a chocolate from my mum. But you know what’s better? My flatmate bought me a movie night date with popcorn and all. We watched  La La Land  and it was like a real date, even if we were just two people in a flat. Oh, that’s nice! I was going to do something like that, but then I got stuck in the library all day because of this essay. I’m still not done. You’re such a procrastinator, Liza. I told you to start earlier. But hey, I get it—Valentine’s Day is basically just a reason to be lazy and eat chocolate, right? Exactly! And then I thought about going out to a restaurant, but the only place that wasn’t full was that weird vegan place near the campus. I’m not sure I want to eat a burger made of mushrooms. I know, right? I tried that once and ended up with a stomach ache. But I did get a proper date last week, just me and my friend Sam. We went to that cinema near the train station. Oh, you went out? You never go out! You’re always stuck in your flat with your cat, doing random stuff. Well, I had a friend who wanted to go out, and I thought, “Why not?” So we went to this new cinema. The movie was  Everything Everywhere All At Once  and I cried like a baby. No way! You’re not that emotional. Maybe you just need to be reminded that you’re not the only person in the world who’s ever been confused by the universe. Exactly! And that’s why I think the cinema is a great place to go. It’s like, you can cry and nobody judges you. Well, maybe I should go out with someone this weekend. I mean, the weekend is coming, and Valentine’s Day was just the start. Yeah, and if you don’t, you’ll be stuck eating ramen and watching bad movies, like me. Deal. But I’m getting a proper date, not just a flatmate. Girl, you’re going to regret that. But I’ll be here to laugh at you when you’re crying over a bad movie.

So, do you think the housing crisis is just a symptom of capitalism or is it something deeper? I mean, I’ve been trying to buy a place for years, and I can’t even afford a deposit. I think it’s a bit of both. Capitalism creates this race to own property, and then the system is structured to keep people like us out. Plus, there's all the racism in housing policies that have been going on for decades. It’s not just about money—it’s about who gets to live where. Yeah, and it’s not just about the price. You have to consider the location, the size, the condition. I mean, I’m an architect, so I know the value of good design, but I also know how hard it is to find a place that makes sense for a single person, let alone a couple. It’s so frustrating. I’m a freelancer, so I don’t have the security of a stable income. And yet, I’m expected to plan my life around the housing market. I mean, why should someone who works from home and doesn’t have a mortgage be treated any differently? Exactly! It’s like the system is designed to keep people in a cycle of debt and insecurity. And it’s not just about money. It’s about power. Who controls the housing market? Who gets to decide where people can live? I think it’s also about racism. I’ve heard stories from friends who are from ethnic minorities and have been told they can’t get a mortgage because of their background. That’s not fair. It’s not just about economics—it’s about exclusion and control. I agree. But there’s also a lot of political will to ignore the issue. I mean, we had this recent referendum on housing, and it was all about building more homes. But where are the homes? They’re still not built, and the prices keep going up. And it’s not just about building more. It’s about regulating the market. We need to stop allowing private landlords to exploit people who are already in vulnerable positions. I think the system is broken, and it’s not going to fix itself. I hope you’re right. I’m tired of feeling like my life is on hold because I can’t afford a place to live.

I just got a call from the nursery. They've confirmed the start date for the baby, and it's all set. I’m relieved, honestly. I’m so ready to get back to work, but I’m also nervous about how it will go. Yeah, I can totally imagine how you feel. I mean, I’ve been dreading the moment you leave the house for more than eight hours, but I also know it’s necessary. How are you planning to manage the weaning? Honestly, it’s going to be tough. I’ve been trying to get the baby used to the bottle, but he’s been really clingy. I keep thinking, “What if he doesn’t take to it?” But the nursery said they have a weaning program they can help with. Maybe I should look into that. I think that’s a good idea. I mean, I know you’re not the only one feeling this way. My mum has been through the same thing with me. She used to say, “It’s not the end of the world, it’s just a new beginning.” Maybe you should try to keep that in mind. You’re right. It’s just a new beginning. I’ve been thinking about holidays too. We’ve been planning a trip to France for next summer. I hope we can take the baby with us, but I know it’s not going to be easy. You know what? I think you should do it. There’s no point in putting it off. I mean, you can always take the baby for a short trip, like a weekend away, and see how it goes. But France sounds amazing – I’d love to go there with you. That would be lovely. But I still need to sort out the nursery stuff first. I’ve also been thinking about the TV. I haven’t watched any for weeks; it’s been so much work with the baby. Do you think I should start watching something? Maybe a show I used to enjoy? I think that’s a great idea. You need to take some time for yourself. Even if it’s just an episode of your favorite show, it’ll do you good. And maybe you can set a time for it, like after the baby naps. That way, you can enjoy your own time again.

I can't believe it's already Friday. I feel like we've had a week of non-stop work. I had to give a statement to the police this morning about that incident at the office. Oh no, really? I hope it wasn't anything too serious. You've been under a lot of pressure lately. Yeah, I know what you mean. I had to deal with a few issues at the store last week too. I’m so glad we're all getting a break this weekend. I heard about the police statement. Did they ask you anything specific? I’m just curious, even though I know it’s not my place to pry. They asked about the timeline, who was there, and what exactly happened. It was pretty stressful, but I think I managed to keep my composure. That’s admirable. I think it must have been a bit of a shock. I had to give a statement once, and it was a nightmare. They didn’t take notes, and I had to repeat myself three times. That sounds awful. I would have been so flustered. I still get nervous when I have to talk to people in authority. I can imagine. I had to give a presentation to a board of directors last month, and I was so nervous I almost choked. You’re not alone in that. I used to be terrified of public speaking. But I guess with the job I have, you learn to adapt. I think it’s about managing your nerves. I’ve started practicing with my colleagues before meetings. It helps. I’m going to try that. I’m having a meeting with the store manager next week, and I really want to make an impression. That’s a great idea. And, speaking of meetings, have you got your EE phone bill sorted yet? I noticed you haven’t paid it for a while. Oh, right! I’ve been so busy with work and the police statement that I completely forgot. I’ll sort it out this weekend. Yeah, that’s a good plan. You know, I’ve been thinking about upgrading my phone. It’s about time I got a better one. I’m actually thinking about buying a new one too. I can’t stand my current one. It’s so slow. I can relate. I had to replace mine last month.

So, how’s the new life treating you, mate? You’ve been married now for a few months, right? Yeah, it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster. She’s a lovely person, but I can’t believe I’m calling her “wife.” Still getting used to the idea. I can imagine. I remember when I got engaged, I was so nervous I forgot my ring at the venue. Not the best start. Oh, you were joking, weren’t you? You never said anything about that. Didn’t even mention it. I didn’t want to sound like a complete disaster. Anyway, how’s the flat? Still got that old mortar and pestle from your mum? Oh, you know her, always had the odd spice or herb in the cupboard. She even gave me some chickpeas to grind for the curry. I still haven’t figured out how to use them properly. I know the feeling. I’ve got this old bread mill from my gran. It’s still in working order, but I haven’t had the chance to use it since I moved out. Maybe I should try making some whole grain bread. You should. I tried making it once, but the dough was too dry. I ended up with a rock, not bread. Still, it’s better than nothing. Speaking of bread, did you know that the Romans used a similar type of grain for their bread? I was reading about it the other day. They even had different types depending on the region. Interesting. I always thought the Roman Empire was more about war and emperors. You know, about the Legions and all that. Well, they had a lot of cultural stuff going on too. They had their own version of TV shows, kind of. Like the  Spartacus  series. It was based on real events, but they added some drama to it. Oh man, I watched that. I loved the way they portrayed the gladiators. It was intense. Although, I always wondered why they had such a high rate of early deaths in the series. You’re not the only one. They probably added that for effect. But it was a pretty accurate portrayal of what life was like back then. Definitely. Anyway, I should get back to work. Got some herbs to grind and a few nuts to crack. Maybe I’ll start making some hummus for the weekend.

Hey, do you remember that time we tried out for the school orchestra last week? I mean, it was like a total disaster. I was so nervous I almost forgot the flute part! Oh, come on, you were amazing! I mean, you played the flute perfectly. But then again, I was in the brass section, so I didn’t really notice anything else. Yeah, I guess that’s true. But I still got a bit nervous when Miss Thompson said, “We’ll be starting rehearsal tomorrow.” I mean, I don’t even know if I’m cut out for this. You’re definitely cut out for it. I mean, you’ve been practising every night. And besides, you know how much I love music. We’re going to be the best band in the school, I’m sure of it. I hope so, but I’m still worried about our English test. I don’t think I studied enough for it. What about you? Honestly, I’m kind of stressed too. I had to do that French lesson today, and the teacher was so strict. She even made us write a paragraph about our summer holidays in French. I got so confused with the verbs. Yeah, I remember that. I tried to remember the past tense of “to go,” and I messed it up completely. I said, “I was gone,” and the teacher looked at me like I was from Mars. That’s what I said! I think she thought I was trying to be funny. But I got a point taken off for that. I’m so bad at French. I wish we had more art lessons instead. At least then I wouldn’t have to deal with all these languages. I know, right? I love art. I mean, I painted this amazing portrait of our teacher last week. She even said it was really good. But I still have to go to all these English and French lessons. Yeah, but it’s all part of the school experience, right? Besides, the school orchestra is going to be awesome. I mean, we’ll be playing together and maybe even performing at the end of the year. I hope so. I just need to get over my nerves. Maybe I’ll try to practice more today. What about you? I’ll try. But I’m still worried about the English test.

Oh, it’s been a bit of a wet start to the week, hasn’t it? I was just thinking how the sky’s so grey, like it’s holding its breath. Yeah, honestly, I’ve been kind of stuck in this grey mood too. I mean, it’s not just the weather, is it? I’ve got this test coming up next week, and I’ve been studying so much that I’ve lost all sense of direction. Like, I can’t even find my way to the library without getting lost. You know, I used to get lost even more back when I was a teacher. I’d go to the staff room and end up in the art department by mistake. The kids would just laugh and say, “Mrs. Smith, you’re in the wrong building!” Oh, I remember when I was still teaching. You always had to be careful with the accents, though. I remember one day, a boy came in with this really strong Yorkshire accent, and I thought he was from Manchester or something, but it turned out he was from Newcastle. I’ve got a friend from Newcastle, and he speaks like that. He’s been telling me about how the dialects can be so different, even within the same county. Like, if you’re from York, you don’t sound like someone from Hull. Exactly! I used to live in Hull, and someone once asked me, “Are you from Hull or Leeds?” and I said, “Neither—just from the Yorkshire coast!” And they looked at me like I was from Mars. I remember that. It’s all about the way you speak, isn’t it? It can tell you so much about where you’re from. I mean, if you’re from Darlington, you say ‘’t’’ for ‘’th’’ a lot. It’s like a badge of honour. Yeah, I can hear that. I’ve noticed it when I’m on the bus or in the park with people from the North. It’s like a different language, but it’s also a way of connecting. Oh, go on then, tell me about your test. Any chance you’re going to pass it? I’d hate to see you fail because of something like that. I’ll pass. I have to. I’m doing it for my future, and I’ve got a scholarship waiting for me if I do.

I just had the most frustrating drive today. I was going to meet someone in Norwich, and I got stuck in traffic for over an hour. It was like the whole city was on strike or something. You know, I’ve had worse. I once got stuck in a queue on the A12 for two hours because a lorry broke down. I ended up missing my wife's birthday dinner. But I didn’t have a choice; I had to go. Oh, you had to go? I wouldn’t have missed my own birthday for anything. Even if it meant getting stuck in traffic. I like to think of myself as a bit of a rebel, you know? That’s the spirit. I think we all have our own ways of dealing with stress. I, for one, try to avoid stress by doing things like jigsaws. It’s surprisingly calming. I used to do puzzles when I was a kid, but I haven’t touched one in years. I guess I got too busy with work and life. Although, I have to say, I feel like I should get back into it. Maybe it’ll help with my mind. I’ve always thought puzzles are good for the brain. My wife used to do crosswords every night. She was amazing at it. But I could never get the hang of it. I prefer something more physical, like fixing cars. You know what I find interesting? I’ve been thinking about genes lately. My mom always said I’d end up like her—always avoiding work and looking for a way out. But I don’t think it’s all in our genes. I think it’s more about the environment and the people we grow up with. Interesting. I’ve had a few conversations about genes and obesity. It seems like there are some connections, but it’s not as simple as just having the genes. Lifestyle plays a huge role too. Exactly. I think we all have a mix of both nature and nurture. I’ve always been a bit of a skeptic when it comes to religion, but I have to say, sometimes it’s nice to have a little bit of faith in things beyond ourselves. I’m more of a practical person. I believe in the science of it all. But I also think there’s something to be said for a little bit of luck.

I just got a new email from the department head about Moodle. It’s about updating our course materials. Honestly, I’m so fed up with the system now. It’s been giving me trouble for weeks. Yeah, I know. I tried to upload a lecture recording last week, and it just kept crashing. I ended up having to send it as an attachment, which is so inconvenient. What’s the deal with Moodle? I thought it was supposed to be a better learning platform. I agree. It’s supposed to be user-friendly, but honestly, it feels like it was designed by someone who’s never actually used it. I’ve been trying to get the IT department to help, but they’re always busy with other things. I tried that too. I sent them an email two weeks ago, and I haven’t even heard back. It’s like they’ve forgotten about it. I’m starting to think we should just switch to a different LMS. Maybe Canvas or something? I’ve been thinking about that too. I mean, I know Moodle is the standard here, but I can’t be the only one who’s had issues. I’ve heard from other lecturers as well. It’s just so frustrating when you’re in the middle of a lecture and the system crashes. Exactly. It’s not just the technical problems, though. It’s also the way the interface feels outdated. I remember when we first started using it, it was modern and intuitive. But now, it feels like it’s been left to rot. I’d love to see a proper upgrade. But I guess with the university’s budget situation, they’re not prioritizing things like this. I mean, I know it’s a lot to ask, but maybe we should all write to the heads of department and demand some action. That’s a good idea. Maybe we can pool our resources and send a collective email. I’m sure the more people who speak up, the better chance we have of getting some attention. Yeah, and if we can’t get Moodle to work, maybe we can push for a trial with another platform. I mean, we’re in the tech field, so we should be able to go with something more reliable. Agreed. I’ll start drafting the email tonight. Let’s make sure we’re all on the same page.

I can't believe how much jetlag I'm still feeling. I swear, I think I’ve been asleep for three hours and I’m already starting to feel like I’ve been awake all day. You’re not the only one. I’ve been lying in bed for the past two hours trying to convince myself that it’s actually morning. I think my brain just refuses to accept that we’ve been over here for a week now. Yeah, I know, right? It’s like we’ve been pulled into some kind of time warp. I keep checking the clock, thinking maybe the time has changed or something. But no, it’s just us. I was thinking the other day about how weird it is that we’re both lecturers. You’d think we’d be more used to dealing with time zones. But no, I think jetlag is just one of those things that hits you harder when you’re tired and trying to adapt to a new environment. Exactly. And it’s not just the jetlag, it’s the babies. I swear, they’ve been keeping us up all night. Last night, Lucy was up three times, and then the baby started crying. I think we’ve lost more sleep in the past week than we did in the entire first year of our relationship. I know, I know. I’ve been trying to stay up late to get some work done, but every time I do, the baby starts wailing. It’s like they’re trying to teach us a lesson. Maybe they’re trying to tell us that we need to slow down and take it easy. I think they’ve got a point. I mean, we are both lecturers, and we’re both trying to juggle our careers and our family life. It’s a lot. But I think we are doing okay. At least we have each other to talk to about all of this. Yeah, I think we are. And I think we’re going to be fine. But I do miss the days when we didn’t have to worry about babies and jetlag. Those were the days of just lying in bed and talking about our lives. I do too. But I think we are learning to adapt. And I think the baby is going to grow up to be a wonderful child.

I've been thinking a lot about friends lately. It's strange how some of them have moved across the world and yet we still keep in touch. You know, like that guy from Cairo, he's been living in London for years now, but we still have those weekly chats. Yeah, it's fascinating how the internet has made it so much easier to stay connected. I mean, I've been working with people from all over the world, and it's amazing how time zones don't really matter anymore. But you know, it's also tough to keep up with the whole visa process when you're trying to visit friends. Exactly. I've been trying to get a visa to visit my cousin in Jordan. It's a bit of a headache, honestly. The forms are so detailed, and the requirements seem to change every month. Have you ever gone through that? Oh, you bet. I had to get a visa for Iraq a few months back. The process was a nightmare. They asked for so many documents, and I had to get a letter from my employer, which was a bit of an ordeal. But I managed, and I actually got a visa. That sounds like a relief. I’ve also been watching the news about the political situation in the Middle East. It's a bit scary, especially with all the oil politics. Do you think the region is ever going to stabilize? I don’t know. There's a lot of instability, and the oil politics only make it worse. I mean, the way things are now, it's like a never-ending cycle. But I do think young people are starting to push for change. They're more aware of their rights and are not afraid to speak up. That's true. I've seen some of my friends in the UK starting to get involved in political discussions, especially about the Middle East. It's a bit complicated, though. You have to be careful what you say, especially if you're not from there. Definitely. I've had to be careful with my translations too. There are certain words that can be misinterpreted, especially when it comes to religious topics like Wahabi. It's a tricky area, you know? I can imagine. I’ve been trying to get my own house sorted out too.

I just had to say, that roast lamb was  excellent —you know, it’s rare to get a proper, juicy lamb these days. I’m so glad we got it from the local butcher, not one of those fancy supermarkets. Yeah, it was top-notch. And I’ve been thinking—should we maybe try that Scottish tablet you mentioned? I reckon it might be a good idea for a holiday. A bit of a change of scenery from all this routine. Oh, you’re talking about the one with the loch and the castle? I’d be  thrilled  to go on a cruise, even if it’s just for a week. It’s been ages since we had a proper holiday. Though I must say, I’m not sure I’d be able to keep up with the pace of a cruise ship. I’m more of a ‘staycation’ person. Ha! I can imagine you pacing around a cruise ship, trying to find the nearest staircase. But seriously, we should consider it. I’ve been thinking about getting back into fitness, too. I do a bit of gym work, but not enough. I need to get back into shape for the long haul. That’s a good idea. I’ve been meaning to start again too. Though I’m not sure I want to deal with the noise of the gym again. Maybe we could try some home workouts? There are all sorts of online classes now. Oh, I’ve been doing yoga at home. It’s very calming. And it’s good for the body, too. I think you’d enjoy it. Plus, I’ve got a new dog—I call him Biscuit. He’s a small terrier, and he’s brought a bit of joy into the house.
