Not to mention the chaos. Biscuit? That’s a lovely name. I bet he’s a handful. I’ve got a neighbor’s dog who’s a bit of a menace, but the kids love him. Speaking of dogs, have you tried getting a pet yet? I think it would be good for the house. We’ve been thinking about it, actually. But with the rented accommodation, it’s a bit of a concern. Landlords can be picky about pets. But I think it’s worth it. You know, having a companion. You know, I’ve always said that a dog can make a home feel like a home.

Alright, I’m starving. Have any of you eaten yet? I’ve been staring at this fridge like it’s got some secrets. I’m more worried about when we’re going to eat than what we’re eating. I’ve been waiting for someone to cook something for days. You know how it is, right? Yeah, I feel you. I’ve basically been surviving on toast and a can of soup. I think I’m starting to get a bit of a taste for it now. You can’t be serious. You can’t survive on that. You’re going to need more than that when you get to uni, and I know you’re planning on going. Oh, I’m still not sure. I mean, I’ve got the grades, but I’m not sure if I’m ready for the whole university thing. I’m thinking of staying here a bit longer. Maybe get some more work experience or something. Yeah, and besides, you’ve got that scholarship, right? You’ve got the money. Why not take it? Yeah, but I don’t think I’ve got the drive. I’ve been unemployed for so long, I’m not sure if I can even be motivated to go back to school. I just don’t know where to start. Listen, I know it’s not easy. I’m still in the process of getting my degree, and I’m not exactly sure what I’m doing, but I’m still here. And I’m still learning. You can do it. Besides, we’re all here for you. We’ll help you get through it. Yeah, and we’ve got this flat. I mean, we’re all sharing the same living space, so we’re in this together. We’ve got each other’s backs. I guess. I just don’t know. My parents are always saying I should get a job, but I just can’t seem to find one. I feel like I’m stuck in this loop. You’re not stuck. You’re just waiting for the right opportunity. And if you’re not getting it, maybe it’s time to take control of your own future. Exactly. And if you need help, go talk to me. I’m a teaching assistant, so I know what it’s like to be in that situation. I’ve been there, and I can help you get there.

Alright, right, so I’ve got this baking lesson coming up for the kids, and I need to make sure I’ve got everything sorted out. I was at Morrisons earlier, and I found a really nice book on baking with kids. It’s got all these fun recipes and tips. Oh, I saw that book too! I think it was on the shelf by the pasta. It looked really colorful. Did you get it? Yeah, I saw it too! Mom, can I help you with the baking lesson? I’ve got a lot of energy, and I love baking. You know I like to help with cookies and things. That’s great, Tom! You’re always so enthusiastic. I was thinking, maybe we could make some cupcakes for the lesson. They’re fun for the kids, and they’re easy to decorate. Plus, it gives them a chance to be creative. I love cupcakes! Can we add some sprinkles? I saw some rainbow ones in the bakery section, and they looked so pretty. Of course! We can do that. But we need to make sure the cupcakes are ready in time. I’ve got to remember to buy the flour, butter, and eggs. Wait, I think I saw a recipe for chocolate cupcake batter – it’s got everything you need, and it’s really simple. Can we make a special one for the half birthday celebration too? I heard you’re having one soon, right? That’s right! We’re planning to have a half birthday celebration for the kids. It’s going to be a surprise, but I’ve got some ideas – maybe we can make a special cake and have a little party with games and decorations. Oh, I can help with the decorations! I’ve got some stickers and paper plates from last time. And we can make a birthday banner, too. That’s perfect. I was thinking of making a banner with the kids’ names on it. We can have it up as we’re waiting for the cupcakes to bake. And maybe we can have a little joke or two – the kids love a good laugh. What kind of jokes? Well, like the one about the baker who always goes on vacation – because he needs to get out of the dough! Or the one about the boy who always wears a hat – he’s a ‘top’ baker!

So, do you ever find it funny how people still argue about whether Facebook is good or bad? I mean, it’s just a platform, right? I know, but it’s funny how it's shaped so much of our lives. I still can’t believe how much time I spend scrolling through it. My friend Andy once said he felt like he was living someone else’s life through their posts. A lot of people say that. I think social media has changed the way we connect, but it’s also made us more superficial. Like, when you're scrolling, you’re not really engaging with people, you're just consuming content. Yeah, and then there's the whole issue of privacy. My mum keeps saying she doesn't understand why people post everything. I told her it’s like living in a fishbowl. You can't take it back once it's out there. Exactly. I remember when I was in university, I used to post a lot. But then I realized how much I was oversharing. I still do it, but more carefully now. It’s like a balancing act between being visible and being private. I think it’s also about how people use it for work and personal life. I work from home, so I have to be really careful about what I post. Sometimes, I feel like I'm being watched. You know, the whole "always on" thing. Oh, I know that feeling. There’s also this weird culture around online validation. Like, you post something and then you feel like you need to get likes or comments to feel good about it. It’s not healthy, really. Definitely. I think about how I used to talk to people face to face, and now it’s all texts and social media. It’s changed the way we communicate. I don’t know if we’re better off or not. I guess it’s like any tool. It can be used well or it can be misused. I think the key is to be aware of how we use it. And maybe, like, take a break once in a while. Agreed. I’m trying to set aside specific times to check my phone. It’s hard, though. Especially in the evenings when everyone is on their phones. Yeah, it’s a real challenge. But I think it’s important to remember what’s real and what’s just online.

I swear, I’ve never seen a film so full of meatballs. I mean, it’s like the whole plot revolves around a giant meatball. I’m just trying to figure out what the point is. Yeah, I know, right? It’s such a weird movie. I mean, it’s supposed to be a kids’ movie, but the way they’re portraying the meatballs… it’s like they’re giving them too much personality. Exactly! And the way they keep talking about the weather. "Cloudy with a chance of meatballs." It’s like the whole movie is a metaphor for something. Maybe it’s about fate? Or maybe it’s just dumb. I think it’s more about how people react to things they can’t control. Like the characters are constantly trying to avoid the meatballs, but in the end, they can’t escape them. Maybe it’s a commentary on life? That’s a bit much, isn’t it? I mean, we’re supposed to be watching this on a Friday night, not analysing it like it’s some kind of deep film. Although, I have to admit, the kid’s perspective is kind of interesting. They don’t care about the meatballs—it’s just a part of the world. Yeah, that’s true. I think the film is kind of a template for how kids see the world. All these big things that seem scary or confusing, but in the end, they’re just part of life. Like, the meatballs are just meatballs. I guess. Although, I still don’t get why the weather is so central to the plot. It’s like they’re trying to make a point about how unpredictable life is. Or maybe the director just got too excited about the idea of weather-related disasters. Maybe. I mean, it’s a kids’ movie. They have to make it fun and engaging. But honestly, I think the way they portray the characters is kind of progressive. Like, the main girl is really strong and independent. She’s not just the damsel in distress. That’s surprising for a film from the '90s. Yeah, I didn’t think about that. I guess it’s a bit of a hidden message. They’re trying to show that even though things can be strange or unpredictable, you can still stand up for yourself. And the way they talk about the remote control.

So, do you know what’s going on with the government these days? I was just reading about New Labour and Tony Blair again. It’s funny how the political landscape has changed so much since he was in power. Yeah, I remember the days when Tony Blair was all about "New Labour" and trying to make the UK more modern. It was a bit of a shift from the old-style Labour, but I have to say, he did bring in a lot of reforms. Still, I think people were a bit tired of the constant talk about the "third way" and the "broad left." Exactly. It felt like they were trying to appeal to both the left and the right, but in the end, it just confused a lot of people. I mean, you couldn’t really tell if they were left or right anymore. I think that’s why the Conservatives eventually made a comeback. I agree. And then there was the whole "flattering the Tories" thing, you know? It was like they were trying to be so moderate that they lost their identity. I mean, it worked for a while, but in the end, it backfired. I think that's what happened. The public wanted a clear choice, not this mix of ideologies. It's like football – you can’t have a team that plays both attacking and defensive styles all the time. You need to pick a side. That's a good analogy! I mean, just look at the way football has evolved. Clubs like Liverpool used to be all about attacking play, but now they’re trying to be more balanced. It’s worked for a while, but I think the fans are starting to miss the old style. Definitely. I watched a match last week where they were playing a more defensive approach, and it felt like they were losing their identity. It's like politics sometimes – you need to stick to your core values, even if it means taking a hard line. Exactly. But I think it's also about the audience you're trying to appeal to. If you're trying to win over the middle ground, you have to find a balance. But if you lose sight of your base, you're in trouble. That's true. It's a fine line to walk, isn't it? Just like in football, you need to find that balance between attack and defense, or you're going to get beaten.

I just finished watching a recording from the British National Corpus, and it’s so fascinating. You know, the way people use "like" and "um" in everyday speech—it’s like a whole different language. Yeah, I remember when I first started studying linguistics, I thought it was just people being lazy. But now I understand it’s more about how language evolves. I mean, even in my job as an editor, I see how people use these filler words differently depending on their region. Exactly. I’ve noticed that in the East of England, people use "like" more than in the South. It’s almost like a regional dialect marker. Have you ever thought about how social media might be changing that? Definitely! I think platforms like LinkedIn and Instagram are influencing the way we speak, even in professional settings. People are starting to use more casual language in formal contexts. It’s almost like the lines between spoken and written communication are blurring. I hear you, but I think some of that’s just the natural evolution of language. I mean, even in the Maldives, where I visited last year, I noticed people using quite a different way of speaking. It’s not just about social media—it’s about how people interact with each other in different environments. That’s true, but I can’t help but wonder how long it’ll take for those changes to become standardised. I mean, even the way we talk about travel—like, "I’m going to Spain" versus "I’m off to Spain"—it’s just one of those subtle differences that really define our speech patterns. And don’t even get me started on flying. I still can’t get over being scared of it. I remember the first time I flew to Wales—just a short trip—but I was so nervous I had to take a pill. It was ridiculous. I get it. I always tell people that flying is just a way to get from A to B, but for some, it’s a nightmare. I once had a friend who was so scared of flying that he refused to go to Spain for a month, even though he loved the culture. I think that’s part of the beauty of travel. It’s not just about the destination—it’s about the journey and the experiences along the way.

Alright, I've got the pesto sauce ready, and the pasta’s about to finish. What’s the plan for Christmas, Claire? I know you’ve been busy with the intern stuff. Oh, it’s been a wild ride. I’ve had to work late a few times, but I’m managing. I was actually thinking we could do something different this year. Maybe a trip to Cornwall? The weather’s been awful here, and I’d love a change of scenery. That sounds amazing. I’ve always wanted to go to Cornwall. But I’ve got to be honest, I’m not sure if I can afford it. I’ve been working part-time and saving up for my own place. I know, I’ve been there too. But you know, there are some really good deals if you plan properly. I think I’ve seen a few listings online for short-term rentals. Maybe we could split the cost? Yeah, I’d love that. It would be so nice to have some time away from the city. Although, I should probably talk to my flatmates first, just to make sure they’re up for it. Hey, what’s up? I’ve just got back from a meeting. I brought some cake, thought you might need a pick-me-up after preparing all that food. Thanks, Jim! You’re a lifesaver. We were just talking about Christmas plans. Claire was suggesting a trip to Cornwall. What do you think? Sounds great. I’d love to go. I’ve been meaning to visit Cornwall for ages. But I have to be honest, I’m not sure if I can take time off work. I’ve been dealing with some projects that are due soon. I get that. But maybe you could take a few days off here and there? Or maybe we could plan something that doesn’t involve too much travel. There are some really nice places here in London that are worth checking out. Yeah, I mean, it’s not like we can’t do something local. Maybe we could have a big dinner or something. You know, like the old days. That sounds good too. I think I’d rather have a nice dinner with good food and good company rather than being somewhere cold and rainy. Exactly. So maybe we could compromise. We could go to Cornwall for a weekend, and then do something local for the rest of the holidays.

So, do you think I should go for the new yoga class that’s starting next week? I’ve been feeling a bit stressed lately, and maybe it’ll help me unwind. Oh, that sounds like a great idea! I’ve been meaning to try it too. I heard the instructor is really good and the class is quite relaxed. You should definitely sign up. Thanks, I’ll do that. I’ve been trying to get more exercise, but honestly, I haven’t been going to the gym as much as I’d like. It’s just so hard to find the time. I know what you mean. Between work and cooking dinner for our friends, it’s hard to make time for anything else. Although, I must say, I think your cooking is getting better lately. Oh, thanks! I’ve been experimenting with new recipes. I tried making a vegetarian curry the other day, and it turned out pretty well. Maybe I should start a cooking blog, you know? That’s a brilliant idea! You’ve got a real talent for it. I can see it being really popular. Do you have any plans for your blog yet? Not really. I was just thinking about it. Maybe I can start with a few simple recipes and then build up from there. I could even include some tips for people who are new to cooking. That would be amazing. You know, I’ve been thinking about starting a food column for the magazine. Maybe we could collaborate? I’d love to have your insights. That’s a great thought! I’d love to work with you. I’ve been meaning to write about food more, and this could be the perfect opportunity. Perfect! I’ll send you some ideas and we can discuss further. Oh, and speaking of food, have you tried the new restaurant that opened near the station? No, I haven’t. I’ve been too busy with work. But I’m definitely going to check it out soon. I heard the reviews are really good. Yeah, I’m going there this weekend with some friends. It’s a fusion place, so the menu is quite interesting. I’m hoping to try some of the new dishes. That sounds exciting. I’ll definitely go with you next time. I’ve been craving something a bit different lately. Great! I’ll make sure to bring some snacks to share.

I just got a message from Lucy saying she’s coming over tomorrow. She wants to catch up, and she’s bringing some wine. I’m glad she’s still in touch. It feels like ages since we last saw each other. That’s great. I bet she’s still the same — full of stories and opinions. I remember when we were all in that little flat in London, and she used to complain about her toe nails all the time. She said they were like little swords. Oh, right! She used to be so obsessed with her manicure. I think she even tried to paint them like a Russian doll. I mean, it was a bit much. But she always said it made her feel like a proper professional. You know, like she was ready for a meeting or something. She did take it seriously. I remember once she had an entire conversation about the difference between a French manicure and a gel polish. It was like she was in a seminar. I didn’t even know what gel polish was at the time. I still don’t. I just do the basics — maybe a bit of polish, but never too much. I’ve got a few friends who are like Lucy, though. They’re always talking about their nails, their skincare routines, and their upcoming trips. Sometimes I wonder if they’re still friends because they have something in common or because they’re just too nice to say no. I think it’s both. They have a way of keeping each other in check. But seriously, it’s a good thing. I mean, without Lucy, I’d be lost. Or at least, I’d be more like me — which is not a good thing. Exactly! And you know, even though we’re both lecturers and stuff, we still have this weird way of staying connected. It’s like we’re not just friends, we’re like collaborators in the chaos of life. Yeah, and I think that’s what makes it special. We can talk about teaching, or about toe nails, or about our friends, and it’s all just part of the same conversation. It’s not a chore. It’s just life, you know? Exactly. And I’m happy about that. Even if it’s just walking home from work and talking about the nonsense we’ve been through.

So, do you remember that film we watched last year? The one with the conspiracy theory twist at the end? I still can’t believe they didn’t mention the obvious clues. Oh, that was wild. I thought I’d figured it out halfway through, but then they threw in that twist. Honestly, I was so confused I almost walked out. Yeah, I know. But it made me think—how many of those films are actually just trying to manipulate our perceptions? It’s like they’re trying to make us question everything. For sure. I mean, we’ve seen it in the news too. People are always talking about conspiracy theories. It’s like the world’s full of hidden messages. I agree. I think it’s part of the media’s way of keeping us entertained, but also keeping us off balance. But then again, maybe that’s just me overthinking. I think you’re not overthinking. I mean, I’ve been thinking about that a lot lately. With the way the news is presented, it’s like they’re giving us fragments of the truth, and we’re supposed to piece it together. Exactly. It’s like a puzzle with missing pieces. And sometimes, the pieces don’t even fit. I mean, who even knows what’s real anymore? You’re not wrong. I’ve been telling my kids that if something seems too good to be true, it usually is. But they don’t listen. They think they’re too smart for that stuff. I remember when I was their age, I thought I was too smart for that too. But I was definitely wrong. You never know what’s about to happen. That’s the thing, isn’t it? Life is full of surprises. Like marriage. I know some people say it’s a choice, but I think it’s more complicated than that. It’s like a mystery. I think you’re right. I mean, I was in a relationship for years, and when I finally did get married, it was like I’d been waiting for something I couldn’t even describe. Exactly. Some people go through life not really knowing what they’re looking for, and then suddenly, it’s there. It’s like a dream come true. Yeah, I guess that’s what we’re all searching for, isn’t it? Whether it’s love, success, or just a little bit of peace of mind.

I've been thinking about Jamaica Inn again. You know, that book by Ethel Lyle? I read it last year and it really got me thinking about old English houses and all that superstition stuff. It's so different from the Wizard of Oz, isn't it? Oh, I remember that one! I read it when I was a lad, back in the 70s. It's a bit dark, though. Not like the Wizard of Oz, which is so bright and magical. But I think it's a good book anyway. It makes you imagine all those old houses with secrets under the floorboards. Yeah, I can see that. I also love Sherlock Holmes. My dad used to tell me stories about him when I was little. He’s like the ultimate detective, isn’t he? He is! And the way he uses logic and deduction to solve mysteries is amazing. I still remember the time I read  The Hound of the Baskervilles . That book really sticks with you, doesn’t it? Definitely. It’s like Lewis Carroll’s books—there’s always a twist. I mean,  Alice in Wonderland  is so full of imagination, isn’t it? It’s like a fairy tale but with a unique twist. Oh, it's one of my favorites. I used to read it aloud to the kids when they were little. It’s amazing how it can make you feel like you're in a different world. Speaking of that, have you ever thought about Morse code? I used to learn it when I was in the army. That’s cool! I didn’t know you were in the army. But I’ve heard about Morse code before. I think it’s the thing that’s used in texting, isn’t it? Not exactly. It's more like a way to send messages over long distances, like with telegraphs. It's part of history, really. I used to use it a lot when I was working in customer services. You meet all sorts of people on the road. That sounds exciting. I'm just hoping this journey will be a little more relaxed. I’m not too worried about directions—though I did bring a map just in case. I can go anywhere with my GPS, but sometimes it’s nice to have a backup plan. You're smart to have a backup.

I just got back from the market. I picked up some fresh veggies and a nice loaf of bread. The first thing I’m going to do is make a proper Sunday roast. You know, like we used to do when we were kids. Oh, I remember those days. We used to have Sunday roasts every single week. My mum would make the best Yorkshire pudding. I still dream about it sometimes. You should try making it with real eggs and butter, not that cheap stuff you get in supermarkets now. Yeah, I’ve heard that Yorkshire pudding is a bit of a lost art these days. I’ve tried a few times, but I always end up with something like a soggy pile of disappointment. Maybe it’s just me. I’m more of a stir-fry kind of guy. Aye, and I think it’s because of all the rules and measurements. You’ve got to get the ratio of flour and water just right, or it won’t rise. I remember my gran used to measure everything with a spoon. She was the best at it. She was, and she used to say that if you don’t measure your ingredients properly, you’re not cooking—you’re just throwing things in a tin. Makes sense, really. I was always the one who tried to just guess. Got burned a few times. I’ve been into a lot of cooking lately, though. I started trying to make my own sourdough. It’s a bit of a pain in the backside, but I think it’s worth it. I’ve got a starter going now, and it’s been bubbling away for weeks. That’s cool. I’ve always wanted to try that. I hear it’s a real skill, though. You have to be patient. Maybe I’ll start with that next. I’ve got a lot of time on my hands now with the kids at school and all. Aye, time’s on your side now. You’re not stuck in an office with a boss breathing down your neck anymore. I remember being stuck in that kind of situation for years. No space, no time, no peace of mind. Yeah, but you’ve got to take advantage of it. I’ve been thinking about going on a bike trip up the coast. Maybe something like the South West Coast Path.

Hey Mum, I just got back from my weekend trip to London. I had the most amazing time, but I’m still pretty jet-lagged. How are you feeling? I’m fine, thank you, but I’ve been feeling a bit off lately. I think it’s the weather here. It’s been so damp, and I’ve been getting some strange pains in my joints. You know how it is with old bones. Yeah, I can imagine. I had a similar thing when I was in my early twenties. But I also remember when you used to get up at five in the morning to bake those amazing scones. I can still smell them in my head. Oh, that’s right! I used to love making them. I still do, but I’m not as fast as I used to be. Oh, and I’ve been thinking about moving house again. I feel like I need more space now that I’m working from home. That makes sense. You know, I was looking at a few places in Bedford. I’ve been trying to get the list of things we need to move. Do you remember the last time we did that? It was a real nightmare with all the boxes and the old furniture. Oh, yes! I remember you getting so stressed when we had to move the old sofa. You even got a bit of a temper. But that’s what you get for being too close to the move. Honestly, I think I was just exhausted. But I’m trying to stay positive. I’ve also been thinking about our friends from university. It’s been way too long since we all got together. You know, I was actually talking to Sarah the other day. She mentioned she’s getting married next year. She’s moving to Spain. I’m so happy for her, but I wonder if I’ll ever be able to travel like that again. I think you’ll be fine. You’ve always had a great sense of adventure. Remember when we went to Cornwall when I was 17? You even caught a weaver fish out of the sea with your bare hands. Oh, that was a disaster! I nearly lost my arm trying to hold the fish. But I still have the photo of it on my wall. I remember that. It’s such a nostalgic memory.

I just got a new plant for the living room. Thought it would be a bit of a mood booster. You know, after the whole lockdown thing, I’m feeling like I need a bit of greenery around me. Yeah, I can relate. I’ve been trying to grow a few herbs in pots, but my basil keeps dying. I swear it’s just not happy with me. Maybe it needs more sunlight? I put mine near the window, and it’s doing alright. I’ve also been thinking about getting a haircut. The one I had last year was too long, and I feel like I’m ready for something new. Oh, you should go for a shorter style. You always look so good with a bit of edge. Speaking of changes, have you heard about the new A-Level reforms? I think they’re trying to make it more flexible, but I’m not sure if it’s actually helping students. Honestly, I’m not too sure either. I remember when we did our A-Levels, it was pretty stressful, but at least there was a clear path. I hope the changes don’t make things harder for the next generation. I agree. It feels like there’s always something changing, especially with the NHS. I just got my vaccinations done – it’s been a bit of a hassle, but I’m glad I did it. Yeah, I know what you mean. I had to wait for ages to get my appointment, and the waiting rooms are always so full. I read somewhere that the NHS is struggling with the petrol crisis too. It’s a bit of a domino effect, isn’t it? Definitely. Gas prices have gone up so much, and I’m worried about how it’s going to affect everyone. My mum said she’s starting to drive less and take the bus more. It’s all very confusing. I guess we just have to adapt. I’ve started walking more, and it’s actually been nice. I feel healthier, and I’m saving money. Plus, the fresh air is good for the soul. That’s a great idea. I’ll have to try that. Anyway, I think I’m going to take a break from the TV and go for a walk. You want to come? Sure, why not? It’s been a long day, and a bit of fresh air might do us both good.

Right, so I was thinking, do you know if the university’s been doing anything about the smoking ban? I’ve been trying to find a spot to smoke, but everywhere’s got that “no smoking” sign. Oh, I know what you mean. I tried to smoke on the balcony the other day, but the wind blew the smoke straight into my face. It’s like they put that sign just to make us feel guilty. Yeah, and I heard they might be introducing some kind of smoke-free zones on campus. I’m not sure if that’s a good idea or not. I mean, I don’t smoke, but I think it’s kinda rude to make others feel like they can’t breathe. I say, let the smokers breathe. It’s not like we’re all born with lungs, is it? I mean, everyone has a right to smoke, right? And the university should just not make it so bloody hard to do. Yeah, but it’s not just about the smoke. It’s about health. I read this article the other day about how secondhand smoke can be dangerous, especially for kids. And we’re not even talking about kids here—just people trying to study and not get coughing fits. I get it, but I think the real problem is that universities are just trying to appear ‘modern’ and ‘aware.’ They don’t want to be seen as places where people can actually smoke anymore. I mean, I’m not against the idea of trying to be healthier, but it’s not like we can just ban all forms of smoking. It’s not like they’re making it illegal to smoke outside. It’s just making it harder to do so. Exactly! It’s all about control. They want to control everything—smoking, drinking, even how we dress. I mean, I think it’s a bit much, don’t you? I think you’re right. But then again, I think it’s also about trying to promote a healthier lifestyle. I go to university, and I know that some of the people here have kids, so it’s not just about us anymore. Yeah, I think you’re right. It’s a complicated issue. I mean, I don’t smoke, but I get that it’s not just about the smoke. It’s about the whole culture around it—like how we talk about it, how we deal with it.

I just can’t believe how long we’ve been driving without seeing anyone. I know it’s supposed to be a holiday, but I’m starting to feel like I’m going mad. I know, right? It’s funny how you feel like you need to see people, yet the moment you do, you want to run away. I’ve been thinking about that a lot. Yeah, I’ve been there. I think it's that weird human thing where you don’t want to deal with the expectations of being seen. It’s like when you're in a group, suddenly you feel under pressure to be the perfect version of yourself. Exactly. And the worst part is, you know you should still be friends, but you don’t want to deal with the hassle of catching up or the awkwardness of not knowing what to say. I remember when I was in university, I had this friend who would always say, “I’m just not in the mood to see you.” It was so easy, right? Just say it and then not see them for weeks. Oh, I loved that. But I guess it’s not quite as simple as that. You still feel guilty, even if you’re not there. Like, you’re not being there for them. Exactly. And I think it’s also because we’re all so busy. You know, work, life, everything. It’s hard to make time for people when your own life is a mess. But what if you don’t want to be friends anymore? How do you even say that? I think the key is to be honest but not cruel. You don’t have to be abrupt. Maybe you just let them know you’re not in the mood to see them and then you just… don’t. It’s like a silent agreement. You both know what’s going on. That makes sense. I think I’ve done that with a couple of people. It’s not easy, but it’s better than pretending you’re still friends when you’re not. Yeah, and it’s not like you’re cutting them out completely. You’re just not there. That way, you don’t have to deal with the pressure of being someone else's friend. I guess it’s just about setting boundaries. And sometimes, that’s harder than it seems.

Mate, I’ve been meaning to ask you—what’s it like being an artist? I mean, I’m studying art history, but I still don’t get how you can make a living off it. You know, like, how do you even start? Oh, it’s not always easy, love. But if you’re passionate about it, it’s worth it. I started in Vienna, you know. I used to paint landscapes, and then I got into murals. It took years to get to where I am now, but the joy of creating something that moves people is enough. That’s cool. I’ve been thinking about doing some street art, but I’m not sure if I’m cut out for it. I mean, I can draw, but I’m more of a ‘behind the scenes’ kinda person. Well, you’ve got the right attitude. I remember when I first started, I didn’t have a studio, just a small room in my flat. I used to paint on cardboard, and then I’d take it to the market. It was messy, but it worked. You just have to be persistent. Yeah, I guess. I’ve been thinking of going to Vienna, though. I heard the museums there are amazing. Any recommendations? Oh, you should definitely check out the Kunsthistorisches Museum. It’s one of the biggest collections in Europe. And the Secession Building—just stunning. I had my first exhibition there in the 80s. Can you believe it? No way! That’s incredible. Have you ever been to London? I mean, I’ve been there a few times, but I’d love to see the art scene there. Yes, I’ve passed through a few times. I remember seeing a Turner exhibition at the Tate. He was a genius. But you know what I miss most? The coffee. In London, they serve it with so much attitude. Yeah, I’ve noticed that. But I’ve been reading a lot lately—this book about the Impressionists. It’s pretty heavy, but I think I’m getting into it. You should read ‘The Story of Art’ by E.H. Gombrich. It’s a classic. I read it when I was your age, and it changed everything for me. I’ll check it out. Maybe I’ll even take you to an exhibition once I graduate. Now that’s the spirit. You’ve got the right mix of talent and curiosity.

I can't believe we've been on the road for three days already. I thought it would take longer, but I guess time flies when you're driving through Poland. Yeah, it's been a mad few days. I feel like I've aged ten years just sitting in this van, eating takeaway and arguing about the best way to drive on Polish roads. You know, I think I'm starting to understand why so many people say that being English is like being a language. It's all about accents, dialects, and the way you say things. Do you ever get tired of being called "laddish" or "brash" just for being from the north? Oh, absolutely. My accent gets me more than my actual personality. I've had people assume I'm from Manchester or Liverpool just based on how I say "thanks" or "bloody hell." And don't even get me started on the sexism I've faced. It's exhausting trying to explain that I'm not just a "flirty teacher" or a "dragon lady." I know what you mean. I've been called everything from "a bit of a landlady" to "a woman who's too much for the boys." It's frustrating because I'm not trying to be anything except who I am. Sometimes I wonder if we're still living in the 1950s. Exactly! And it’s not just about how we speak—it's about how we're treated. I think people still assume that women can’t be assertive or professional. I had a male colleague recently who’d rather have a female student call him "sir" than speak to him as an equal. I'm sorry you've had to deal with that. I've had my share of sexist comments too, especially when I was working as a teacher. People would say things like, "Oh, you're such a good listener" or "You're not too bossy, are you?" As if being assertive is a bad thing. It really is. We’re not just being unprofessional—we're being taken less seriously. And it’s not just in the workplace. It’s everywhere. I think it's time for a real change. I agree. But I'm not sure how to start. Maybe just by speaking our minds and not letting people define us. Who knows, maybe we’ll change the conversation.

Well, I’ve been sorting out the garden again, and it’s been a bit of a challenge, to be honest. I tried planting some new flowers, but the spiders have been everywhere! Got to be careful with the watering can, I tell you. Oh, I know what you mean. I had a bit of an incident with a spider last week. I was out in the garden, and one of those big, black ones came scuttling across my feet. I screamed so loud, I woke up the whole house! You must have had a start! I remember when I was a kid, my mum used to say that if you ever saw a spider in the garden, it’s a sign of good luck. But I’m not so sure anymore. I think it’s just the weather making them more active. Maybe that’s true. The weather’s been so strange lately, isn’t it? One minute, it’s sunny and warm, the next, it’s pouring with rain. I tell you, I’ve been caught in the rain more times this year than I’ve had holidays! I know, it’s been quite a rollercoaster. I’ve even had a power cut recently. I was in the middle of making a cup of tea, and the lights just went out. It was a bit of a shock, but at least the tea was still hot. You’d have had to have been a wizard to make that happen! I remember when I was teaching, we used to have regular power cuts. The school would have to switch to generators, and we’d all be standing in the dark, waiting for the lights to come back on. I can imagine. Still, I think the garden has been the best part of the past few weeks. I’ve even started hand-thrown mugs. It’s something I’ve wanted to try for years, and I’ve been getting quite good at it, if I do say so myself. That’s wonderful! I’ve always admired people who can do things like that. I’ve never had the patience for crafts, but I do love decorating. I’ve been painting the walls in the garden room, and I think it’s looking quite nice. It really is. I’ve been thinking about the local festival coming up. I think we should go this year.

I can't wait for our holiday! I’ve been thinking about it all week. Are we going somewhere fun this year? Oh, yes, we are! We’re going to the coast again. It’s been a while since we’ve gone to the seaside. I think we’re heading to Scarborough this time. Scarborough? That’s a good choice. I remember going there when I was a kid. The beach is still beautiful, and the town has a nice vibe. You’ll love it, lass. I hope so! I’ve heard it’s really peaceful. I was wondering, are we bringing the whole family? I mean, my mum and dad are still around, right? Yeah, we are. The whole family’s coming. Even your cousin Alex is coming along. He’s been wanting to go somewhere with the sea for ages. Good. That’ll be nice. You know, I’ve been thinking about taking some old photos from the 70s, you know, those black and white shots. Maybe we can look at them over the holiday, and remember the old days. That sounds brilliant! I still have a few photos from when I was little. I can bring them too. We could have a little photo album. It might be fun to show the kids, too. Yes, that’s a great idea. I’ll bring the ones from my grandparents’ house. They had some really old ones. I wonder if they still have the original negatives. I’m sure they do. You know, I’d love to see the old places again. Even if they’ve changed a bit, it’s always nice to look back. It reminds us how far we’ve come. I know what you mean. It’s funny how time flies. I feel like yesterday I was just starting school. Now, I’m off to college next year. It’s crazy how fast things change. It really is. But I think it’s good that you’re looking forward to your future. As long as we stay connected, we’ll always have this kind of time together. That’s the best part of it, isn’t it? No matter where life takes us, we always have each other. And that’s something to be grateful for. Absolutely. I’m really looking forward to the holiday. I can’t wait to see all the places and meet up with everyone.

I just watched  10 Things I Hate About You  again, and I was like, "Oh my god, this movie is so good!" It’s like,  why  haven’t I seen it before? Yeah, I know, right? It’s one of those classic rom-coms that just never gets old. I mean, the chemistry between Katie and Patrick is  so  good. It’s like they were made for each other. Totally! And the way they deal with their problems—like, she’s got to go through all that drama just to get him to like her. It’s so realistic, even though it’s a movie. Yeah, I think that’s why it’s so relatable. I mean, I can totally see myself in Kat, honestly. I’m not a rebel, but I do get annoyed when people don’t take me seriously. Like, why can’t guys just see that I’m smart and not just some pretty face? Exactly! And I feel like that’s what so many girls go through. I mean, I get it, you know? I’ve had teachers who think I’m just there to sit in the back and daydream, but I’m actually super into my subjects. Oh, I know. It’s just frustrating. But I guess that’s why I’m thinking about applying to a good school next year. I want to go to a place where people actually value your work, not just your looks. That sounds awesome. I’ve been thinking about a trip to London too. I’ve never been there, and I’ve heard it’s amazing. I was planning to go with my cousin next summer, but I’m not sure yet. Oh, that’s cool! I’ve always wanted to go to London. I’ve been reading so many books set there, like  Pride and Prejudice  and  Harry Potter . I can’t wait to see the real places they talk about. Yeah, it would be so much fun. You could see the landmarks, eat good food, and just have a great time. Maybe we can plan a trip together one day? That’d be awesome. I mean, if we can afford it, of course. But I think it’s something we should definitely try to do. Definitely. I’m really looking forward to it. And I can’t wait to see how the school year goes too.

Well, I've just seen this on Facebook, and I couldn't believe it. Someone posted a photo of a chicken pox rash, and they're saying it's the worst thing ever. I nearly fell out of my chair. Oh, I remember when I had chicken pox. My mum had to keep me in bed for weeks. It was terrible. I reckon it's worse than the flu, if you ask me. Yeah, I had it when I was a kid too. But I think it was actually pretty mild. I remember playing in the garden, and the spots were just on my arms. I didn't even miss school. I didn't have chicken pox at all. My mum said she was lucky because she had it when she was young and it didn't affect her too much. But I do remember her talking about how it was a real nuisance for the family. I think I had it when I was about five. My dad used to say it was the best thing that ever happened to me, because he had to stay home with me and it gave him a chance to spend time with the family. Oh, I remember when my brother had it. He was a mess for weeks. He kept scratching, and got infected. It was a nightmare. I got a bit of it, but nothing serious. I think it's actually more common in younger people. I remember reading that chicken pox tends to be more severe in adults. So it's better to get it when you're a child. Yeah, I’d say it's a bit of a double-edged sword. You get over it, but you also have to deal with the after-effects. I remember the scarring from my childhood chicken pox. I know that. I still have some scarring on my arms. I used to laugh about it. I told everyone that I had passed the test of time. But now I think it's a bit of a reminder of how far I've come. We should talk about religion. I've been thinking a lot about it lately. Especially with the whole OCD thing. It feels like there's something more to it than just being a mental illness. I think it's a real condition. I've known people who have it, and it's really hard.

I just got a new fridge, and it’s so much more efficient than the one we had before. Honestly, I think it’s the quietest fridge I’ve ever had. You can hear the old one humming like a little engine. Oh, I bet the old one had a personality. I remember my gran’s fridge — it used to make all sorts of noises. She said it was trying to tell her something. Yeah, I used to have a fridge that made a sound like someone was humming in the back. I used to think it was a ghost. I had a fridge that even had a broken light. I used to play with it like it was a toy. It was so old, it was like a museum piece. I had the same fridge for over ten years. It was the only thing in the house that stayed the same. Now I’ve got a new one that’s so smart, it knows when I’m coming home. You know, I think the fridge is one of the few things that can give you a sense of nostalgia. I still miss the one I had when I was a kid. It had a real, old-school design. You know, I was just thinking about Germany. My brother-in-law went there last summer, and he said the food was amazing. He tried all sorts of things, like sausages and schnitzel. I’ve never been, but I’ve always wanted to. I think I’d like to go to Berlin. I heard it’s got all those cool street art and delicious beer. I went to Munich once, and I had the best bratwurst of my life. But I had to be careful — I didn’t want to drink too much beer. I think I’d go to Germany for the culture. I love the architecture. I passed a beautiful old building in Frankfurt once — it looked like a fairy tale. Germany is a country with a rich history. I think you can feel it in the streets. Even the cars there are a little different from ours. Oh, and the accents! I heard some people there with the most unique tones. I think it’s like a different language, but it makes sense once you get used to it. You know what’s funny? My dad always said that the only way to understand German is to learn it.

Hey man, how’s life treating you? You’ve been busy with that restaurant gig, right? It’s been a whirlwind, honestly. We’ve been doing a few events lately, and I’ve been trying to get some time to work on my own stuff. How about you? Still in that uni grind? Yeah, still stuck in the same boat. Just finished my thesis, but I’ve got a few interviews lined up for internships. Still figuring out what I want to do next. That’s cool. You always had that creative vibe about you. You know, I was thinking about music the other day—specifically, that band you love, The Black Keys. You ever seen them live? Oh man, I did! Last year, they played at the Royal Albert Hall. It was crazy. They had this energy, like, every single note was raw and real. You should check out their new album,  Delta Kream . It’s like they’re bringing that bluesy vibe back to the forefront. I’ve heard about it, but I haven’t gotten around to it yet. I’m more into the drumming side. I’ve been practicing with some new gear, and I reckon I’m getting closer to that groove. You ever drum? Not really, but I’ve always wanted to. I mean, I’ve got a rudimentary sense of rhythm, but I’d kill for a real drum kit. Maybe one day, I’ll just grab one and see what happens. That’s the spirit. You never know, maybe you’ll end up playing in a band. I mean, I had a friend who used to jam with a few people, and it turned into a real thing. Yeah, I’ve thought about that. I’ve got a few mutual friends who are into music, and we’ve been talking about starting something. It’s still in the early stages, but it’s fun to dream about it. Sounds like a plan. I’ll be waiting to hear your next move. And if you ever decide to pick up the sticks, let me know—I’ve got a few tips to offer. Will do. And hey, if you ever need a gig or a place to rehearse, you know where to find me. Deal. Let’s keep in touch, mate. You never know where life’s going to take us. The music scene’s always got something to offer.

So, what do you think, love? I know it's a bit early for coffee, but I thought we'd stop on the way back from the supermarket. You know, just a little pick-me-up before we head home. Yeah, mum, I'm fine. But I guess it's not every day we get to stop for coffee. You know, I've been thinking about that summer holiday we were talking about. Should we go to Durham or maybe do something in Newcastle? Durham sounds nice. You remember that little shop near the castle? The one that sells all those quirky souvenirs? I think it's still there. And the town is so peaceful. Plus, it's not too far from where we used to live. But I’d say we should definitely plan something for the weekend, you know, to make it a proper holiday. Yeah, and I’ve got this idea about doing some kind of group trip with a few of my friends. Maybe even a domino drive, like the one we heard about in the news. You know, those people who drive around the countryside, selling stuff? Oh, that’s the one. I remember the one in York, they were absolutely ridiculous. But I suppose if you’ve got a van and a few friends, it can be a fun way to earn some extra cash. And it’s a great way to see the country. Although, I’d be worried about the traffic on the A1. It’s always so busy. Yeah, I heard about that too. You know, about the people who get stuck in the “drive through” all day. It’s like a whole different world out there. But I think it’d be cool if we could do something like that. Maybe even start a small business, like selling things at markets. That's a good idea. You know, I've always thought about starting something like that. Maybe you and I could do it together. It’s not too late, and it could be a great way to make some money for the holidays. Yeah, that sounds like a plan. I'll start looking into it. And I'll bring the shopping list too. We can do the market on Saturday, and then we’ll have all the supplies for the summer. Sounds perfect. Just don’t forget to bring the sleeping bags.

Hey, mate! How's it going? You're looking more like a grown-up every day. You're not one to talk, Tom. You’ve got a few years on me, and you’re still living with your parents. Oh, come on, I’ve got a flat in Sussex now. I even got a job teaching English. You know I wanted to be a writer, but life had other plans. Well, I'm an assurance analyst, which is basically a fancy way of saying I check people's finances for a living. But I love it. I like the structure, even if it’s not creative. That’s cool. You always had the kind of personality that thrives in a corporate environment. I, on the other hand, am still figuring out how to balance being a teacher and a single man in his early 20s. Speaking of which, have you heard about Jo? She’s pregnant again. Wow, that’s a lot. I remember when she had her first kid, you were still in uni. Now she’s got two, and she’s about to have a third. Yeah, it’s wild. But I guess that’s just how it is. My sister’s got three, and my cousin’s got four. It’s like the family tradition now. Maybe I should start thinking about settling down. I mean, I’m in a good place financially, and I’m not trying to live in a van down by the river. Just be careful with money and budgets, mate. I’ve seen too many people fall into the trap of spending too much on things they don’t need. I know, I know. I’ve been tracking my expenses and even set up a joint bank account with my roommate. It’s not like I’m living with her, but it’s a good way to manage things. That’s smart. I tried that too, but I always ended up arguing about how much we should spend on groceries. Yeah, I can imagine. But I think it’s worth it for the peace of mind. Plus, I’ve been thinking about moving to South Korea for a while. It’s a chance to see the world and gain some experience. That sounds like a dream. But be careful with the cost of living and the language barrier. I know. I’m planning on learning some Spanish and even taking a few lessons in the city.

I just got a call from my sister. She's been really down lately, and it's not just the usual stress. She's been diagnosed with cancer, and it's affecting her mental health too. It's so hard to watch someone you love go through this. Oh no, that’s really awful. I’m so sorry to hear that. I can only imagine how hard it's been for you. I remember when my dad was diagnosed with prostate cancer a few years ago. It was tough on the whole family, but we pulled together. Yeah, it’s not easy. She's not just dealing with the physical aspects—it's the uncertainty, the fear, the whole thing. I can't even imagine what she's going through. I’ve been trying to support her, but I feel like I’m not doing enough. You’re doing more than enough, believe me. I think sometimes people don’t realize how much emotional support is just as important as physical care. Have you talked to her about how she's feeling? I have, but she’s not really opening up. She says she’s fine, but I can tell she’s struggling. I’m worried about her mental health too. I keep thinking, what if she doesn't make it? What if she gives up? I know how that feels, and I know how important it is to be there for someone like that. Maybe you should talk to her about getting some professional help? I know it’s hard to ask someone to do that, but it might be the best thing for her. I’ve thought about that. I just don’t want her to feel like she’s a burden. But maybe it’s time I stopped being so quiet about it. I can’t keep pretending I’m fine. Exactly. You are doing the right thing by being honest. And remember, you’re not alone in this. If you ever need someone to talk to, I’m here. We’re all in this together. Thank you. I really appreciate that. I just hope I can be there for her the way she needs me to be. You will be. And I’m sure she’ll be there for you too. We’re a family, and we’ve always looked out for each other, even when it’s hard.

Alright, let’s talk about the kids. You know, they’ve been promising to take up tennis seriously, but I haven’t seen much of them at the local courts lately. What’s going on? Yeah, I’ve been meaning to ask you about that. I’ve been thinking about getting some coaching. My friend’s dad is a coach, and he said he could help me out. But I don’t know if I should start now or wait until next term. That sounds like a good idea. Coaching can make all the difference. But have you thought about how much it might cost? I’ve been thinking about investing in my own business, and I’d hate to spend too much on things that don’t pay off. I’m not sure. I mean, I know my dad plays football, and he says it’s good for discipline. But I’m more into tennis. I’d rather play with my friends than go to a gym. Plus, I heard there’s a new tennis club opening in town, and it’s cheaper than the other ones. Oh, I heard about that too. I think it’s the one that’s next to the park. It might be a good idea for the kids to try it out. They can meet other young players and maybe even get some competitive experience. But I wonder if they’re still interested in the tennis thing after all the time they spent on football. Honestly, I’m not sure. I’ve been trying to convince them that tennis is better for their future. I mean, it’s a professional sport, and there are so many opportunities. But I also know that some of my classmates are more into football, and they’re already getting offers for apprenticeships. That’s the thing, though. You have to think about what works for them. If they’re passionate about tennis, it’s worth investing time and effort. But if they’re not, it might not be the best use of their energy. I remember when I was younger, I was all about football, and I didn’t take tennis seriously until later. Yeah, I think I’d rather wait and see what happens. I mean, I’ve got school exams coming up, and I don’t want to get too distracted. Maybe I can go to the new tennis club after school or on weekends.

So, do you think we’ll get to Lancaster on time? I’ve been trying to get a good seat on this train, but it’s been so crowded since we left London. I think we’ll make it. The only thing is, I got a bit of a problem with my bag. It’s stuck between two seats, and I can’t get it out without moving the whole row. You don’t mind if I borrow your bag for a minute, do you? Not at all! Just let me know when you’re done. Oh, by the way, did you hear about the cockle disaster we had last summer? I still can’t get over how the whole family ended up with fish and chips that tasted like cardboard. Oh, I remember that! My mum made the worst attempt at cooking, and we all ended up complaining about it for days. I guess that’s part of the tradition, though—being stuck in a seaside village with no real cooking facilities. Exactly! I mean, it’s a great chance to visit the coast and see the view, but sometimes the food is just... not up to standard. Anyway, did you hear about the university trip we’re planning? I think we’re going to visit the campuses in Lancaster and Manchester next week. Yeah, I got the email last night. It’s supposed to be part of my masters dissertation on regional dialects and social mobility. I’m really looking forward to it. Do you think the coast will influence the dialect in any way? Possibly. I’ve been doing a lot of research on that, and there’s definitely some interesting patterns when you look at coastal versus inland areas. Plus, it’s about time I got out of the city for a bit. Work’s been so hectic lately. I know what you mean. I’m trying to balance my admin job with my studies, and it’s hard not to get overwhelmed. I heard about your redundancy at work too. Are you okay? Yeah, I’m okay. It was a bit of a shock, but I’m focusing on my research now. It’s a chance to do something I really care about. I just hope I can finish my dissertation on time. That’s really brave of you. I’m going to start applying for some part-time jobs soon to help with the cost of living.

So, do you remember that band we used to listen to back in school? The one with the really loud guitar riffs and the singer who looked like he was always about to lose it on stage? Oh yeah, I remember that! They were kind of a big deal in our year. I think they even played at the school concert one time. You remember that? You were so excited, you stood on a table and tried to sing along with them. Oh, don’t remind me! I ended up getting called out by the head teacher. But honestly, it was the best night of my life. I mean, even if I did end up with a sore throat for a week. You were a total fan. Still are, though. I saw you last week at the music store, staring at their latest album like it was the last thing on Earth. Yeah, I know, I know. I just love the way they mix heavy riffs with some really emotional lyrics. It's like they're telling a story through the music. You ever think about starting a band? I mean, we both have that kind of passion. Honestly, I’ve thought about it. I mean, we’ve both been playing guitar since we were kids. We even had a small gig at the local pub last summer, and it was insane. People were going nuts, and the bar owner even gave us free drinks for the night. That’s amazing! I should’ve been there. I was too busy studying for my exams. It’s funny how things work out, isn’t it? We were just two kids with a lot of energy and no real direction, and now we’re in a situation where people are actually paying to hear us play. Yeah, it’s wild. I mean, we’re still barely out of sixthform, but we’re already doing stuff like this. I think it’s because we’ve known each other for so long. We’ve got that kind of bond that makes it easier to take chances. I agree. We’ve got each other’s backs no matter what. Even if we do end up on opposite sides of the stage, I know I can count on you. And I’ll always be there for you, mate. No matter what. That’s what friends are for.

I can't believe we've got to this point in Pandemic. I thought we’d have cured the last outbreak by now. Yeah, I thought we'd be on our third pandemic by now. But we’re stuck with this one, and it’s getting more complicated. I think the real issue is we’re all playing like we’re on different teams. You know, like a game of chess but with less strategy and more chaos. I’m not sure who’s actually in charge here. I mean, we’ve got six of us, and it feels like we’re just throwing darts at the board. You know, I remember when we first started playing this, it was just me and my brother. Now we’ve got a whole army of people who argue over whose turn it is. It’s not just the turns, it’s the way we all talk over each other. I swear I’ve heard at least three different dialects in this room, and I’m not even from Wales. Oh, come on, you know we’re all from different places. You’ve got a Welsh accent, I’ve got a South African upbringing, and he’s from Bristol. We’re all a little different. Exactly. But in this game, we’re all supposed to be working together. I mean, don’t you think we should have a better system for assigning roles? I think the real problem is we're too suspicious of each other. Like, every time someone says "I’m going to the lab," I immediately think they’re being dishonest. Yeah, and we all have different ideas about what constitutes a "lab" anyway. Do we mean the real lab or just a card? I think the real solution is to take a break and have a drink. This game is like a guesthouse in here — everyone wants to be the host. That’s true. We could always take a break and switch to something like Clue. At least that way, we’d know who’s the murderer. Clue? We’ve played that so many times, I’ve memorized the entire cast of characters. I think we're all just tired of this game. It’s not that it's hard; it's that we're all just not playing well together. You know what’s funny? I think we all think we’re the best at this game.

I just got a text from the kids’ school saying they’re doing a CBeebies pantomime this year. It’s a bit of a surprise, but I think it’s a great idea. It’ll be fun for them to get into the spirit of the season. Is it for the summer? I thought World Book Day was earlier this month. Yeah, I remember that. But I think the pantomime is part of the school’s summer festivities. They’re planning a big celebration for the kids’ birthdays, too. They’re going to do it all in the school hall. That sounds lovely. I was just thinking about how we could celebrate the birthdays around the same time. It’s a good opportunity to bring everyone together. Maybe we can do something similar at home? That would be great! I love doing stories with you, especially the ones from CBeebies. I remember when we read "The Tale of Peter Rabbit" together. It’s such a classic. Yeah, and the stories are always so full of adventure. I love the way they bring the characters to life. Sometimes I wish I could read them as well, but I’m still learning. You’ll get there, love. I taught a few kids who were at the same level as you. It’s all about making the words come alive. And don’t forget, we did World Book Day last month. It was such a hit with the kids, and the decorations were amazing. Yes! We read "The Very Hungry Caterpillar" and made all those little snacks. It was so much fun. I wish we could do something like that again for the birthdays. Maybe we can have a storytime before the birthday party. I can even try reading one! I know I’m not perfect, but it’ll be fun for the kids. That’s the spirit! And if you’re not sure, I can read with you. It’s always great to share the stories. Also, I think we should plan the birthday cake. Maybe a CBeebies-themed one with some of their characters on it. That would be perfect. I can make a cake with a little Peter Rabbit on the top. It’ll be a hit for sure. And I can help you with the frosting. I’m getting better at it every day! That’s the best news I’ve heard all week.

So, do you think we should actually move out of this flat? I mean, it's been a year now, and honestly, I’m starting to feel like we’re just stuck in a time loop. Same meals, same arguments, same view of the same street. I can’t lie, it’s beginning to feel a bit stale. But I like the location. Hitchin's not too far from London, and the pubs are decent. Plus, we’ve got each other. If we move, it’s going to be a whole new set of problems. Honestly, I’d love to move, but I’m worried about the cost. I’ve been looking at the rental prices in Hertfordshire and they’re through the roof. I’m still paying off my student loans, and I’m not sure I can afford to take the plunge. I get that, but we’re both in stable jobs, right? You’re a journalist, and I’m in engineering. We’re not exactly broke. Maybe we can look into shared accommodation or even consider relocating to somewhere more central? That’s a good point. I’ve been thinking about moving closer to the city for work. It’d be easier to get to the office, and maybe meet some new people. Plus, it might help us find someone new to be part of our circle. I like that idea. It might be good for all of us. But I’m still a bit nervous about the whole process. I mean, what if we get into a bad place? Or worse, what if we can’t afford it? That’s fair. But we’ve been through a lot together. We’ve survived past arguments about the Wi-Fi and the lack of a proper oven. If we can get through that, we can get through anything. Exactly. And if we do move, maybe we can try out some new recipes. I’ve been craving Italian food, and I think it’d be a good way to start fresh. Italian, you say? I’ve been reading about this new restaurant in St Albans. It’s supposed to be great. I think it’s worth checking out if we ever decide to move. Sounds like a plan. I’ll go with you on that. And maybe after that, we can finally get that oven we’ve been dreaming about.

I just got a new book from the library, and I couldn't help but think about how much I miss reading with the girls. It's been ages since we had our book club at my place. How are you all doing? Oh, I've been meaning to get back to it. Life’s been a bit too busy with the admin stuff lately, but I still love reading. It’s like a little escape. Speaking of which, have you ever thought about starting a book club again? Honestly, I haven’t had the time. But I’d love to join if you all do. I’ve been meaning to read more, honestly. I’ve been so bogged down with work lately. It’s like I’m always on the go. I know what you mean. I’ve been working late a lot, and I think it’s affected my reading habit. But I’ve been trying to make time, even if it’s just a few pages a night. It’s been helping me unwind. That’s great. I think it’s important to find that balance between work and personal time. Speaking of balance, I remember when I was a kid, we used to play with all sorts of toys. My brother had this old wooden train set. It was so dusty, but it was amazing – we used to build whole railway lines in our garage. Oh, I had a similar experience. My dad used to build these awesome model airplanes for me. He’d even paint them and make them look real. I still have a few of them in a box up in the attic. That’s so sweet. I still have some of my childhood toys too. There’s this little plastic dinosaur I used to collect. I kept it for years, even after I outgrew it. It’s kind of a reminder of how far I’ve come, but also how much I’ve changed. I think that’s the beauty of childhood toys – they have this way of staying with you. They remind us of who we were, even if we’re not the same person anymore. Absolutely. And I always found it fascinating how people speak differently depending on where they’re from. My mum used to talk with a very strong East Anglia accent, even in the city. It was so different from the way people around us spoke.

So, Dad, you've just come back from that trip to Spain, right? I heard it was amazing. Did you have a good time? Oh, it was brilliant, really. We stayed in this seaside town called Torremolinos, and it was just perfect. The weather was great, and the food was amazing. I remember you saying something about the beach being like a postcard. Was it really that beautiful? Oh, absolutely. The beach was packed with people, and the sun was just perfect. But what really surprised me was the local market. You could get everything from fresh seafood to handmade crafts. That sounds incredible. Did you try any local dishes? My brother mentioned something about paella. Oh, we definitely had paella. It was so different from what we're used to. The rice was really fluffy, and the saffron gave it that beautiful golden color. I love cooking, so I’d have tried that for sure. But I bet the seafood was even better. Did you go out on a boat or something? Yeah, we took a boat tour to see some of the coastal villages. It was quite a sight. I think I still have them in my phone. That's great. I'd love to go on a trip like that. Maybe next year we can plan something. You know, just the four of us? Yeah, that would be nice. But I think you lot are already more adventurous than me. I just like to relax and enjoy the simple things. You're not that old, Dad. Maybe you can still go on more trips. You were telling us about that trip to France a few years ago, wasn't it? Oh, that was a good one. We got lost in Paris, but it turned out to be a funny story. I think I still have the photo of us trying to read the map. Yeah, I remember that. It was a classic travel mishap. But it made for some great memories. Exactly. You can't plan for everything, but you can always have a good time. I agree. So, are you going to go on another trip soon? Maybe with us?

Morning, everyone! How's the weekend shaping up? I’ve already made coffee, and there’s toast in the toaster if anyone’s hungry. Morning, Dave! Thanks for the coffee. You know, to get the real-world perspective. Oh, I could help with that. I’ve been working on a piece about sustainable energy in the UK. You’d be the perfect source.
