I think I’m ready to get back into the swing of it. Perfect. I’ll start drafting a proposal this week. We can meet up and figure out the details. Maybe you can bring your engineering skills to the table, and we can combine the storytelling with the science. I’ll make sure to get the tech side of things right. I’ve got a friend who’s a data analyst, and we could pull some interesting stats for the article. That’s brilliant. I’m really excited about this. It’s been a while since I had a project that felt so meaningful. And it’s not just about the project, Steve.

So, Reg, we've got to make sure we get to the airport on time. I still can't get my head around how the satnav keeps leading me down the wrong roads. I've been using Google Maps for weeks, and it's like it's got a mind of its own. Yeah, I know what you mean. I tried using it last week to get to the train station, and it led me through a construction zone that closed halfway. I ended up walking for twenty minutes. It's not like it used to be. Back when I was a student, it was always spot on. You're telling me! I once used it to get to the local pub and ended up in a village that didn’t even have a pub. The only thing I saw was a guy with a dog who looked like he was waiting for the bus. I had to ask for directions twice. That doesn’t sound too bad. I used to rely on paper maps when I was younger. I remember once getting lost in the countryside near Liverpool and ending up in a field with nothing but cows and a few sheep. I had to wait for a farmer to come out and ask him where I was. I think the problem is that we're all used to getting instant directions. You just tap a few buttons, and boom—you're there. But it's not always that simple. I mean, don’t get me wrong, I use Google Maps all the time, but sometimes it's better to just ask someone. I’ve been trying to use it less lately. I think it’s good to get out of the car and actually talk to people. You never know, you might end up meeting someone new, like a friend or a mate who can help you out. Exactly! I remember when I was working on the construction site, I used to take the bus to and from work, and I made some great mates that way. It’s not all technology and apps, you know. Sometimes a simple conversation can be the best way to get somewhere. That’s true. I had a mate who used to drive me around the city when I first moved here. He knew all the shortcuts and the best places to stop for a pint.

I've been meaning to ask you, how are you managing with that constant feeling of being run down? I've had a few episodes of fatigue lately, and I'm not sure if it's just the stress of running this startup or something more serious. Oh, I know what you mean. I've been feeling the same, especially with the school term and all the extra work I've taken on. I think it might be a combination of things—workload and not enough rest. But I've started going to the gym more and trying to eat healthier. It's making a difference, honestly. That’s a good approach. I've been doing a lot of reading about nutrition and mental health lately. It’s amazing what a difference a balanced diet and some mindfulness can make. I’ve been using some apps to track my sleep and hydration, and it’s really helped me feel more in control. That sounds really effective. I've been meaning to try some of those apps but haven't gotten around to it yet. I guess it’s all about consistency, isn’t it? Absolutely. I’ve had some really good days when I stick to my routine, and then there are days when I fall off the wagon. But I try not to be too hard on myself. It’s a journey, right? Exactly, and it's important to have support. I’m glad we’re all in this together. Speaking of which, I was just in the botanical gardens, and I noticed how much the plants are thriving here. I wonder how they manage the climate and soil so well. It's fascinating. I remember reading that Stockholm’s green spaces are carefully maintained to promote biodiversity and public well-being. I think they use a lot of local plants and sustainable practices. That’s really impressive. I wish more cities would take that approach. I mean, we’re all trying to improve our health, but if we can also make our environment healthier, that’s a win-win. It makes me think about how we could apply some of these ideas to our own small garden at home. That’s a great idea! I’ve been thinking about starting a small herb garden myself. Not just for aesthetics, but for the health benefits. I’ve heard that even small green spaces can make a big difference in mental health.

I just can’t get over how different my accent is from my parents. I was raised in Gillingham, yet I sound so much more posh than them. It’s like I’ve got a different accent from the same place. Do you think it’s because I’ve been to university? Oh, I know exactly what you mean. My accent was pretty strong when I was younger, but over the years, I’ve softened it up. I used to be a bit of a Cockney, but now I sound more like a regular Londoner. It’s funny how time changes your voice. I think it’s more about who you surround yourself with. I grew up in Harlow, and even though I still have a strong Essex accent, I’ve picked up some of the London slang from my colleagues at the care home. It’s sad in a way, because I feel like I’m losing my roots. Yeah, I’ve noticed that too. I used to live in Chatham and had a pretty clear Kent accent, but now that I’m unemployed and spending all my time in the flat, I’ve started to sound more like the people I hang out with. It’s like my accent is changing, even if I don’t want it to. It’s got me thinking about how much our accents shape our identities. I mean, I still have memories of my mum’s voice, and it’s so different from mine. I remember her talking about the old days, like she never changed her accent at all. That’s true. My wife used to say I had the voice of a man who’d been through a lot. Even now, when I speak, people can tell I’ve been through some rough times. I think it’s the way I carry myself, not just the way I speak. I think it also has to do with how we’re raised. My mum always said we should speak proper English, but I think she was just trying to make sure we didn’t end up like her. She used to get so angry when we said things like “chaos” instead of “chaoz.” I think I’ve got a bit of a problem with my accent, too. I’ve been trying to sound more “educated” because I want to get a job, but it’s not working.

I've been thinking about the Halloween party this weekend. I was going to make a baked Alaska, but I couldn't find the ice cream. Have you seen it? No, I haven't. But I saw some cheese in the fridge, though. You know, I was going to make some grilled cheese for supper. Maybe I can do both? That sounds good. Though I think a baked Alaska is a bit of a challenge without the right ingredients. I remember my grandmother used to make it for special occasions. She always said it was like a dessert for the stars. That’s cool. I guess it's like a dessert for the stars. But I'm still not sure about the ice cream. I mean, I’ve never made a baked Alaska before. What do I do with the ice cream? Oh, you just put it in the oven while the sponge is baking. It's all about timing. I used to help her with it when I was younger. She always made sure the sponge didn’t collapse. It was like a delicate ballet. A delicate ballet? That sounds like a lot of work. I don’t think I’ve ever had a baked Alaska, though. Maybe I should try it. I mean, it’s Halloween, and I want to impress my friends. Impressing your friends is one thing, but the real challenge is making it right. You know, I was thinking about my career. I’ve been recruiting for the programme I run at work. It’s been a tough few months, but I think we’re on the right track. Cool, I guess being a programme director is like being a ballet master, huh? I mean, you have to manage all these people and make sure everything runs smoothly. In a way, yes. But let’s not get too serious. Remember when we were kids and we tried to make baked Alaska for our Halloween party? I think it ended up more like a sponge cake with a melted ice cream core. Oh, that was a disaster! We had to eat it with a spoon. It was like trying to eat a frozen lake. Exactly. But it was memorable. I think that’s what makes Halloween so special. It's about memories, even if they’re a bit messy. Yeah, I guess that’s true. I just hope this year’s party goes better.

Good morning, love. That’s a proper breakfast you’ve made, ANON. Eggs, bacon, and toast—just like home in Shipley. I’ve missed that taste. You know, I still think about the days we used to make breakfast together in Japan. Remember when we used to argue about the best way to cook eggs? You always insisted on a runny yolk, and I preferred them firm. Oh, yes! I still think that’s the way to go. Soft and warm, runny, but not too wet. Though I suppose it’s a matter of taste, isn’t it? Though I do wonder, have you ever thought about flying lessons? Just for fun? Flying lessons? You’re back to that again! I thought you were done with that after your last attempt, which ended with you nearly crashing into a tree. That was a long time ago. I’ve thought about it more since I’ve been back. I mean, it’s not like I’m not capable—just need a bit more practice. I even did a bit of research last week. It’s not that expensive, and it could be a fun way to spend a weekend. You’d come with me, wouldn’t you? Only if you promise not to crash again. And if you don’t mind the fact that I’ll be the one who’s actually in control. I mean, I’ve got more experience than you, don’t you? Don’t be so sure. I’ve got more years of experience in the skies, and I’ve got the patience of a saint. Although, I do think you’d be better off with a different instructor. You know that man at the airfield—always so calm, so kind. He’s got that 'I’ve seen it all' look. Oh, I know him all right. He’s the one who told me I was “too emotional to fly.” I’m not sure if that was a compliment or not. Well, I suppose it’s not the first time you’ve been told that. But you’ve come a long way since then. And if you’re going to go, I’d say you’ve got enough confidence to do it. Maybe you’re right. I might just give it another shot. After all, you’ve got to try new things, don’t you? Especially when you’re in a new place, like this lovely Swansea.

Alright, I’m not even going to pretend I know what I’m doing here. I’ve been trying to get this Scrabble board to work for the last 15 minutes, and I’m still not getting a single word right. What’s the deal with this game? Oh come on, it’s not that bad. I mean, I’ve only been playing for a week, and I’ve already managed to beat you twice. You just need to focus. And maybe stop staring at the tiles like they’re going to bite you. You're both being too harsh. I’ve only been playing for like three days, and I’m already winning. I think I’ve got a knack for this. You just need to relax, Simon. It’s not like you’re trying to win a championship or anything. Oh, I’m definitely not trying to win a championship, but I am trying to remember if ‘quartet’ is a valid word or not. And don’t get me started on the spelling of ‘jealousy’—I still think it should be spelled like ‘jealouse’. Oh, you’re just jealous that your spelling is so bad. I mean, you’ve still got a B in English Literature from A Levels, right? You got a B. I got an A. That’s not even fair. Okay, okay, let’s not get into that. We’re here to play Scrabble, not argue about grades. Though I will say, I did win the Chelsea Flower Show last year with a garden that looked like it belonged in a magazine. That’s a different kind of competition. A Chelsea Flower Show? You’re a chef, not a gardener. I thought you were the one who got sunburned trying to make lasagna in the summer. I didn’t get sunburned, I got inspired. You know, the kind of inspiration that makes you want to start a garden. Though I think it’s a bit too late for that now. You know, I remember reading somewhere that the word ‘scrabble’ actually comes from the Scottish word for ‘to scuffle’ or ‘to scramble’. That’s pretty cool, isn’t it? Yeah, I bet it’s also related to the fact that Scrabble is the only game where you can actually spell your own name in three letters. You know what I mean? It’s like, ‘Barry’—B-A-R-R-Y.

I've been thinking a lot lately, you know. I've had a few years now since I retired, and I feel like I've had time to reflect on things. I mean, I've always been a bit of a thinker, but now I feel like I've got more time to actually do it. That’s true, isn’t it? I’ve been thinking about that too. It’s funny how you’ve got all this time and yet you still feel like you’ve got so much to do. I mean, you can’t just sit around all day, you know. You’ve got to keep your mind active somehow. Yeah, I know. I’ve started reading again, actually. I managed to get hold of a couple of books from the library. I’ve been reading about history, you know, things from when I was a kid. Sometimes I feel like I’m back in the old days, sitting in the garden with a cup of tea and a book. That sounds lovely. I used to do that when I was a childminder. I’d sit by the window with a book and watch the kids play. Sometimes I’d read while they were napping. It was peaceful. It was peaceful, wasn't it? I remember when I was younger, I used to dream of having a garden like that. I never had one, though. My parents didn’t have the money to build one. You know what I mean? Oh, I know what you mean. I think a lot of people from our generation had to work hard to make ends meet. We didn’t have the luxury of time and money to enjoy things like that. Exactly. I think we both have a lot to be grateful for, though. We’ve had our share of struggles, but we’ve also had moments of joy. I think it’s important not to take those for granted. Absolutely. I think that’s what makes people like us special. We’ve been through a lot, but we’ve still managed to find happiness in the little things. I think that’s what keeps us going. Yeah, I couldn’t agree more. I’m just glad we’re still here, still talking, still enjoying each other’s company. That’s the best part of life, isn’t it? It really is.

I've been thinking about the new app that’s supposed to help with meal planning. You know, the one that suggests recipes based on what you have at home. It’s been all over the news, and I’ve been tempted to try it out. Yeah, I saw that too. I think it’s called "Cooking with What You’ve Got." It’s got some good reviews, but I’m a bit wary. I mean, I love cooking, but I’m not sure if I’d trust an app to suggest the right combinations. What do you think, Speck? Honestly, I think it’s a bit gimmicky. I’ve used a few of these apps, and they tend to suggest things that are either too simple or too complicated. But if it’s free, maybe I should give it a shot. I’d love to try some new recipes without having to run to the shop every time. I agree with you, Speck. I’ve been cooking more lately, ever since I started taking my fitness seriously. I think I’ve got a bit of a knack for it now. I’ve even started experimenting with some new ingredients I picked up from the local market last week. That’s great! I’ve been meaning to start doing that too. I’ve been so busy with work and my kids that I haven’t had much time to cook. I’ve been relying on takeout and frozen meals for the most part. I know what you mean. Our kids have been in and out of the house all week, and it’s been a bit of a challenge. But I think it’s worth the effort. Cooking is such a great way to unwind and spend time with the family, isn’t it? Absolutely. And speaking of family, I heard there’s going to be a new train station opening soon in the area. I think it’s going to be a big boost for the local economy. It’s going to make it easier for people to travel and visit the town. Yeah, I read about that too. I hope it actually gets built on time. The delays have been frustrating, but I can see how it would be a huge help for the community. I think it’s going to be a game-changer. It’s going to make it easier for locals to get around and for tourists to visit.

So, do you remember that time we tried to organise a stag weekend last year? I think it ended up being more of a disaster than a celebration. Oh, how could I forget? We tried to book a cabin in the woods, but the place turned out to be like a haunted house. Got a group of us stuck there overnight with a broken heating system and no signal. Yeah, and that one guy from our course, Dave, started telling ghost stories, and honestly, I thought we were gonna have to call the police. I swear, the whole place felt like it was watching us. It was like  The Shining , but without the creepy music and the twin Peaks vibe. Anyway, you know what I’ve been thinking about lately? That documentary about Shakespeare on TV – the one that’s been getting all the hype. Oh, yeah, the one where they reenact all the plays? I mean, it’s interesting in a way, but I still prefer reading the original texts. There’s something about the language and rhythm that you can’t really get from a screen. I get that, but the way they’re using modern actors and settings makes it more accessible. Plus, they’ve got some really good commentary from scholars. I’ve been binge-watching it during my seminars. It actually helps me understand the context better. Fair enough. I guess it’s just a different way to engage with the material. Speaking of which, did you see that new Premier League game last night? Man City vs. Liverpool – it was a thriller. I missed it, but I heard it was wild. I’m still in shock that Man City managed to pull through. Honestly, I think they’re the most consistent team this season. Yeah, but it’s not like they’re the only ones doing well. Chelsea and Arsenal are also having a good run. It’s like every team is chasing the title now. Exactly. But I think it’s going to be a really tight race. I’m already thinking about how I’ll be watching every game live once the season gets going. I can’t wait. And hey, you remember that time we tried to watch a film marathon at the university? That one time we had to stay up until 4 a.m. just to finish  The Dark Knight .

Hey, it’s so good to see you again! I’ve missed our chats. How’s life treating you lately? Honestly, it’s been a bit hectic, but I’m surviving. Work has been crazy with the new campaigns, and I’ve been trying to balance it with my personal life. How about you? Still juggling your project with your studies? Yeah, it’s been a rollercoaster. It’s going well, actually. I love the creative side of it. I’m working on a campaign for a new line of organic skincare, which is super interesting. I’d love to get into something like that, but I’m still figuring out what I want to do long-term. I’ve been meaning to visit my parents more, but work has kept me so busy. It’s one of those things I keep putting off. I get that. But it’s important to make time. You know, I’ve been thinking about my future plans more seriously. I’m considering moving to a city where there are more opportunities, maybe somewhere like Manchester or Bristol. That’s a good move. I think cities like that offer more space for personal and professional growth. I’m tempted to go back to London, but I’m not sure yet. Yeah, London has its perks, but it’s also pretty overwhelming. Maybe one day, when I’m more settled, I’ll consider it.

I just made a new pot of tea. You know, I’ve been trying to grow some herbs in the garden, but the mint keeps taking over. I’m not sure if it’s a good thing or not. Oh, I know the feeling. My mum used to have a little patch in her garden, and she swore the mint was the best thing she ever grew. But it just spread everywhere, even through the fence into the neighbor’s yard. Yeah, I think she was right about that. It’s so fragrant, and it’s great for making tea or adding to salads. But I’m not sure if I want to let it take over the whole garden. I’ve got some tomatoes and lettuce that I’m trying to grow, too. I suppose you need to be careful with what you plant. I’ve been thinking about starting a herb garden of my own. I’ve got this plant called rosemary that I bought from the market last week. It’s been doing pretty well so far. That sounds great. I’ve heard rosemary is really good for cooking, especially with chicken or potatoes. Do you have any other herbs you’re growing? I’ve also got thyme and parsley. Thyme is a bit tricky, though. It seems like it doesn’t like being moved around too much. I had to replant it a couple of times because it kept dying. Oh, I’ve had similar problems with my basil. I thought I was doing everything right, but it just started to wilt one day. I was so sad. I think I need to do a bit more research on how to care for these plants properly. Yeah, I’m actually doing a bit of research for my PhD on plant growth and soil composition. It’s all about understanding how different factors affect plant health. Maybe I can help you out with that. That would be amazing. I’d love to know more about what’s going on in the soil and how to give my plants the best start. I’ve always been a bit of a novice when it comes to gardening. No worries, we all start somewhere. I’ve had my fair share of failed attempts too. But I think it’s a great way to connect with nature and get some fresh produce without spending too much.

Good morning, Tony. How was your weekend? I heard you had a promising young footballer over for lunch. Oh, it was fine, thank you, Roger. I had a few of the younger players from the local team over. They’re all very eager and full of energy. I even met one of the parents, a lovely lady with a daughter who’s just started playing. That’s great. I always think footballers have a lot of influence on the kids. It’s surprising how much they do for the community, isn’t it? Definitely. But I won’t lie, some of them are also into snooker. One of the younger ones, a lad called Jamie, is pretty good. He’s got a lot of natural talent, and I think he might be going into the professional ranks. Snooker? Interesting. I’ve always thought snooker players are more of a quiet bunch. But then again, I’ve never been one for the games myself. I preferred the garden. You know, the old-fashioned way. Yes, I know what you mean. My wife and I have a small patch in the back. I’ve started to take more interest in it lately. It’s a bit of a task, but it’s rewarding when the first flowers come up. I remember when I used to garden. Back in Cairo, I had a small plot in the compound. It was a bit of a challenge, but I managed to grow some tomatoes. Though, I suppose most of my time is spent marking students’ work these days. It’s a bit of a grind, but you get used to it. I can imagine. I’ve been doing the same, though I must say I’ve been thinking about retiring early. I’ve been thinking about joining the police or armed forces, just to switch things up a bit. Well, you never know. It’s always good to have a plan B, isn’t it? And who knows, maybe you’ll end up in a completely different line of work one day.

Right, we need to get this sorted. The Christening is in two weeks, and I still haven’t got the venue booked. I can’t wait to see all my relatives and cousins. Yeah, and we’ll have a nice weekend. Maybe we can take a walk in the park too. It’s been a while since we’ve had a proper family day out. Well, I must say, it's been a while since we all sat down like this. It feels like ages since the wedding, doesn’t it? Alright, so I’m trying to get my paperwork sorted for the thesis submission. It's a bit of a mess, honestly. I've got all these forms and deadlines, but I can't figure out where to start. I've been thinking a lot about dreams lately. That’s what we were talking about earlier, right? You know, those vivid ones where you’re flying or you're somehow in a completely different place. Maybe if we win the lottery? Yeah, the lottery! I’ve been thinking about it a lot lately. I mean, the chance is slim, but it’s still fun to dream about.

I can't believe we ended up in A&E again. It's like we're playing some kind of sick game. I know, I’m still reeling from the fact that I ended up with a broken arm. That’s something we need to talk about more. Maybe we should plan something more relaxing next time. No rushing, no stress. Just us, doing something we both enjoy.

I've been thinking a lot lately about starting a small business. So, do you think we should go for the fish and chips or the burger? I’m still not sure. I mean, the fish and chips is a classic, but I’ve had enough of it lately. Och, I’ve been meaning to tell ye about this wee trip I took to the Highlands last summer. It was proper bonnie, mind ye. I got a wee camera, y’know, not the fancy kind, just a compact one, but it captured the light on the lochs like it was magic. That sounds lovely. I’ve always wanted to go up there. I’ve been thinking about starting to do some landscape shots. The weather over there can be quite unpredictable, though. Oh, aye, that’s the thing about Scotland. You never know what the sky’ll do. One minute it’s clear blue, the next it’s all grey and pouring. I remember one day I was taking pictures of a mountain, and the clouds rolled in so fast, it was like the sky was closing in on me. You never know what you’re gonna get. Exactly. And the light, though—there’s a moment when the sun starts to set and the light catches the hills. It’s like the whole world is bathed in gold. I got a couple of photos from that day that I’m still really proud of. That sounds amazing. I should really try to get out there. I’ve got a bit of a backlog of photos I want to take. Maybe I’ll join a group or something. It’s not just about the pictures, it’s about the experience. Aye, that’s the thing. If ye go with the right mindset, it’s not just a trip—it’s a journey.

I just got the nursery confirmation letter, love. It’s all set for the start of next month. I couldn’t be more relieved, honestly. Right, so I was thinking about what I’m going to wear for the conference next week. I got this new jacket from the charity shop, but I’m not sure if it’s too casual for the venue. You’re worrying about a jacket? You’re a professional, not a student. Just wear it, mate. If it’s not too baggy, you’ll be fine. Yeah, but you know how those charity shop jackets can be. And if you’re ever stuck, shoot me a message. I’ve got a few tips on how to style your stuff without looking like you’re camping in a tent. You’ll be the envy of the office, then. The guy who can pull off a charity shop look like it’s from a high-end designer. I’ll take that as a compliment. Now, I think I need to go and get some new clothes. Well, I've just made the tea, lass. It's proper strong, as it should be. You know, the real thing, no muck about it. I’ve had a bit of time to think, and I reckon we should start a proper tea time tradition again. Used to be a thing in the old days, didn't it? Oh, I agree with you, Bob. I just made a really lovely stew. It’s got all the classic ingredients – carrots, onions, a bit of cumin and some homemade beef stock. I’m so glad I got a few jars of the proper stock cubes from the supermarket. You know, the ones that are a bit more like the real thing. Oh, I love a good stew. I’m not the biggest fan of stews and soups, but I can’t deny they’re comforting. I still remember the first time I tried a proper Sunday roast in London. My flatmate had to explain it all to me because I thought it was just a normal roast dinner. It was like a feast! I tried going to a pub last week. I showed up with my passport and a smile, and they just said, “No, we don’t take walk-ins.” It was a bit of a shock. I was in London last week and saw a protest outside Parliament. It was about climate change, and there were a lot of people with posters and signs.

Hey, you’re back! How was your holiday? I’ve been dying to know all the details. Oh my goodness, it was amazing! But once I realized the importance of just being there for them, it made all the difference. That’s such a good point. I think that’s what we need more of—people who are willing to listen and support each other. Exactly. I’m glad we’re both trying to make a difference in our own ways. Speaking of which, have you got any plans for the weekend? I was thinking of going to that new café in town. I was just thinking the same thing! I’ve been craving some good coffee and pastries.

I just got a call from Lucy. She’s been going through a really tough time. She’s got cancer, and it’s not looking good. I feel awful for her. I know, she’s been so upbeat lately, and now this. It’s just so unfair. I was going to visit her this weekend, but I’m not sure if I should. You should. She needs people around her. I know it’s hard, but she’s had a lot of support from her friends. I remember when she was still working at the gallery, always so full of life. Yeah, it’s like a cruel twist of fate. But even though it’s sad, I think she’s making the most of it. I found a few that might be worth looking at. The planning application for the new school is going through, so it might be a good time to move. That’s a good point. I’ve been thinking about it too. We need more space, and the village is growing. Yeah, it’s a good opportunity. I can go and see one this weekend if you’re up for it. I’m in. Let’s go together. Time to take a break from worrying about Lucy and focus on something positive.

I swear, I don't know how people do it. Every day’s the same, and it’s just like...  sigh  I can’t even begin to explain how much I hate this job. It's like I’m trapped in a time loop, and I can’t break free. Oh come on, you’re not the only one. I’ve been working here for six months, and I still haven’t figured out how to make the residents stop complaining about the same thing every single day. It’s like they’ve got a grudge against the building. Yeah, well, I don’t like the fact that I have to deal with the same problems over and over again. People think I’m like a personal assistant, but I’m just here to make sure the place stays clean and the lights work. And I don’t even like the fact that I’m expected to be friendly with everyone. I mean, I’m not a social worker or anything. I just want to make sure people are safe, not that I have to make small talk with them all day. Exactly, and it’s not just that. I don’t like the fact that I have to handle all the complaints by myself. One day it’s about the heating, the next it’s about the noise from the floor above. It’s just exhausting, and I don’t even get a break. I know, and the worst part is that no one ever seems to understand how much work it is. You think you’re just cleaning up after people, but it’s not like that. It’s like you’re managing a whole other job while dealing with these things. Yeah, and there’s also the fact that I don’t like the way some of the residents treat us. It’s like we’re not even human to them. I mean, I’m just trying to do my job, and I get shouted at for the smallest things. I can’t even begin to tell you how many times I’ve been asked to fix something that’s not even broken. I just want to say, “Look, I’m doing my best here,” but no one ever listens. I know, and that’s what I hate the most. It’s not like we’re not trying to help.

I just bumped into a bunch of English people in Antwerp, it was so weird. We were all in the Christmas market and started chatting, and it turned out they were from Herne Bay too. It felt like we were all part of some big English family, even though we were thousands of miles apart. That’s funny, I remember when I was younger, we used to go on package tours to places like that. I always thought it was so strange how we’d be in a foreign country and still feel like we were in England. You could hear the same accent, the same slang. Yeah, I remember that. I used to go on package tours too when I was younger, before I started working in care. It was such a different time. Now I just shop at the local market in Harlow, and I pick up a few souvenirs for the kids. I think it's partly because we all speak the same language, even if we're not from the same part of the country. I was thinking about that the other day when I was trying to learn some German for a trip to Berlin. I kept mixing up words because I was so used to English rhyming patterns. You know, I always thought that language was a big part of what made us English. Even though I’ve been retired for years, I still find myself using old phrases and expressions. It’s like they’re stuck in my head. I suppose it's also the way we all have our own little quirks. Like my brother, he always says “biscuit” instead of “cookie,” even though he’s lived in the US for years. I think it’s part of who we are. And then there's the whole thing with Christmas. I can’t wait for the Christmas markets in Brighton. I’m thinking of taking the kids there this year to do some shopping. It’s just so much more fun than going to the big shops in the city. You know, I used to go to the Christmas markets when I was working. It was such a magical time. Even though I’m not working anymore, I still miss the feeling of the season. And don’t even get me started on the puppies. I’ve been trying to get one for years, but I’m still waiting for the right one.

I just saw the news about the equality vote in Ireland, and I think it's brilliant. I mean, it’s about making sure people are treated fairly, right? Yeah, I heard about it too. I think it’s a big deal, especially for people who’ve been struggling for so long. But I can't believe we’re still having this conversation. Shouldn’t it be settled by now? I know, it's so frustrating. I mean, how many times do we have to fight for basic rights? I remember when I was in school, the teacher said something about equality, but it felt like it was just a word. I still remember my mum talking about how she had to fight for her rights at work. She said she was one of the few women in her office, and no one took her seriously. But she never gave up. That’s inspiring. I’m just glad things are changing now. Though I do feel like the government is moving slowly, even though they say they support equality. They say one thing, but do another. I mean, I can’t even get a job these days. I can't believe we've been on the road for six hours already. I thought it would take less time. I got lost twice, and now I'm more confused than I was at the start. So, do you know what’s really interesting about telomeres? I read this article the other day that says they’re like the caps on the ends of our chromosomes and they get shorter as we age. It's like the biological clock, ya know? Yeah, I remember hearing about that. But I'm not too sure how it works exactly. Is it related to how we age or is it more about how our cells divide? It’s like the body’s way of saying, “Hey, you’re getting old.” That’s fascinating. So if we could find a way to keep telomeres from shortening, we could basically live longer? I’ve been thinking about taking a weekend away for a bit. Maybe some hiking or kayaking. I need to get out of the house more with the toddler. That sounds like a great idea. I just got this new coffee maker, and I think it’s amazing. I was making coffee for the whole family this morning, and it was so smooth. I just got a new Christmas tree, love. It’s a real one from the local market, you know. I got it on Saturday and put it up today. It’s so much nicer than the plastic ones, don’t you think? Oh, I think that’s a great idea. It’s not about the size of the gifts, it’s about being together. You know, I remember when I was a kid, we used to have this little German Christmas tree ornament, and every year, my dad would tell the story of how he got it. Alright, I’m officially in my new flat in Sussex. It’s a bit of a shock after living in Bedford for so long. I’m still trying to get used to the layout. Oh, I can imagine. Hey, it’s so good to see you again! I’ve missed our chats. How’s everything going with your placement? Oh, it’s going okay, I guess. It’s a bit overwhelming at first, but I’m learning a lot. So, do you remember the last time we went to a gig in Newcastle? That was the time when the band played "Bohemian Rhapsody" and the crowd just lost it. It was wild, I tell you. Oh, I remember that! Grandma, I’ve brought you some new books and a few bits of chocolate. I know you love reading and chocolate. Oh, thank you, love. That’s very kind of you. That’s great. You’re growing up, son. And I’m proud of you. Politics can be confusing, but it’s important to know what’s going on in the world. And more importantly, to have a voice in it.

So, what do you think about the blood moon tonight? I heard it's supposed to be pretty big. Yeah, I saw it on the news. I think it's going to be visible from here. It’s about your own family coming together. That’s what makes a dinner table special, isn’t it? For sure. It’s the best part of the day. Even when they’re being loud, I love seeing them all together. That’s the real thing. Just being in the same room, laughing, sharing meals, and talking about the day.

I've been thinking a lot about the Scottish referendum lately, old chap. It's got me curious about how things are changing, you know? So, Dad, I was thinking, do you remember that time we tried to cook that weird lasagna from the supermarket? I’m still not sure how it ended up tasting like a combination of pasta and shoe polish. I just saw a sheep crossing the road, and I almost hit it. I was so startled, I slammed on the brakes and nearly sent us all flying. You're not the first one I've heard say that. I just made a new batch of soda bread. It’s a bit of a tradition in our family, passed down from my mum. Even if we’re all a bit older, life is too short not to make time for the people we care about. Exactly. I’ve been trying to be more punctual with my family calls. So, do you ever find it strange how people from different parts of England still have such different accents? I even learned a bit of Yorkshire, which is totally different from my own. I think it’s also about the social class and education level. But I also think language is a living thing—it changes with time, culture, and interaction.

Right, I just watched  The Favourite  again, and it’s still so good. I don’t know how they managed to make that film without a single person actually smiling. My mum used to make us popcorn and popcorn. Yeah, I know. It’s something I miss too. I think it’s because we’re all so busy these days. So, I was reading about the Scottish referendum the other day, and it made me think. Well, I’m not sure either. Maybe that’s the beauty of it. It’s not just about politics; it’s about people. I remember my granddad used to say, “We’re all in this together, but we’re not all the same.” That’s been stuck in my head ever since. I think that’s the key. It’s not just about the government; it’s about the people. I go to school with some kids from Scotland, and they talk about it a lot. They say they’re proud of their culture, but they’re worried about what happens next. I hope it all works out. No matter what happens, Scotland will always be a part of our history, and Yorkshire’s part of the UK.

I swear, I can't understand a word they're saying on Jeremy Kyle. It's like they're speaking in code or something. Yeah, I know, right? I mean, I’ve been to Chester, and I can tell the difference between someone from here and someone from Derby or York or Wakefield. Exactly! It’s like the accents are all different dialects, but we still all speak the same language.

I just can’t believe how bad Manchester United are this season. I mean, they’ve got money, they’ve got players, and yet they’re still struggling. It’s like they’ve lost their identity or something. I just watched  The Bee Movie  again with the kids, and I still can’t get over how much it’s got to do with royalty. Or like a good parent, I suppose. Keeping everyone in line, making sure everyone gets what they need.

I just love this café, it's got the best coffee in town. I had a cup of real Yorkshire tea when I was younger, but now I’m more of a coffee person. So, do you ever think about what’s going to happen when we’re old? Like, what if we’re still living together in some weird flat in the middle of nowhere? I mean, I can’t imagine ever being that old. I can't believe it's already 7pm. I’ve been chopping onions for what feels like hours. I’m starting to think I’m going to cry. Oh, come on, you’re not that bad. You’re just overthinking it. I swear, you’re more dramatic than my ex. You say that like it’s a good thing. Look, I’m a project co-ordinator, not a chef. Why do I even try to cook? It’s easier to just grab a pizza. Oh, don’t be so lazy. You know I’m not going to eat it if you don’t. Plus, we’ve been planning this meal for weeks. You said it was going to be your special recipe. Yes, well, I thought I’d try this new vegetable stir-fry thing. It’s supposed to be healthy and quick. But I’ve managed to turn the onions into something like a science experiment. I just received the speaker consent forms from the university office, and I think we need to get everyone’s signatures on them by the end of the week. Otherwise, the seminar might not be approved. I’ve emailed them twice, but I haven’t heard back. Maybe we should all reach out again this afternoon. It’s important we get everything sorted before the meeting with the department head. That’s a good idea. I can do that. But let’s not forget, the seminar is on international business communication, and we need to ensure the content is clear and relevant. We’ve got a good structure already—introduction, cultural differences, language barriers, and case studies. Yes, and I think we should include some real-world examples from different countries, like China and Germany. That’ll make it more engaging for the students. Exactly. I’ve been thinking about adding a slide on non-verbal communication as well. It’s such an important part of international business, and it’s often overlooked. Maybe we can compare gestures and body language across cultures. That sounds like a solid addition. Let me check the slides again to see where that would fit best. Also, we need to make sure the case studies are up-to-date. I’ve been looking at a few articles on recent mergers and collaborations between UK and Asian companies. I can add a case study on the recent joint venture between a British tech firm and a Japanese company. It’s a good example of how communication challenges can be overcome. Perfect. I’ll also include a short quiz at the end to test the students’ understanding. It’ll help reinforce the key points and keep them engaged. I like that. We should also make sure the seminar is accessible to all students, so we need to include some language support materials as well. Maybe a glossary of business terms with translations. Yes, and we can also offer a pre-seminar reading list. That way, the students can go in with some background knowledge. Agreed. I’ll draft the reading list and the quiz questions today.

I can't believe we've just finished our last lecture of the semester. I feel like I've been in a classroom all week. I’m so ready for a break. Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve been thinking about the house we’re going to buy. It’s gonna be a big step, but I think we’re both ready for it now. Absolutely. I mean, we’ve been together for years, and this is the time. But I’m just a bit nervous about the whole process. What if we get the wrong place? I know what you mean. It’s a lot to take in. But I think we’ll figure it out. You just need to stick to the budget and not get carried away. And we’ve got a great mortgage adviser on board, so we’re in good hands. I hope so. I just want to make sure we’re both on the same page. It’s not just about the money, it’s about making the right choice for us as a couple.

I just made a new batch of homemade granola. I added some flax seeds and chia for extra nutrients. It’s been a while since I tried something like this. I think it’s a great way to encourage healthy eating at home. That sounds amazing! I love the idea of using flax and chia. I’ve been trying to get more into whole foods myself. But have you ever thought about how much food gets wasted in the UK? I read a report saying that around a third of all food is thrown away. Oh, that’s a huge figure. I think part of the problem is that we’re not used to planning our meals properly. My granmother always used to make sure she used every bit of food. She even made soup from the bones. I think I need to start applying that philosophy at home. Definitely. I remember when we visited her house growing up. The kitchen was always full of jars and containers with leftovers. She used to say, “There’s no such thing as waste, only forgotten opportunities.” It’s something I’ve been trying to pass on to my younger cousin, who’s into cooking now. I wonder how much that still plays a role in the lives of people in the UK today. It’s less common now, but I think those ideas still linger. It’s an interesting way to approach relationships. Speaking of traditions, I’ve been thinking about work experience and careers advice in schools. I’m a teacher, so I often see how students are encouraged to pursue certain paths. Do you think schools are doing enough to prepare kids for the future, especially with things like robotics and urban farming? I think they’re trying, but there’s still a lot of outdated advice. I was an engineer, and I remember how much of a struggle it was trying to find work in the “closed” industries. Now, with the rise of private industries and tech, it’s a different landscape. I go back to my hometown sometimes, and it’s shocking how little has changed in some areas.

I've been thinking a lot about how work has changed things for us. I know it's not just me—everyone's got more on their plate these days. Between research projects, meetings, and trying to keep up with the kids, it's like we're managing a full-time job plus a part-time circus. I couldn't agree more. That's true. I've started setting aside specific times for work and family, and it's helping. I'm not perfect at it, but I'm learning. I think the key is communication—and making sure we're both on the same page. Communication is everything. I’ve been trying to make more time to talk with you and the kids, even if it's just a quick chat during dinner. It’s important to stay connected. I know we’re both stressed, but we can’t let that pull us apart. Exactly. I've noticed how much better things are when we're in sync. It's not just about work—it's about our relationship too. I think we both need to remember to take care of ourselves, even if it's just a few minutes of relaxation each day. I agree. I've started taking short breaks during the day to clear my mind. Sometimes it's just a few deep breaths or a walk around the block. It helps me come back to things with a clearer head. That sounds like a great idea. Maybe we can do something like that together? Like a weekend getaway or just a quiet lunch out. We haven't had much time for ourselves lately, and it's important to recharge. That would be nice. I think we both need to do more of that. I know it's easier said than done, but I think it's worth the effort.

I've been thinking a lot lately, you know. That sea down by the coast, it's real peaceful. I used to go there often when I was younger, before I got stuck in this rut. Now, it's like I can't even afford the bus fare. Oh, I know how you feel. I used to go to the seaside with my mum every summer. It was like a holiday. But now, I just sit at home and watch the telly. I can't even afford to go out anymore. What's the point? I understand, but you've got to keep your head up. I know it's hard, but you've got to find something to look forward to. Maybe volunteering? I know a few places that need help. It's not about money, it's about making a difference. I tried volunteering once. It was for a community centre. But after a while, I just felt so down. I've heard about baby blue tits and how they're struggling. It would be nice to do something for the birds. I remember when we used to have so many of them in our garden. That's a great idea. I know a conservation group that's doing some work with blue tits. They could use volunteers. It's a good way to meet people and get some fresh air. And you can do it at your own pace. I’d like that. It might be a start. I’ve been feeling so lonely lately, and it's getting worse. I don’t know what to do with myself. I know. I’ve been feeling the same way. I barely leave the house anymore. It's like I'm just waiting for something to happen. Maybe that’s why I need to get out and do something. You’re not alone in this. I know how hard it is, but you’re not stuck. You can still make a difference. Just take it one step at a time. Find something you’re passionate about, even if it’s something small. That's what I need to hear. I'm going to look into volunteering. Maybe I can start with the blue tits.

So, do you know what’s the latest in beauty products, Sarah? I was just at the shop the other day, and there were so many new things on display. Alright, skipper, you got a minute? I needed to talk to you about this museum trip we were planning. I was thinking of going to the Walker Art Gallery down in Liverpool. I've heard it's got some real gems. What do you think? Oh, you’re talking about the Walker? That’s a solid choice. I’ve been there a few times. You know, the one with the big glass dome? There’s a route that goes straight to the city centre, and it’s cheaper than trying to fight the traffic. That might be a good idea. I’m not a fan of parking, especially with the fines these days. But I’ve got this interview for a Masters in Social Work next week, so I can’t really make any big decisions yet. That sounds like a big step. I hope it goes well. You’ve been working so hard. I just can’t believe how quickly time’s flying, can you? It feels like yesterday we were both in university, and now I’m teaching kids who are already more independent than I ever was. I remember when I first got my stepdaughter, I thought I’d be the best parent ever, but now I realize how much you have to learn. Yeah, exactly. There’s just so much to navigate. I get that. I had my own dreams too, and I think it’s natural to feel a bit lost. But I also think that the more you give to others, the more you grow in return. I suppose I’ve been a bit lost in the chaos, but maybe it’s time to start thinking about how I can find some balance. I mean, I’m not giving up on my dreams entirely — just maybe not as fast as I used to.

So, do you remember that episode of  Doctor Who  where they went to the future and ended up in a really weird version of Earth? I just found this really nice set of pendant lights on eBay. They’re from the 70s, and they look so retro. I think they’d go perfectly with the living room we’re thinking about buying. Oh, really? Oh, I've been thinking about gettin' a hamster for ages. Me nan used to have one, and it was so cute. I mean, sure, they’re not as big as a guinea pig, but they’re quiet and don’t make a mess. I’ve already got the cage, the wheel, and a little ball of hay. I just need a name for my new friend. You’ll have to get a name that’s not too posh. I mean, it’s a hamster. Maybe I should start writing my own book about my fears. I could call it  The Great Uncertainty . You’d be a bestseller. So, do you know what’s up with the school project? I’ve been trying to get my head around it all week, and I’m still stuck. Yeah, I know. It’s that environmental thing, right? Like, maybe we can start a group or do something on our own. I mean, the school project is just a start, right? We could make it bigger if we wanted to. That sounds like a good idea. Right, I’ve had enough of this. I’m telling you, the only reason I agreed to cook tonight was because you promised you’d help. I didn’t say I’d do all the work! So, do you guys remember that film we watched last week? The one with the time travel and the alternate universes? I thought it was brilliant, but honestly, the ending confused me. Oh, I know! Yeah, I agree. I love a good story, but if it's too complicated, I just lose interest. I mean, if you’re going to make a film that’s all about logic and time travel, it should be more about the characters and less about the rules. I think that’s the key. If they’d focused more on the characters and less on the gimmicks, it might have been better. But I still think it was a good film—just not for me. I think it’s a matter of taste. Some people love the complexity, and others don’t. But I still think it’s worth a watch if you like sci-fi.

I can't believe we've only been back for a day and already I'm missing Paris. It's so hard to get used to the smell of the UK again, isn’t it? Oh, I know, love. You're not the only one. Alright, let’s get this rice sorted. You know, I’ve seen a few ways to cook it, but I think the best way is to use the coconut milk and some of that curry paste we’ve got. I just had the most bizarre experience yesterday. I was at the supermarket, and they had this new ‘Scan As You Go’ thing. I thought it was a prank at first, but then I found out it's real. Alright, so I just got here, and I’m still trying to figure out why this restaurant is called  The Lea . I thought it was a typo for  The Leia  or something. Nah, it’s not a typo, it’s a real name. The Lea is a real river that runs through East London. It’s one of those little waterways that people don’t talk about much. Yeah, but it’s got a weird vibe. I’ve seen some interesting stuff on those canals. You ever seen a canal boat with a  kosher  sign on it? No, but I’ve heard of people trying to make their own  kosher  food on boats. I mean, you can’t really make a proper  kosher  meal on a moving boat, can you? Wait, is it about the laws? Like, the  kosher  laws? Exactly! It’s all about the dietary rules. You can’t mix milk and meat, and you have to check that everything’s been prepared by someone who’s  kosher -certified. I guess it’s a bit like how some people go to  Italian  restaurants and order something  Italian  but then it turns out to be  Italian -style, not actually  authentic  Italian. It’s all about the  condiments , too. You can’t just throw on some ketchup and call it  Italian . It’s got to be  garlic ,  olive oil ,  basil —the real stuff. I mean, I  love  garlic, but sometimes I just want to grab a  microwave  meal and not think about it. I get that. But I think microwaves have their own  culture  too. My grandma used to say that if you put a  club  sandwich in the microwave, it’s not a  club  sandwich anymore. I’ve heard that. My café has a  club  sandwich on the menu, but it’s not microwave-friendly. It’s got to be made fresh every day. So, are we talking about the  club  as in the social club, or the  club  as in the sandwich? Both. The  club  is a big part of London’s social scene. You can go to a  club , drink some  Italian  wine, and then eat a  club  sandwich. It’s like a  full circle . You know what’s funny? I used to think the  Lea  was a typo, but now I think it’s a whole  river  of stories. Yeah, it’s a  canal  of stories, really.

I've been thinking a lot about the benefits system lately, especially with everything that's been happening in Parliament. It's got to be tough on people like us, isn't it? Aye, it's a right mess. I’ve seen friends of mine get turned down for help when they really need it. I mean, how does someone with no job and no savings manage? The rules keep changing, and it’s like they’re trying to make it harder for people to qualify. I’ve heard that the council is now asking for more proof of everything, even things like food stamps. Yes, I've heard that too. It’s not just the government; even the local authorities are getting involved. I remember when I was working, I used to think that the state would always be there for you. But now, it feels like they're more interested in cutting costs than helping people. I feel the same way. I used to be proud of my work as a civil engineer, but now I can’t even get a job on a building site. The younger generation, they got more opportunities. We just… we’re stuck. I’ve also been watching a lot of TV lately, and it’s all about politics and the economy. I think the media is making it look like we're all scrounging, when most of us are just trying to survive. That’s the thing, isn’t it? There’s a stigma attached to being on benefits. It’s not just about the money; it’s about how people see you. I tell you, I'd rather work than feel ashamed. But the work is gone, and the money is not coming. I know. We’re not the villains here. We’re just people who've been through a lot. I think the politicians should listen more and less talk. They don’t live our lives, so they don’t know what it's really like. And maybe if more people like us spoke out, they might actually start to change things.

I can't believe it's already 7 o'clock. I feel like I've just sat down. The roast chicken was delicious, though—properly cooked and everything. I think you did a great job with the side dishes too.
