So, do you know what’s going on with the car? I’ve been trying to get it started for like twenty minutes, and it just won’t budge. I know, I’ve tried turning the key a dozen times. It’s like it’s decided to take a holiday or something. You think it’s the battery? Maybe. But I thought the battery was fine last week. I mean, we drove to York and back without a problem. Yeah, but that was a few weeks ago. Maybe it’s just aging. Or maybe it’s the fuel system? I’ve heard of cars acting up when the fuel is old. I don’t know, I’m not sure I want to get into that. I just want to get back home, you know? It’s getting late, and I don’t want to be stuck out here in the dark. I know, I’m not looking forward to this either. But maybe we should try jumping it? I’ve got the jumper cables in the boot. I just need to find them. Yeah, let’s do that. I don’t think I’ve ever jumped a car before, though. Will it be too hard? Not really. It’s just a matter of connecting the cables properly. You just have to be careful with the polarity, though. If you mix it up, you could damage the car. Right, I remember my uncle telling me about that. He once tried to jump his car and ended up frying the alternator. Yeah, that’s a common mistake. So, here’s the plan: I’ll get the cables out, connect them to the battery, and then try to start the car. If it doesn’t work, we’ll have to call someone. Sounds straightforward enough. Let’s do it then. I’m just glad we’re not alone out here. I’d be really worried if we were. Me too. I mean, it’s not too bad, but I’d rather not be stranded in the middle of nowhere. Especially with the weather getting colder. Yeah, I agree. Let’s get this sorted before it gets too dark. I don’t want to go through this again. Agreed. Let’s get the cables out and give it a go. Who knows, maybe it’ll start right up. We’ll be home before you know it.

Right, so I’ve been feeling really off for the last few days. Headache, and my throat hurts like hell. I think I might have a bit of a cold or something. I’m not even sure if I should go to work tomorrow. You’ve been looking tired, yeah. But if it’s just a cold, you’ll be fine. I had one last week and it knocked me sideways. Still, don’t push yourself too hard. If you need to stay home, do it. Yeah, listen to him. I’ve been through that before. One day you’re fine, the next you’re like a zombie. Just rest, drink plenty of fluids, and take some paracetamol if you need to. But don’t ignore it, you know? It could be something worse. I know, but I’ve got a big event coming up next week. If I’m off sick, it’ll mess up the whole schedule. I can’t afford to let that happen. You don’t have to do it alone, you know. Maybe someone else can step in. You’ve got friends, right? We’re not all that far away. And don’t forget, you’re not the only one with responsibilities. I’ve been juggling my own work and family stuff. If you’re in trouble, just say the word. We’re not all that different, really. Fair enough. I appreciate that. But I’ll still try to make it in. Maybe I can work from home. I’ve got the laptop, the Wi-Fi, and I can manage the stuff on my phone. Sounds like a plan. Just don’t overdo it. Your health comes first. I’ve seen what happens when people push too hard. Thanks, you two. I really appreciate the support. I know I can rely on you. That’s what friends are for. Now, if you’re feeling better, maybe we can go out for a drink later? It’s been a while since we had a real catch-up. Yeah, that’d be good. Just make sure you’re up for it. No pressure, just a chance to relax and catch up. Sounds like a solid plan. I’ll let you know how I’m feeling tomorrow. Thanks again for the advice and the support. I really value this group. To health, and to not getting stuck in work too much.

I can't believe it's been a month since I broke up with Tom. It feels like it's been forever, but I still can't stop thinking about him. I know, I feel the same. It's so hard to let go, especially when you were really happy together. Do you think it was worth it? I mean, he was nice, but he always kept things so complicated. Honestly, I think he was more of a burden than a blessing. We started off great, but as time went on, it just got more stressful. He always had these weird ideas about how we should live, and it felt like I was constantly trying to prove myself to him. Yeah, that's a common issue. I've seen it with so many people. Sometimes, the ones who are the most toxic are the ones who seem the most supportive at first. It's like they're trying to get you to depend on them, and then they just take advantage. Exactly. I thought I was in love, but maybe I was just in love with the idea of being with him. I mean, I still miss the good times, but I can't go back. I need to move on, even if it hurts. I get that. You're so strong, you know. I admire how you're pushing yourself to stay positive. It’s not easy, but you're doing it. I wish I could say the same about my situation. Thanks, that means a lot. I’m trying not to let the pain control me. I’ve got work and friends to focus on. Plus, I want to be there for the people I care about, not just for myself. That's what matters. You're not just moving on from a relationship, you're moving on from a part of your life. It's a new chapter, and I think you're going to shine in it. I hope so. I'm starting to feel like I have more control over my life again. It’s scary, but I think I'm ready for something new. Maybe even a new job? I've been thinking about applying for a position in a different department. That sounds amazing. You've always had a way of making the best out of any situation. I’m proud of you, and I really hope you find someone who's worth your time and energy.

Alright, let’s talk about the old tales, shall we? I’ve been thinking about the time when we first heard those stories as kids. You remember the one about the Wicked Witch of the West? Oh yes! I remember that one so well. Grandpa used to tell it to us every winter evening. He said the witch was so evil, she tried to steal the kingdom’s gold. But wasn’t she just misunderstood? I think she was protecting her land, not being evil at all. That’s a good point, little one. The stories often have more than one side to them. Like, in some versions, the witch wasn’t evil at all, but just someone who had been wronged by others. I like that idea! It makes the stories more interesting. But then again, in some versions, the witch was actually a great sorceress who had a bad reputation. So, are all the stories about good and evil really just people with complicated lives? Exactly. Good and evil aren’t always black and white, you know. There are shades of grey. I think that’s why we’ve always loved these tales—they make us think. But what about the monsters in the stories? Are they all evil too? Sometimes, they’re just misunderstood or scared of something. Like the goblins in the forest. They might just be lonely or looking for a friend. Like the troll in the bridge who wanted to eat you? Was he really evil? Some versions say he was just a lonely creature who thought being scary would protect him. But others say he was evil and wanted to hurt people. That’s so interesting! So, the same story can be told in different ways, depending on who’s telling it? You’re catching on, aren’t you? That’s what makes these tales so special. They’re not just stories—they’re reflections of our own lives and the world around us. I like that. It makes me feel like I can understand the world better. That’s the magic of stories, love. They help us explore the world around us and learn about the good and the bad in people—and in life itself. I think I’ll start my own story tonight. Maybe about a kind witch who helps people instead of hurting them. I’ll be the hero who finds her and helps her out!

I just got a text from the school about the filming trip. They said they’re doing it tomorrow, so we need to make sure the kids have their gear ready. Yeah, I remember the last time they did something like that. One of the children spilled a drink on the camera, and it took them an hour to clean it up. Honestly, I’m not sure why they even bother with these trips. It’s more hassle than it’s worth. But I guess it’s good for the kids to get out and experience things. I think it’s good for them. It makes them feel like they’re part of something bigger. Plus, I saw one of the teachers talking about it last week. She said they’re doing a documentary on local history. Yeah, and I heard they’re filming the old mill in the village too. I can’t wait to see that. Well, I hope it goes smoothly. I’ve got to take the kids to the gym this evening to get them ready for the trip. I was going to do some running on the machines, but maybe I can do that tomorrow. You should go. It’s good for you. I’ve been meaning to go myself. I’ve been so busy with work and the kids. I even had doughnuts for breakfast this morning. I did too. I couldn’t resist. I blame the kids for that. They’ve been asking for them all week. You know, I had one last night. It was really good—glazed with a sprinkle of sugar. I think it was from the bakery in Norwich. I had one too. I picked the best one from the bin. Not that I was looking for anything special, but I thought it was fair. You two are ridiculous. But I can’t say I’m not tempted. Well, the gym is a chance to burn it off. I’ve been meaning to get back on the treadmill. I think I’ll go with you. It’ll keep me off my feet and away from the doughnuts. Though I might still take one. Then go for it. But don’t do it too often or you’ll be stuck with us for the rest of the year. And your legs will be in trouble. Oh, I’m already in trouble with the kids.

I've been meaning to ask you, how are you holding up with that back pain? It's been a while since we last caught up, and I've heard more than one person mention it. Oh, it's still a bit of a pain, but I'm managing. I've started doing some gentle stretching every morning, and it's helping a little. Still, it's not easy being a small business owner and constantly on your feet. I can imagine. I used to be on my feet all day teaching, and it's a bit of a relief now that I'm retired. Though I can't say I'm not missing the routine. Still, it's the best way to avoid that back pain. You're lucky, really. I've got this new project I'm working on—starting a local boot sale. It’s the kind of thing that used to be a common sight in our town, but now it's pretty rare. I thought it might be a good way to bring people together and support local businesses. That sounds like a great idea. I remember when we used to have boot sales in Brighton every Sunday. There was something about the community spirit back then. People would come out in droves, and it was always a lively affair. I used to enjoy that. Yeah, I know. I think the Green Party is pushing for more local initiatives like that to encourage sustainability and community engagement. It's one of the reasons I've been leaning more towards their policies recently. I can see the appeal. I've been following their stance on climate change, and it's quite progressive. It's good to see someone taking the lead in that area, especially in a place like Brighton where environmental awareness is quite high. Exactly. And it's not just about politics—it's about making a difference in our daily lives. Maybe I'll start with a small boot sale and see how it goes. Who knows, it might just take off. If you need any help with it, I'm always up for a bit of community work. After all, we're both old enough to remember the good old days. That would be great. I'll let you know more once I get the dates sorted. It's going to be a bit of a challenge, but I'm optimistic.

So, do you remember that time we tried growing those plants in the garden? I think it was the string of spider plants we bought from the market. I swear, after a month, they were taller than me. Oh, I remember! I was so proud of you. You were like a real gardener, talking about soil pH and all that. But then we had that one plant that just… died. I think it was because we overwatered it. You said you were giving it a proper drink, but it wasn’t happy. Yeah, I was a bit of a green thumb back then. I even tried growing some herbs. I thought I was the next Jamie Oliver. But then I made a pasty with too much salt, and it left the house in a dramatic fashion. Oh, I still remember that. You screamed so loud, I was sure the neighbors would call the police. And then you tried to blame it on the pasty, not the salt. Classic. Well, I had to make it up to them. I bought everyone a pasty, and we had this little celebration. I think it was the only time I made a pasty that didn’t cause a scene. Still, it was a bit of a mess. I left the kitchen in a state. Yeah, and it was the day before your big presentation. You were so nervous, and then you had to deal with the pasty situation. I think you gave a speech that was full of metaphors about plants and growth. I did. I said something like, “Just like these plants, we all need a little water, but too much can drown you.” I think it was a bit of a stretch, but the professor said it was an original thought. Yeah, that was you. You always have these crazy analogies. I mean, even when we were discussing politics, you tried to compare Trump to a plant. He was a parasite, you said. He drained the resources of the country, you know. Exactly! He was like that overwatered plant. He couldn’t survive on his own. But I guess I took it too far when I said he should be composted. That started a debate with the barman. Oh, he laughed at that. Said you were the first person to use compost in a political debate. I think he started a new tradition at the pub.

I can't believe we've got a killer whale on Blue Peter. I mean, it's not like we've seen a real one in the wild since we were kids. I remember my mum used to say that killer whales are like the bears of the sea, but I think she just wanted to scare us. Yeah, I remember that too. Though I think she was more fascinated by them than scared. She used to watch all the documentaries on BBC2 when I was a kid. She even tried to get me to go whale-watching once, but I was too scared of the dark and the waves. You know, like the time we tried to camp on the beach and ended up with a tent full of sand. Oh, that was one of those weekends where we were supposed to be studying for exams, but ended up getting distracted by the sea. I still have the blue Peter badge from that day. It's got a whale on it and I've kept it in my wallet ever since. It’s like a little piece of my childhood. That’s sweet. I still have the one from when we first got our own flat. It was a tiny thing, just a sticker, but it meant the world. I think we both got them on the same day, right? The day we decided to stop moving around and start building a real life. Exactly. I remember that day vividly. We were both so nervous about committing to each other, but after that weekend, everything changed. I think that’s one of the reasons I still keep that badge. It's like a reminder of what we were before we got too serious. I know. And I still remember the way you looked when we first kissed on the beach. You had the badge in your hand, and I thought,  there goes the girl who’s going to be the one to settle down . You were the one who kissed me first. I was just about to run away. I think the killer whale on the badge was the only thing keeping me from bolting. And you didn’t. I’ll always be grateful for that. And for the fact that we ended up in this beautiful house, in Norfolk, with a view of the sea. I sometimes think we wouldn’t have found each other if it weren’t for that weekend.

Well, I've just been talking to Bob about the hostel situation. You know, it's getting real tricky. Places are so full, and the staff are stretched thin. I can't even remember the last time I saw a proper meal in there. Oh, I know. I've been trying to get a spot for my cousin’s nephew. He's got a bad knee and needs somewhere to stay for a while. But all the rooms are taken. It’s like a lottery now, isn’t it? Yeah, and the food’s worse than it was when I was a kid. I remember my mum used to cook proper meals. Now, they just serve soggy toast and lukewarm soup. I don’t know how anyone manages to stay healthy in there. I tell you what, I think they should bring in some proper chefs. Or at least make sure the meals are warm and fresh. I’ve been thinking about this for ages. You know, when I was younger, we used to have a cook in the shop. She could make a meal out of nothing. Oh, I remember that. She was one of the best. She’d make a roast dinner out of a tin of beans and some leftover bread. But that’s not the point now. The point is, the hostel’s got to be a place of safety, not a slum. It’s not just the hostel, though. I’ve been thinking about the old abattoirs. Our parents used to work there, remember? They’d come home with the smell of blood and meat on them. But now, it’s all automated. No one’s even seen a real butcher for years. I know, I know. My dad used to talk about the old days. He said it was all about the rhythm of the work. The clanging of the machines, the smell of the meat, the way the workers all knew each other. Now it’s all cold and impersonal. You know, I had a friend in hospital last week. She’s been there for months. They’ve got a great ward, but it’s just so lonely. I’ve been dropping in with some tea and a book. She’s got a nice collection of old photo albums. She says they remind her of life before everything went wrong. I remember that. She used to teach English in a secondary school.

I've been meaning to ask you about your time in recruitment. I heard you worked in that field before becoming an associate lecturer. Was it a big change? Oh, it was a massive shift! I loved the fast-paced environment and meeting people, but after a few years, I found myself wanting more creative work. Teaching felt like the perfect fit for my skills and passion. That's a relief to hear. I've always admired how you balance your teaching with your research. It must be interesting to evaluate academic literacy in your courses. Have you noticed any trends in students' writing skills? It's a bit of a mixed bag. Some students are incredibly articulate, while others struggle with basic structure and grammar. I’ve noticed that many students are more comfortable with digital communication, which affects their academic writing in some ways. I can relate. When I was teaching, I saw similar patterns. I often found that students who were more active online were less prepared for the formal tone and structure required in essays. Have you ever had to address that in your courses? Absolutely. I’ve had to design workshops that bridge the gap between informal and academic writing. It's not always easy, but I think it's important to help students understand the difference and how to adapt their writing style accordingly. That sounds incredibly valuable. I remember having to do something similar when I was in my early teaching years. It’s a bit of a challenge, but it's so rewarding when students improve. How do you approach that in your classes? I start by giving them feedback on their drafts and have them revise based on the comments. I also encourage peer feedback because it helps them see different perspectives. It's a slow process, but I see the progress over time. That's a great strategy. I think peer review is one of the most effective tools in developing critical thinking and writing skills. I've always found that when students are involved in the process, they take it more seriously. Definitely. I think it’s about creating a supportive environment where students feel comfortable making mistakes and learning from them. It’s all about growth, right? Absolutely. It’s not just about teaching content—it's about teaching how to think and communicate effectively. That’s the real challenge, and I think it’s one that makes the job so rewarding.

So, do you know what’s up with the new study space in the library? I swear it’s got more coffee machines than the café down the road. Honestly, I’ve been avoiding it since it opened. I don’t know why, but it feels like everyone’s secretly judging me for not having a laptop. Or maybe I just don’t want to get caught on camera by the surveillance cameras. Aww, come on, that’s just the vibe. You know how it is—every place that’s supposed to be chill ends up being a vibe chase. But don’t worry, I’ve already been there. It’s mostly just students trying to get work done and people trying to get work done in the same space. Just a bit of chaos. Yeah, I was there the other day, and I swear there were more people with matching socks than with actual work to do. I think it’s called productivity, but I’m not sure. Oh, I know the feeling! I saw this guy wearing socks that looked like they were designed by a toddler. He was writing a thesis—personally, I think he might have been trying to make it look like he was productive. That sounds like my kind of vibe. I once saw someone wearing socks that looked like they were made of socks. I almost asked them if they were trying to be the sockiest person in the room. I once saw someone wearing two different colored socks, and I thought they were being ironic. Then I realized they were just missing a sock and thought it was a statement. I think the secret to being a successful student is to dress like you’re not trying, but also look like you’re trying really hard. That’s the whole point of this place. Exactly! It’s like the library is a place where you can be both lazy and productive at the same time. I’ve been told I’m doing it right. I think it’s called survival. You survive the chaos, and then you go home and do your actual work. Or you don’t. Either way, you’re still here. Yeah, and if you’re not surviving, you’re just thriving. I’ve been told I’m thriving. Or maybe you’re just standing in the wrong area. I think it’s called the ‘university life’ experience.

So, I was just thinking about that film we watched last night,  Black Hawk Down . You know, the one about the US military in Somalia? It was incredible, wasn’t it? I mean, the way they showed the chaos and the strategy — it really made me think about how the military operates. Yeah, it was pretty intense. I don’t know if I could handle that kind of stress in real life, though. I mean, what if you’re in a situation like that and you mess up? I’d probably end up in a lot of trouble. I don’t think the military’s all that scary, though. It’s just a job, right? Like, if you’re qualified and you go through the training, you’re pretty much set. Although, I bet it’s not all sunsets and smooth sailing. You must have heard stories about the horrors of war, though. Yeah, I’ve heard some pretty chilling stories from my cousin who was in the army. He said it’s not all about discipline and teamwork — it’s also about survival. You learn to read the human mind, and sometimes, people aren’t what they seem. That must be really tough. I guess it’s not like working in an office, where you just deal with paperwork and emails. It’s all about high stakes and making split-second decisions. Oh, I know. And you know what? It’s not just about the military — you see it in some of the films we watch. Even in  Mad Max: Fury Road , there’s a kind of military structure, even if it’s not the real one. Yeah, you know what I mean. I mean, it’s kind of fascinating to see how different cultures use the military. I was reading an article the other day about how some countries use the military for protection, while others use it to control the population. That’s interesting. I mean, I guess it all comes down to the country and its history. I’m not sure I want to think too much about it, though. I mean, I’ve got enough on my mind with work and trying to get through my degree. I know, I know. But it’s all part of the conversation, right? You’ve got to have something to talk about when you’re hanging out like this.

So, do you know what’s up with all these people from London coming into town? I swear, it’s like every weekend there’s some new bunch of posh types showing up, acting like they own the place. Yeah, I’ve seen it too. They always seem to think they’re so much better than everyone else. I mean, they’re just tourists, right? But they act like they’ve been here forever. Honestly, I don’t get it. I mean, some of them are nice enough, but the ones who come here just to flex their wealth? It’s exhausting. I had to talk to one guy last week who was basically bragging about his flat in Kensington. It was like he was trying to impress me with how much he could afford. And don’t even get me started on the racism. I was at a café the other day, and this guy from London was talking to a group of us about how "we’re not welcome here." It was so ridiculous. We’re all British, for God’s sake! It’s so frustrating. Like, why do some people feel the need to put others down just to feel superior? I mean, I’m from the North, and I know how it feels to be looked down upon. It’s not cool. I agree, but sometimes it just feels like the whole country’s divided. It’s not just Londoners, though. I’ve seen people from different parts acting like they’re better just because of where they're from. It’s like there's this invisible hierarchy. Yeah, and don’t even get me started on politicians. They’re all talking about unity, but they’re not doing anything about the divisions. I mean, I’m an architect, and I design buildings for people. But I can’t even be sure if I’ll be able to find a decent job in the future. I know, man. I’m a film-maker, and I’m trying to get a foothold in the industry. I’ve got some ideas, but I’m not sure if the world’s ready for them. It’s like everyone’s too busy with their own problems to care about what others are trying to do. I’m an architectural assistant, so I work with my cousins. We’ve got plans to start our own practice, but it’s going to take time.

So, do you think the parents will like our flat? I mean, it's got a bit of character—those old wooden beams, the mismatched kitchen stuff, and that weird window that creaks when you open it. Honestly, I think they’ll love it. It’s got that cozy, lived-in feel, and the view from the window is just perfect. Plus, the kitchen has that rustic charm that only a few people can pull off. Oh, I’ve seen some interesting places in my time, but this? It’s like a museum of modern living. Still, I hope they like the fact that we’ve kept the original wiring and the 1970s tiles in the bathroom. You know, I remember when I first moved into my flat, I thought the floorboards were going to fall apart. But now I can’t imagine living anywhere else. It’s like a second home. Yeah, I know. And don’t get me started on the garden. It’s not much, but it’s got that bit of green space that makes it feel like a real home. Although, I’m still not sure about the chickens. Oh, don’t worry, they’re only for the garden. They’re very tame. You can even feed them with the leftover nuts from the kitchen. My mum used to say that if you don’t feed the chickens, they’ll come and visit you. I’ve always thought that the old saying about the chicken and the egg is a bit of a mystery. But then again, I’m not really into the whole chicken and egg debate. That’s the thing about people, they make all these rules and then don’t follow them. Like the rule about not using plastic bags. I still use them for the groceries because they’re so convenient. Right, but I heard that using plastic bags is bad for the environment. Though I don’t know if that’s true. Maybe it is, maybe it isn’t. I’m just trying to reduce my carbon footprint. I think that’s the thing with young people—they want to do the right thing, but sometimes it’s hard. Like, you try to reduce your use of plastic, but then you end up buying more things just to be eco-friendly. You know, I’ve seen people who don’t care about plastic or the environment at all.

So, do you ever find it weird how the internet can make you feel both connected and completely isolated at the same time? I mean, I can talk to my mum in Sunderland, but I still feel like I’m missing out on real life. Yeah, I get that. It’s like we’re all just scrolling through our phones and not really engaging with each other. I think it’s also making people more anxious. I’ve noticed that even in conversations, people are more concerned about what others think than actually talking about something real. That’s true. I’ve been trying to cut down on social media, but it’s so addictive. I can’t seem to stop checking my notifications. It’s like the algorithm is designed to keep you hooked. I know what you mean. I’ve been working on a project at work that involves a lot of data analysis, and it’s made me realize how much of our lives are now governed by algorithms. They even predict our behavior before we decide to act. That’s kind of creepy, isn’t it? I mean, I get it’s useful, but there’s a line we’re crossing. I’ve been thinking about how politics is also affected by this. You know, how social media can create echo chambers and make people more polarized. Exactly. I’ve noticed that even among my friends, we’re more divided than ever. It’s like we all have our own bubbles. And then there’s the weather, which is always a conversation starter. It’s so weird how it can shift so quickly here in Cambridge. Yeah, I was just in the café and it went from sunny to drizzly in five minutes. I think I’ve been cooking more lately because the weather’s been so unpredictable. Have you tried any new recipes? I’ve been trying to cook more, actually. My flatmates are quite adventurous, so we’ve been experimenting with some new things. I did this weird fusion dish with Indian and Italian flavors last week, and it was a bit of a hit. That sounds interesting. I’ve been meaning to try out some new recipes myself. I’ve heard that the house prices here in Cambridge are really high. How are you managing with that? It’s tough. I’m a graduate civil engineer, so I’m in a decent position, but it’s still a struggle.

Right, I’ve been meaning to ask you all – have any of you noticed how the nurses’ shift patterns have changed lately? I’m so tired I can barely keep my eyes open after a 12-hour shift. Oh, I know exactly how you feel! I’ve been working with the same team for months now, and they’ve been swapping shifts like it’s a game. I swear one day I’m on night duty, and the next, I’m back to day shifts. Yeah, I’ve noticed too. I’ve even had to ask my manager twice about why I’m being shifted so often. Honestly, it’s getting frustrating. I’ve got a young child to look after, and I can’t keep doing this. I feel for you both. I’ve been working with the same care home for a while now, and they’ve been in constant flux too. I think it’s just how things are these days. Everyone’s trying to cover for each other, I guess.
